jobs.title: RFP-SDN-KRT-26-040- Baseline Consultancy for GBV consortium project in Sudan
jobs.description:
**Terms of Reference (TOR) for**

***Baseline Consultancy for GBV consortium project in Sudan***

Who is the Danish Refugee Council?

Founded in 1956, the Danish Refugee Council (DRC) is a leading international NGO and one of the few with a specific expertise in forced displacement. Active in 40 countries with 9,000 employees and supported by 7,500 volunteers, DRC protects, advocates, and builds sustainable futures for refugees and other displacement-affected people and communities. DRC works during displacement at all stages: In the acute crisis, in displacement, when settling and integrating in a new place, or upon return. DRC provides protection and life-saving humanitarian assistance; supports displaced persons in becoming self-reliant and included into hosting societies; and works with civil society and responsible authorities to promote protection of rights and peaceful coexistence.

DRC has been operating in Sudan since 1994, working in collaboration with a number of partners on protection, GBV, shelter, WASH, CCCM, food security/economic recovery, peacebuilding and humanitarian mine action and clearance. More specifically, DRC is leading a consortium with Trocaire, Norwegian Church Aid, and nine Sudanese Women-led-organisations to respond to gender-based violence (GBV) and conflict sexual related violence (SCRV) in Sudan.

## Purpose of the consultancy

The Danish Refugee Council based in Sudan seeks proposals from Consultant(s)/consultancy firm that will work in collaboration with the consortium management unit, the wider consortium agencies, and FCDO and is responsible for leading and carrying out the baseline assessment for this project. This includes developing the methodology and execution of the baseline assessment and providing recommendations to fully establish the set-up of the project. All work should be aligned with project priorities and protection/do no harm principles. The ideal candidate(s) would preferably have experience working on previous baselines/evaluation, ideally have worked on projects related to the prevention and response to sexual and gender-based violence and have experience collecting data safely and ethically on GBV-related topics with women, girls and other at-risk groups.

## Background

Sudan is in the midst of one of the world’s worst protection crises. An estimated 12.4 to 12.7 million people—predominantly women and girls—are at risk of gender-based violence (GBV) in Sudan, a figure that has quadrupled since the conflict erupted in April 2023. According to [UN Women](https://www.unwomen.org/sites/default/files/2024-12/sudan-gender-alert-2_en_2024.pdf) and the [United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA)](https://www.unfpa.org/resources/unfpa-situation-report-sudan-january-february-2026), women and girls account for 98% of documented conflict-related sexual violence survivors, facing systematic abuses including rape, gang rape, abduction, sexual slavery, intimate partner violence, and forced child marriage. Assessments reported by [UN News](https://news.un.org/en/story/2026/04/1167330) further reveal that 76% of women aged 25 to 49 feel unsafe in public spaces and displacement camps. While hundreds of formal cases are verified annually, humanitarian agencies emphasize that severe underreporting—driven by social stigma, fear of retaliation, and the collapse of healthcare and legal systems—means documented incidents represent only a small fraction of the actual crisis. Additionally, access to survivor-centred sexual and gender-based violence (SGBV) services remains extremely limited. Many survivors have never received basic medical and psychological care, and they struggle to access justice and socioeconomic rehabilitation. Prior to the conflict, Sudan had made modest progress on women’s rights, including repealing the restrictive Public Order Act and criminalizing Female Genital Mutilation (FGM) and child marriage. The current conflict has reversed these fragile gains. Sexual violence is being used as a tactic of war, causing severe physical and psychological harm and social exclusion. Socially, the conflict has shattered community structures and support systems, amplifying vulnerabilities. Survivors now remain increasingly stigmatised and isolated, facing multiple forms of discrimination and increased vulnerability, escalating the risk of exploitation and violence. All this makes urgent protection and accountability measures critical. In a context where populations are not effectively supported by law enforcement, there is a lack of access to and functionality of formal justice mechanisms, leading to large-scale protection threats. The lack of a political solution in Sudan, alongside the lack of solutions for the millions of Sudanese affected by displacement affect national and local-level stability, both in regard to ongoing conflict and competition over resources, as well as rising rates of criminality and food insecurity in response to increasing poverty and vulnerability. Cultures of impunity and stigmatisation are perpetuating and reinforcing violence against women and girls -with sexual violence normalised and seen as inevitable.

Launched in 2026, HOPE-S (Healing, Outreach, Protection, Empowerment) is a five-year, £19.95 million programme funded by the [UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO)](https://reliefweb.int/file:///C:/Users/ADMIN/Downloads/Business%20Case%20and%20Summary%20(S4007819)%20400781%20(Published%20-%20July%202026)) to tackle GBV and conflict-related sexual violence (CRSV) across conflict-affected regions of Sudan. Following a call for proposals, the Danish Refugee Council in Sudan has successfully been awarded the annual grant agreement (AGA), leading a consortium with Trocaire, Norwegian Church Aid, and nine Sudanese Women-led-organisations. The programme has three outcomes:

- **Risk Mitigation:** strengthen WLO/community structures for community-led prevention
- **Response:** improve access to essential GBV/SGBV response services for survivors
- **Social norms:** Harmful social norms/behaviours that perpetuate GBV/CRSV are transformed, and protective community norms are strengthened

The programme design explicitly references **localization** - support the leadership of Sudanese WLOs, working in high-risk locations- and, in turn, has inclusive, participatory delivery informed by a Gender Equality, Disability and Social Inclusion (GEDSI) analysis & safeguarding.

## Objective of the consultancy

The baseline study aimed to be participatory and will serve to define indicators to capture both quantitative and qualitative data throughout the 5-year project to update the Project’s M&E framework with initial data, to build further on the evidence and indicators used in other projects supporting survivor-led networks, allowing an analysis of the impact and effects cumulatively and to lead an intersectional needs analysis.

**The assignment has the following key objectives:**

- Provide quality baseline data (quantitative and qualitative) to respond to the already designed indicators in the Project's logical framework/M&E framework, including ethical considerations for data collection
- Define methods and tools to evaluate some of the indicators in the Project's logical framework/M&E framework drawing on relevant interagency GBV guidance, minimum standards, and survivor-centred ethical principles.
- Provide inputs into the M&E framework – including baseline targets;
- Provide an analysis of key forms of marginalisation, exclusion and barriers faced by groups at risk of GBV/CRSV, and inform DRC and consortium partners' programming, engagement and strategic priorities.
- Provide recommendations to Project stakeholders in order to strengthen the Project’s impact and effectiveness.
- Identify the locally relevant harmful norm through a participatory social norms exploration

*Preparation*

- Review project proposal documents, resources, and standards, including a desk review of the context
- Develop a baseline methodology, for both beneficiaries and humanitarian stakeholders. The scope of the baseline assessment covers locations across 5 states (Central Darfur, North Darfur, South and North Kordofan and Khartoum)
- Develop data collection tools
- Share draft tools, sampling frame and analysis plan with CMU
- Develop an interview and data collection schedule, with support from Consortium MEAL Co as necessary. This should include proposed ethical guidance throughout the process
- Train, support and supervise data collectors on data collection tools and techniques (in Arabic)
- Identify key stakeholders and conduct field interviews
- Analyse data into an initial set of findings disaggregated by age, gender, and inclusion.

*Data collection, analysis and report*

- Train consortium staff/partners on data collection tools and techniques, as required.
- Supervise data collection timeline and quality, consolidating findings on an ongoing basis.
- Analyse data collection into an initial set of findings (disaggregated by age, gender, and disability inclusion), supporting additional data collection as identified.
- Validation meeting (with presentation) and final report

**Other key information:** An independent midline and endline study is planned by FCDO, which will be contracting an independent evaluation company. Additionally, FCDO is also contracting a third-party monitoring entity. The midline and endline study will utilise as much as possible the same methodology as the baseline in order to ensure the comparability of the findings. The objectives of this assignment (full report, data collection tools and presentation of findings) is expected to be completed in English and Arabic.

1. ## Scope of work and Methodology

**Proposed Scope (to be confirmed during onboarding) :** The assessment will focus on understanding safety and security concerns, available support systems, and social dynamics influencing the safety of women and girls in crisis-affected areas. The study will use secondary data, community mapping, a survey, and primary qualitative data to gather information on safety perceptions, responses to violence, and community-driven initiatives for GBV prevention and support. The consultant will be responsible for developing a full assessment protocol based on this TOR, including refining the methodology and finalizing the data collection tools tailored to each target group, conducting data analysis and writing report. The consultant will also ensure that the data collection methods and tools are adapted to the cultural and social context of the selected locations. In addition, the consultant will ensure that all enumerators receive training prior to data collection on the code of conduct, safeguarding, and basic protection principles. The consultant will be responsible for ensuring that strict safe and ethical approaches procedures are adhered to at all stages of the assessment. The geographical scope includes Central Darfur (Zalengi, Nertiti, Um Dukhn Golo locality), North Darfur (Tawila locality), South Kordofan (Dellemi, Thobo, Dilling, Kadugli, Abyssia and Abu Jabayha localities), North Kordofan (El Obeid and Rehad localities Khartoum (East Nile, Ombduram- Umbadda, Omdurman- Khariri, Bahri and Khartoum localities). It will target key populations, including women, adolescent girls, men, community structures, service providers, and both government and non-government actors. All participant data will be anonymized, and confidentiality will be maintained at all stages. The assessment will follow strict ethical standards to minimize harm to both participants and researchers.

**Methodology :** The baseline assessment will utilize a mixed-methods approach, combining secondary data from desk-based document review and primary quantitative and qualitative data collection.

- **Survey (quantitative):** one survey with modules on perceived safety and wellbeing, access to services, and social norms, with the Washington Group Short Set on functioning.
- **Qualitative Methods: Key Informant Interviews (KIIs):** Interviews with relevant stakeholders, including service providers, WLOs and local partners, religious and traditional leaders, community leaders, and local authorities (if appropriate)
- **Focus Group Discussions (FGDs):** Discussions with different community groups (women, girls, men, boys, and marginalized groups) to capture diverse experiences and concerns. Please refer to the geographic scope
- **A review of secondary data** to assess drivers of GBV and types of GBV in the proposed implementation areas, barriers to accessing GBV services, and existing practices of WLOs and local national NGOs regarding safe and ethical data management, referral pathways, and SOP. This will include data from local actors, government sources, and other agencies
- Validation meeting: the consultant will facilitate a validation meeting to share/ verify initial findings and recommendations, with a remit to how they can be integrated into the context in Sudan.
- **Presentation:** of findings to consortium unit and to FCDO. CMU will logistically organise but expect the consultant to present the findings.
- **Final report (**no more than 20 pages). The final report should also include (raw analysis, data tools, analysis and secondary sources used), including a short 2-3 pages max summary as well as recommendations & proposed targets
- **Tentative Indicators to be baselined** (see below). This will be confirmed, and the logframe shared during onboarding, after confirmation with FCDO, DRC and Tier 2 & Tier 3 partners).

**Indicator**

**Method**

**Impact 1:** % of women, girls and other at-risk groups in targeted areas reporting improved perceptions of safety and psychosocial wellbeing.

Individuals

**Impact 2:** Average self-reported impact of WLOs and/or women and adolescent girls in decision-making structures

Women’s Reported Impact Questionnaire

**Impact 3:** % of women and girls, including those at risk of GBV/CRSV, who report being able to access service they need, including health, psychosocial and protection services.

Individuals

**Outcome 1:** % of supported WLOs/women representatives reporting increased ability to influence decisions in identified formal and informal structures.KII

**Outcome 2:** % of supported service delivery points meeting agreed minimum quality standards for survivor-centred GBV

KII

**Outcome 3:** % of women, men, girls and boys in target population who report that they disagree or strongly disagree with locally relevant harmful norms related to GBV/CRSV.

SNET

## Deliverables

The Consultant will submit the following deliverables as mentioned below:

Throughout the phases, the Consultants/consultancy firm will be supported by the Chief of Party and the Consortium MEAL Coordinator (the latter acting as the primary focal point) who will facilitate access to the wider consortium for field data collection activities, and ensure they are conducted in a sensitive, safe and harmonized manner.

**DRC's responsibilities**

DRC is responsible for providing a briefing and will facilitate meetings with consortium stakeholders and share background information/documents (with support from the wider consortium). The wider consortium will support in providing secondary documentation information, list of locations, agreed list of KIIs and WLOs identification and will be responsible for data collection. The consortium members will either hire the data collectors or make their staff available during this time period. Each of the 12 consortium agencies will identify and make available a focal point - who will also engage in briefing, validation meetings, and act as a primary focal point in coordinating the data collectors, sharing information on locations, KIIs, WLOs, etc. Output documents will be reviewed for quality, and final payments will be made upon submission of all agreed deliverables.

**Consultancy firm/consultants’ responsibility**

The consultant will be responsible for all aspects of the deliverables and other responsibilities stipulated in the ToR. It is expected that the Consultant will be able to conduct work remotely. The consultant(s) is/are responsible for providing the following deliverables:

- **Inception Report:** Share detailed methodology, assessment tools, and a work plan outlining activities, timelines, and milestones
- **Data collection tools:** Develop and share questionnaires, interview guides, etc as applicable
- **Training** – train data collectors, keep track of information, and brief/debrief focal points
- **Clean raw data & data analysis –** clean and analyse data collected during the assignment
- **Update M&E framework** (site- and theme-specific) baseline, midline targets on planned results and indicators
- **Validation meeting** – Conduct a validation meeting with key consortium members & FCDO to validate the findings
- **Draft Assessment Report:** A preliminary report summarizing key findings and gaps.
- **Final Assessment Report:** A comprehensive report with findings, analyses, and actionable recommendations.
- **Presentation:** A PowerPoint summary of key findings and recommendations - at least two PPTs (1) with consortium (2) with FCDO (&/or other external stakeholders - to be confirmed)

The Consultant(s)/consultancy firm can work flexibly over the period of a **maximum of 40 days**, starting ideally in mid**-December 2026- mid February 2027.** While the exact dates and number of working hours will be flexible and adapted to operational requirements (including Christmas/end of year break), it is expected to be finalized in the application process. A suggested indicative breakdown of the work schedule is as follows:

- Onboarding and Desk review 5 days
- Baseline methodology, tool development and training 7-10 days
- Data collection, cleaning and analysis 7-14- days
- Report drafting 6 days
- Presentation and validation meeting (consortium and FCDO) 2 days
- Report revision and finalization (post DRC review) 3 days

In advance of each phase of work, the Consultant will be expected to confirm with the DRC Chief of Party/MEAL Coordinator that the number of days outlined above remains appropriate; maximum figures can be reduced or increased as required, at the discretion of DRC. Accordingly, deadlines for all deliverables will be finalized based on consultation with DRC CMU with the final report package delivered by **15th February 2027.** Tentative early findings to be provided by 17th January 2027 (aligned with donor reporting

## Duration, timeline, and payment

The Consultant(s) will be expected to work full-time over the course of a **maximum of 40 days** (period of **mid-December 2026 –mid-February 2027)**. While the exact number of days, dates, and number of working hours will be flexible and adapted to operational requirements and the holiday period, this will be finalized in the application process. Accordingly, deadlines for all deliverables; which will be synchronized with two possible payment tranches

1. 30% upon submission of inception report and validated Data collection tools, along with invoice
2. 70% upon submission of validated final report (with validated PPT, raw data, updated M&E framework) along with invoice

The consultant shall be prepared to complete the assignment no later than ***15th February 2027.***

Proposed Composition of Team

Evaluation team – consisting of Lead Evaluator (with GBV and evaluation skills) – in both Arabic and english

## Eligibility, qualification, and experience required

**Consultant(s) profile and technical competencies**

### Essential:

- At least 5 years’ experience in conducting baseline studies and/or evaluations, using mixed methods evaluation skills and having flexibility in using non-traditional and innovative methods, including participatory and inclusive methods of data collection;
- Experience in the implementation of and monitoring/evaluation of humanitarian, and development Gender-based violence or women empowerment projects in fragile contexts with expertise in gender and human-rights based approaches
- Specific data collection experiences in the areas of ending violence against women and girls, in particular experience engaging with and conducting or guiding interviews with survivors;
- Able to work independently as well as collaboratively in diverse teams with multiple stakeholders across the delivery chain with varying capacities
- Ability to produce timely and high-quality written reports
- Ability to work remotely- training and guiding data collection and analysis process remotely
- The candidate/s must read, speak and write English and Arabic fluently;

### It is expected that the Consultant will be able to conduct the assignment remotely. As the consultant is expected to train, engage and support the data collectors in Sudan - at a minimum the consultant(s) are expected to work in same time-zone as Sudan.

### Desirable:

- Professional experience in Sudan is preferred.

Bidders must meet the Essential Criteria below for this tender. Failure to comply with the criteria will result in the disqualification of the bid. Submitted offers will be reviewed on “Pass” or “Fail” basis to determine compliance with the below formal criteria/ requirement:

**Essential**

**Requirements**

1- The consultant must possess authorization to work in Sudan and/or have the necessary permissions for travel and data collection within Sudan and/or have access to an authorized third party with permission to collect data and operate in Sudan.

Please note that bids shall respond to all criteria, or their bid may be disqualified.

Bidders who pass the technical evaluation will be invited for an online panel interview. The interview will be evaluated per the following criteria:

**Technical criteria #**

**Panel Interview criteria**

1- Previous experience in similar data collection, analysis, and research projects 5%

2- Clarity of proposed process 20%

3- Demonstration of understanding of challenges and best practices across various contexts 20%

Please note that bids shall respond to all criteria, or their bid may be disqualified.

### Desirable:

## Technical supervision

The selected consultant will work under the supervision of the SALAMA project Chief of Party (Muhammet.Kalei@drc.ngo) with day-to-day engagement with the Consortium MEAL Coordinator (Christian.Eboh@drc.ngo)

## Location and support

The assignment can be carried out remotely with working hours preferably in the same time zone as Sudan.The Consultant will provide her/his own computer and mobile phone

## Travel

N/A

## Submission process

**Application process:** Interested applicants/consultancy who meet the required qualifications and experience are invited to submit their expression of interest, which includes the following documents as per the RFP letter invitation, including:

- CV(s) with details of qualifications and experience, indicating documentation of relevant assignments undertaken and full correct details of three professional referees
- The envisioned work plan (maximum 5 pages) that summarizes
- An understanding of the objective of the baseline
- A proposed methodology and envisaged work plan which contains a well-informed approach to the participation of survivors in the study and approaches to ethics, "Do no harm" and gender sensitivity;

Deadline to submit the expression of interest is **Wed 9th December 2026.** The final deliverables of the assignment are expected by 15th February 2027 (exact date to be determined with the consultant(s))/consultancy firm.

## Evaluation of bids

DRC will evaluate the proposals and award the assignment based on technical and financial feasibility. DRC reserves the right to accept or reject any proposal received without giving reasons and is not bound to accept the lowest or the highest bidder. Only those shortlisted will be contacted.
