jobs.title: Annual Audit Sound of Silence, India
jobs.description:
**Organisation**

Hoffnungszeichen | Sign of Hope e.V.

[www.hoffnungszeichen.de](http://www.hoffnungszeichen.de), [www.sign-of-hope.org](http://www.sign-of-hope.org)

**Position**

Auditor

**Type of Contract**

Short-term consultancy

**Type of Audit**

In depth

**Location**

Home-based with field mission travel to North and South 24 Parganas, India

**Languages Required**

English, Bengali

**Application Deadline**

07.12.2026

**Starting Date**

11.01.2027

**Auditing Period**

From 01.02.2026 to 31.12.2026

**Project Title**

Sound of Silence: Sustaining tribal women’s voices and leadership for climate risk reduction among tribal communities in the Sundarbans, India – Exit phase

**Total Project Budget**

390,000 EURO

**Annual Project Budget**

119,878 EURO

Hoffnungszeichen | Sign of Hope e.V. (SoH) is announcing **an open tender procedure for external independent financial audit services in India**.

**Background and Organisational Setting**

SoH is a Christian motivated organisation for Human Rights, Humanitarian Assistance and Development Cooperation. Based in Constance, Germany, SoH is dedicated to helping those in distress and exploited people worldwide.

SoH will be the private German executing agency and the contracting party, with Development Research Communication and Services Centre (DRCSC) and Lokamata Rani Rashmoni Mission (LRRM)being the local implementing agency.

The project purpose of the Project *Sound of Silence* at the exit phase is to consolidate and transfer ownership of climate-resilient community-led systems to tribal women’s and youth groups in the project area. The grant will scale eco- livelihoods through integrated farming, sustainable aquaculture and animal husbandry strengthen climate adaptation via information hubs, and expand mental health, telemedicine and governance networks. It will enable marginalised communities to sustain livelihoods, well-being and climate resilience independently, while fostering equity, cultural identity and long-term sustainability.

**Audit Objectives**

The purpose of the in-depth audit is to provide SoH with a sound basis for its accountability, transparency and accuracy in the financial disclosure towards the funding agency Swiss Philanthropy Foundation (SPF). The tasks of this recruitment relate to:

- An annual audit, with a detailed examination of all the supporting documents for the period of 01.02.2026 – 31.12.2026;

This in-depth audit will verify the compliance with standards of the funding agency SPF, SoH, national regulations and the international accounting standards (ISA).

The auditor will review all of the project’s financial documents, receipts lists, records of transactions, all vouchers and receipts disbursed, and relevant project documents in order to come up with a professional, independent opinion on the financial accounting of the project “Sound of Silence: Sustaining tribal women’s voices and leadership for climate risk reduction among tribal communities in the Sundarbans, India – Exit phase” for all funds received and expended by DRCSC and LRRM from 01 February 2026 to 31 December 2026.

Additionally, the audit shall give recommendations on strengths, weaknesses, and required improvement in the project-related financial and human resources management systems of DRCSC and LRRM.

The audit will support the project quality assurance measures implemented by SoH and contribute to the decision-making process with regard to the project management and monitoring of finances by SoH and DRCSC and LRRM.

**Expected Deliverables**

The auditor is expected to produce **two audit reports**, an audit certificate and a management letter, which will comprise the following:

1. Presentation of the scope and mandate of the audit, as well as the list of documents that formed the evidence for the audit,
2. An opinion whether financial statements (statement of accounts broken down for each year being audited) are issued in accordance with the financial reporting framework of the project, donor requirements and an internationally recognized accounting standard,
3. A checked, signed and stamped list of all (100%) project costs receipts, sorted by budget lines (list is provided by the local implementing partner).
4. Recommendations on identified shortcomings, and, if applicable, comments on the follow-up of audit observations and recommendations from previous years.

Audit documents can be issued in English or German.

**Scope of the Audit**

The audit should focus on the following:

- The correctness and completeness of the accounting records,
- The financial report, showing all project related income and expenditure structured by budget lines,
- Deviations of expenditure by budget lines. The expenditure, which exceeds or falls below the budget appropriations by more than 30 %, shall be explained separately, if the approval of the donor has not previously been obtained,
- That receipts and relevant supporting documents are available for all project related income and expenditures (100% verification),
- The management of the funds made available, which includes the transfer of project funds, all interest earned from the project funds during the reporting period and further income generated by the project,
- Reviewing the appropriate use of funds according to the project objectives,
- Evaluation of the efficiency and cost-effectiveness of the usage of funds,
- Budget adherence through the comparison between budgeted and actual costs in the currency in which the expenditure was incurred. The audit report will not convert the examined amounts into the Euro amounts,
- Reviewing if personnel costs and social security contributions conform to the regulations in the project country and are locally comparable,
- The economical use of the project equipment and assets,
- The inventory and the use of capital items, their whereabouts and their purposive usage,
- Compliance with the legal framework of the project (project agreements and annexes, contracts, etc.) and the donor requirements,
- Compliance with the policies of the local implementing partner regarding procurement, financial administration, human resources management and travel.

**Procedures and Communication**

The auditor will be given access to all necessary documents in the project offices through the local implementing partner DRCSC and LRRM as well as relevant donor documents through SoH.

The auditor will be responsible to set up a schedule in agreement with the local implementing partner DRCSC and LRRM. Any expenses for field trips, postal and translation services and other expenses shall be included in the auditor’s proposed budget. DRCSC and LRRM will support the auditor with logistics and arrangements, however, all payments of the contract will be made directly by SoH.

**Qualifications and Experience**

- Necessary qualification to serve as a recognized independent auditing authority,
- Minimum of five (5) years of experience conducting external independent audits of projects funded by international institutional donors in India,
- Experience in conducting audits for donor-funded projects is desirable.

jobs.title: Humanitarian Ethical Storytelling Guidelines Consultancy
jobs.description:
**Terms of Reference IPPF Humanitarian Ethical Storytelling Guidelines**.

**Background:**

IPPF works with Member Associations (MAs) and Collaborative Partners (CPs) in almost 150 countries across the world to advance sexual and reproductive health and rights. In humanitarian settings, IPPF supports locally led action across preparedness, response and recovery, focusing on the delivery of life-saving sexual and reproductive health services to women, girls and marginalised communities.

Stories, images, audio and video can help communities influence decisions, document needs and solutions, support advocacy and fundraising, and demonstrate the impact of our humanitarian work. However, storytelling in emergencies carries heightened ethical and protection risks. IPPF works on sensitive sexual and reproductive health and rights issues, including services for survivors of sexual and gender-based violence, gynaecological care, contraception, abortion care, HIV services and support for people with diverse sexual orientations, gender identities and expressions. This work often takes place in countries affected by conflict, displacement and insecurity, including settings where sexual and reproductive health and rights are highly contested, restricted or criminalised and where communities, service users and providers may face stigma, opposition, surveillance or violence.

These conditions can affect whether consent is genuinely voluntary and whether sharing someone’s identity, experiences or location could cause harm now or later. Communications can also reinforce power imbalances by presenting people only through crisis, removing important context, privileging certain voices or exposing individuals and communities to additional risk.

IPPF is therefore commissioning a consultant to develop concise, practical Humanitarian Ethical Storytelling Guidelines for use across the Federation. The guidelines will cover the full communications process, from commissioning and collecting content to writing, editing, storing, publishing, reusing and retiring material.

The guidelines will reference existing IPPF communications materials including the Words Matter guide and consent form.

**Purpose and objectives:**

The purpose of the assignment is to create clear and usable offline guidance that helps colleagues across the Secretariat and MAs communicate and gather content about and in humanitarian contexts in ways that uphold dignity, agency, safety and accuracy. The guidelines should be suitable for communications, advocacy, fundraising, media, digital content, donor reporting and programme documentation.

The consultancy will;

- Strengthen trauma-informed, rights-based and locally led approaches to humanitarian storytelling.
- Set ethical standards for content while allowing adaptation to local context.
- Help teams identify, reduce and respond to safeguarding, protection and data risks within content gathering and usage in humanitarian settings and emergencies.
- Provide practical decision-making tools.

**Intended users and scope:**

The primary users will be the Secretariat and MA staff. The guidelines should also inform the work of photographers, filmmakers, journalists, translators, editors, designers, agencies and other suppliers commissioned by IPPF humanitarian.

The guidance should apply across a wide scope of contexts, including conflict, climate emergencies, displacement and protracted crises.

**Scope of work:**

The consultant should;

- Conduct a focused desk review of relevant IPPF policies, existing materials, consent materials, safeguarding and data protection requirements, alongside established humanitarian and ethical storytelling standards and examples.
- Consult a representative group of Federation staff and MAs to understand current practice, risks, operational constraints and examples of good practice.
- Create the structure, principles and practical tools with IPPF and selected MAs, ensuring that the guidance reflects locally led humanitarian action.
- Draft concise guidelines with realistic examples, decision-making tools and templates that can be applied by teams with different levels of communications capacity.
- Community consultation, including toolkit testing, feedback and any resulting revisions, could be incorporated at a later stage.

**Required content:**

The final structure will be agreed during inception. At a minimum, the guidelines should address the following areas.

- Foundations of storytelling in humanitarian contexts - power and representation
- Tips for pre-production for ethical content gathering
- Ethical best practice for content collection
- Informed consent in humanitarian emergencies
- Trauma informed interviewing
- Anonymisation and safeguarding (across production and post-production)
- Visual representation (photography and film)
- Accuracy and positioning in story-writing and quotes
- AI generated and digitally altered content guidance
- Data storage security
- Practical tips for co-creation in humanitarian settings

**Deliverables:**

The consultant will deliver a written toolkit.

1. An inception notes with the methodology, workplan, consultation plan, proposed structure and key ethical questions for agreement with IPPF.
2. Summary of findings from the desk review and consultations, showing how will shape the guidelines.
3. Consultation with MAs and Secretariat for contextual and technical input.
4. A draft and then finalized set of Humanitarian Ethical Storytelling Guidelines which includes practical resources and links out to existing IPPF resources

**Working arrangements:**

The consultant or consultant team will work closely with the IPPF Humanitarian Team and wider IPPF staff. The assignment is expected to be completed remotely.

**Consultant profile:**

The consultant or team should demonstrate;

- At least 10 year's experience in ethical storytelling and content production for INGOs or civil society organisations.
- Extensive practical field experience in gathering humanitarian content.
- Expertise in informed consent, safeguarding, trauma-informed practice, protection and responsible data management in humanitarian or other high-risk settings.
- A sound understanding of power, representation, gender equality, sexual and reproductive health and rights, and locally led humanitarian action.
- Experience developing concise guidelines, toolkits, training materials or editorial standards for other international organisations or civil society networks.
- Excellent English writing and facilitation skills, with the ability to turn complex ethical and operational issues into clear, practical guidance for diverse audiences.
- Experience consulting across cultures and regions and working collaboratively.

**Timeline:**

**The consultancy will run in several phases, comprising approximately 6–10 weeks of work spread over a longer period to accommodate consultations, feedback and revisions.**

**Budget:** Up to USD22,000.00.

jobs.title: Fieldwork Consultancy for the SGBV Care Pathway Study (Addis Ababa)
jobs.description:
Tiko Africa Ethiopia invites qualified consultants or firms to carry out a mixed-methods study on screening, service readiness, quality of care and access barriers along the SGBV care pathway for adolescent girls and young women (AGYW) aged 15–24 in Addis Ababa. The consultant will lead the study from data collection through analysis and reporting.

**1. Background**

Tiko is an African non-profit organisation addressing the “Triple Threat” facing adolescent girls and young women in Sub-Saharan Africa: early pregnancy, HIV and sexual and gender-based violence (SGBV). The Triple Threat package, delivered through Tiko’s technology-enabled, community-driven platform, is Tiko’s standard programme in all of its intervention areas. In Addis Ababa, Tiko supports screening, care and referral for survivors of SGBV, and for young women identified through transactional or survival sex screening under the Dignified Livelihoods Initiative (DILI), which adds livelihood support to the Triple Threat package.

This study asks where adolescent girls and young women drop out of the SGBV care pathway, and why. It looks at screening and disclosure, service readiness, quality of care, and barriers to access and referral completion. Findings will help Tiko strengthen the SGBV component of the Triple Threat package.

The study uses in-depth interviews, key informant interviews, focus group discussions, a short provider survey, and existing Tiko platform and programme records, existing facility readiness (SARA) records, and a review and synthesis of the published and grey literature. The study protocol and English tools are final, subject to the inception review and any ethics conditions, and the ethics review process is underway.

The study instruments are: the AGYW in-depth interview guide (Tool 1) with its journey-mapping card (Tool 1a); the provider key informant interview guide (Tool 2); the referral-partner key informant interview guide (Tool 3); the community focus group guide (Tool 4); the provider survey, built in KoboToolbox (Tool 5); the service readiness (SARA) extraction template (Tool 6); and the routine programme data extraction template (Tool 7).

Tiko recruits and screens participants for eligibility through its own safe channels. The consultant schedules and conducts the interviews. Sample sizes are targets; any change must be discussed with and approved by Tiko. Tiko's recruitment list assigns each participant's entry route and pathway stage using the rules in protocol Section 7.4.1, including girls identified through both routes and the stage that takes priority when more than one applies. For the transactional or survival sex route, the list also records duration of engagement.

Pathway stages. The five stages in the study are: (1) recently screened or identified; (2) accessed one or more services; (3) referred and completed the referral; (4) referred but did not attend; and (5) started services then discontinued. Recruitment aims for about equal numbers per stage within each interview group Tiko will tell the consultant if a stage cannot be filled, and shortfalls are reported, not absorbed into other stages.

Sampling and allocation. Tiko will confirm in writing, before fieldwork, the allocation of the 20 provider interviews by cadre (providers, mobilizers, case managers, counsellors), and of the community, caregiver and peer groups. The provider survey includes providers, mobilizers and case managers and covers screening practice, training and protocol awareness, service availability and referral practice. The qualitative samples are not designed for statistical comparison between age groups or pathway stages; differences are described and interpreted qualitatively.

**2. Purpose of the consultancy**

The consultant will carry out ethical, high-quality data collection; transcribe and translate the data; analyze the quantitative and qualitative findings; and write the study report. The consultant works under the direction of the Tiko research team and delivers findings that Tiko can use to improve SGBV screening, service delivery and referral.

## **3. Scope of work**

### **3.1 Data collection targets**

**-Method** - In-depth interviews (IDIs), SGBV screening or disclosure route; **Target** - 30 (15 aged 15–17; 15 aged 18–24); **Participants -** AGYW at different pathway stages

**-Method -** IDIs, transactional or survival sex screening route; **Target** - 20; **Participants -** AGYW across the five pathway stages

**-Method -** Key informant interviews (KIIs); **Target** - 32 (20 providers, mobilizers, case managers and counsellors; 12 referral partners); **Participants -** Service staff and partner organisations

**-Method -** Focus group discussions (FGDs); **Target** - 6–8 groups of 6–8 people (4–6 community and caregiver groups; 2 peer groups of young women aged 18–24 not enrolled in Tiko services); **Participants -** Community members, caregivers, peers

**-Method -** Structured provider survey; **Target** - About 30; **Participants -** Providers, mobilizers, case managers and counsellors

**-Method -** Secondary data: routine Tiko platform records; **Target** - All records for study service points in the reference period; **Participants -** Screening, service and referral data, extracted with Tool 7

**-Method -** Secondary data: service readiness (SARA) records; **Target** - All study service points; **Participants -** Existing facility readiness assessments, extracted with Tool 6

**-Method -** Literature review and synthesis; **Target** - Published and grey literature from Ethiopia and comparable urban settings; **Participants -** Updates the protocol’s review; used to interpret findings

### **3.2 Activities**

**-Inception.** Review the protocol and tools, and agree upon a work plan, field schedule and quality-control plan with Tiko.The inception report also includes: (a) a protocol and tools review that assesses feasibility and recommends any changes, which the Tiko research team reviews and validates before the tools are finalised; (b) a sampling and recruitment strategy explaining how the consultant will work with Tiko's recruitment lists and safe channels to select participants and fill each pathway stage; and (c) a literature review and synthesis that updates the protocol's review with relevant evidence, especially from Ethiopia and other urban settings (maximum 5 pages). Literature findings are reported separately from the study's primary findings and used to interpret the results.

**-Tools in Amharic.** Translate the tools and information sheets from English into Amharic and back-translate them. Resolve differences with the research team with a small number of participants outside the sample, recruited by Tiko under the approved protocol. Tiko submits any substantive change made after translation or piloting to the REC as an amendment, and only REC-approved versions are used in fieldwork.

**-Field team.** Recruit and train female interviewers and facilitators with experience in sensitive research. Training lasts at least five \[5\] days and covers the protocol, consent and assent, trauma-informed interviewing, safeguarding, referral to psychosocial support and data security. Training also covers the study's interviewing rules (never asking a girl to describe the violence or to confirm her screening result, and non-labelling language for transactional or survival sex), recording service-point codes, and the reporting duty when a girl under 18 discloses abuse.

**-Data collection.** Conduct all interviews, discussions and the survey in private, safe settings, in Amharic. Record audio only with consent. Record the service-point code in the provider survey (Tool 5, A8) and against each service an AGYW describes (Tool 1, Section E), so findings can be linked to the SARA data.

**-Transcription and translation.** Transcribe audio verbatim in Amharic and translate into English. A named reviewer checks at least \[10%\] of transcripts against the audio. Transcription and translation run progressively during fieldwork, not only at the end, with a fuller check of each interviewer’s first transcripts so quality problems are found early.

**-Supervision and quality control.** Supervise fieldwork daily, review interview notes weekly, and hold debriefs after each fieldwork cycle.

**-Data handover.** Deliver to Tiko: Amharic and English transcripts; audio files; raw and cleaned survey datasets with a codebook; the qualitative codebook and coded project file; completed journey-mapping cards; the consent log, kept separately from the study data; a log of safeguarding incidents and referrals; a protocol-deviation log; and the fieldwork log. All files except the consent log are de-identified.

**-Analysis.** Agree an analysis plan with Tiko. Analyse the qualitative data thematically, using a coding framework and software such as ATLAS.ti. Analyse the survey data descriptively. Triangulate with the service-readiness (SARA) and routine programme data that Tiko provides, and compare findings across pathway stages, entry routes (SGBV screening or disclosure, and transactional or survival sex screening) and age bands. Develop a care-pathway analysis matrix showing, for each pathway stage, where participants enter, where they progress, where and why they discontinue or face barriers, and what supports referral completion and continued care. Assess quality of care against the WHO first-line survivor-centred response (LIVES) and the WHO/UNAIDS Global Standards for quality health care services for adolescents. From the routine data, produce a descriptive screening-to-completion cascade for each entry route, reporting a stage only where its denominator is recorded. Triangulate across AGYW, provider and referral partner interviews, the provider survey and the existing records, and highlight where these perspectives differ. With about 30 survey respondents, survey results are descriptive only and are not presented as representative of all providers in Addis Ababa. The consultant analyses the existing SARA and facility-readiness records and does not collect new facility data unless Tiko agrees in advance.

**-Validation.** Present emerging findings to the Tiko research team and invited stakeholders in one validation meeting, and revise them using the feedback.

**-Reporting.** Submit a draft and a final report (maximum \[20\] pages plus annexes) with an executive summary, methods, findings by objective, programme and policy recommendations, and a short brief of 3–5 pages for non-technical readers. The discussion interprets the findings against existing evidence and relevant standards (WHO LIVES, the WHO/UNAIDS adolescent quality standards and Ethiopian national SGBV guidelines), noting where findings from Addis Ababa agree with or differ from other settings. Literature findings are kept distinct from the study’s primary findings. Authorship or acknowledgement in any publication follows actual contribution and Tiko’s publication and authorship policy.

### **3.3 Tiko's responsibilities**

• Ethics approval and any amendments, with written confirmation before fieldwork starts.

• Recruitment and eligibility screening, with recruitment lists showing each participant’s study code, entry route, pathway stage, age band and, for the transactional or survival sex route, duration of engagement.

• The study list of service-point codes, and completed SARA and routine-data extraction templates (Tools 6 and 7) for the study service points.

• A named psychosocial support focal person on call during fieldwork, and the referral directory.

• A data-sharing agreement and the secure storage location for study data.

• Tablets and a KoboToolbox account for the provider survey \[confirm: Tiko or the consultant\].

• Participant reimbursement and interview venues \[confirm: paid directly by Tiko, or included in the consultant’s budget\].

## **4. Ethics, safeguarding and data protection**

Tiko Africa Ethiopia manages and coordinates the ethics review and Institutional Review Board (IRB) approval process for this study. Applicants and consultants do not need to budget or plan for IRB approval in their proposals. The consultant must follow the final approved protocol, any ethics conditions that Tiko passes on, and the requirements below. Fieldwork starts only when Tiko confirms in writing that approval is in place.

- Obtain written informed consent from adults and assent from girls aged 15–17.The protocol asks the REC to waive parental permission for girls aged 15–17; if the REC does not grant the waiver, Tiko will issue the revised guardian procedure before fieldwork. Where a girl aged 15–17 has no parent or guardian available (for example, she lives independently, is separated from her family or is street-connected), follow the REC-approved alternative, such as consent from a trusted adult she nominates or an independent advocate appointed by Tiko, so that these girls are not excluded. Use witnessed or thumbprint consent for participants who cannot read, as approved by the REC
- Do not contact or approach potential participants outside Tiko’s approved recruitment arrangements.
- Follow the approved protocol when a participant discloses abuse, immediate danger or another safeguarding concern. Make referrals through the approved referral procedure, taking account of the participant’s safety and consent.
- In focus groups, inform participants during the consent and assent process when deciding to participate that confidentiality is requested from all participants but cannot be guaranteed once information is shared in the group.
- Interview in private, with a trained female interviewer, and never at a place or time that puts the participant at risk.
- Do not give incentives beyond the reimbursement approved by the REC. Provide refreshments to all participants. Give AGYW interview and focus group participants the reimbursement for transport and time set out in the approved protocol and consent materials; providers and referral partners interviewed during working hours receive refreshments only.
- Stop or postpone an interview if the participant is in distress or danger, and link her to Tiko's psychosocial focal person the same day.
- Report any disclosure of immediate risk, and any safeguarding concern, to the Tiko study coordinator within 24 hours, following the referral and reporting procedure in the protocol.
- Use participant codes only. Keep names, contacts and recordings on encrypted devices, upload them to the designated Tiko secure storage location, and delete all local copies only after Tiko confirms successful receipt and handover. Delete local audio copies once Tiko confirms the upload and the transcript check is complete. Handle personal data in line with Ethiopian personal data protection law and the data-sharing agreement.
- Staff and subcontractors sign a confidentiality and code-of-conduct agreement, including Tiko's safeguarding and PSEA policies, before fieldwork.
- Provide supervisors and interviewers with debriefing and psychosocial support during fieldwork.

## **5. Deliverables and timeline**

The schedule below assumes the ethics review is complete before week 1. It will shift if that is delayed:

-Deliverable - Contract signing and inception report: work plan, field schedule, analysis plan, quality-control plan; Due - Week 2

-Deliverable - Amharic tools (translated, back-translated, piloted) and training report; Due - Week 5

-Deliverable - Fieldwork progress reports; due - Every 2 weeks during fieldwork

-Deliverable - Completion of data collection, submit clean data (transcripts, datasets) and fieldwork log; Due - Week 13

-Deliverable - Draft report with analysis outputs (coded transcripts, survey tables); Due - Week 17

-Deliverable - Validation meeting, final analysis and submission of final report, brief and cleaned dataset; Due - Week 20

Tiko pays within \[30\] days of accepting each deliverable and gives written comments on each draft within \[10\] working days. The fieldwork report covers response rates by group, deviations from the protocol, safeguarding incidents, challenges and lessons. The study runs about 20 weeks in total. Each payment depends on Tiko’s written acceptance of the related deliverable.

## **6. Qualifications and team**

A lead consultant and a field team. A firm may propose one lead, named supervisors and a named analyst.

- **Team lead.** Master’s degree in public health, social science, gender studies or a related field, at least \[10\] years of social and public health research, including at least \[7\] years leading qualitative and mixed-methods research on SGBV or adolescent health in Ethiopia, including analysis and report writing. Demonstrated experience leading research with adolescents on sensitive topics, including SGBV or other safeguarding-related research, is required.
- **Field supervisors (2–3).** Master’s degree in public health, social science or a related field, and at least \[5\] years of qualitative fieldwork, including at least \[2\] years supervising field teams, preferably on gender-based violence or with adolescents.
- **Interviewers and facilitators.** Women fluent in Amharic, with at least a bachelor’s degree in social science, public health, nursing or a related field, at least \[2\] years of qualitative interviewing experience, and training in trauma-informed practice. Experience with adolescents is an advantage.
- **Transcription and translation staff.** Native Amharic speakers with strong written English and a record of accurate verbatim transcription.
- Qualitative data analyst: Master’s degree in a relevant field and at least \[5\] years in qualitative analysis and in literature review and synthesis, secondary data analysis and triangulation, with proven use of qualitative analysis such as ATLAS.ti or NVivo. The proposal must name who is responsible for qualitative coding and thematic analysis, quantitative data cleaning and descriptive analysis, integration of findings, and report writing. Qualitative analysis experience is assessed separately from skill with statistical software.
- Quantitative analyst. Degree in a relevant field and at least \[5\] years analysing survey and secondary programme data with Stata, SPSS or R, including data cleaning, descriptive analysis and triangulation of data from several sources. Either analyst role may be held by the team lead if they meet the requirements.

The team lead must show recent ethics-approved research, a working knowledge of Addis Ababa, and a clear safeguarding record. Conflicts of interest, such as current work for Tiko or its partners at study sites, must be declared.

**7. Ownership and confidentiality**

All data, tools, recordings and reports belong to Tiko. The consultant may not share, publish or reuse them without written permission, and the duty of confidentiality continues after the contract ends.

jobs.title: Independent UN Human Rights Council Expert (Arctic member of the Expert Mechanism on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples)
jobs.company: UN Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights
jobs.description:
**The Secretariat of the Human Rights Council is now accepting applications for the following additional mandate holder vacancy:**

**Expert Mechanism on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples, member from the Arctic**

This **unremunerated** United Nations expert position established by the Human Rights Council is expected to be filled at the Council’s 64th session (22 February – 2 April 2027), with the appointment to be made at the end of that session. Individuals seeking appointment should have extensive recognized professional experience and expertise in the field of human rights, with an emphasis on the particular human rights issues to which the position relates.

The “**special procedures**” of the Human Rights Council are independent human rights experts with mandates to report and advise on human rights from a thematic or country-specific perspective. Special procedures are either an individual (called "Special Rapporteur" or "Independent Expert") or a working group composed of five members, one from each of the five United Nations regional groups: Africa, Asia-Pacific, Latin America and the Caribbean, Eastern Europe and the Western European and other group. These experts are appointed by and report to the Human Rights Council.

**Subsidiary expert mechanisms** provide the Council with thematic expertise, focused mainly on studies, research-based advice or best practices. They meet and report annually to the Council. Members of expert mechanisms are independent human rights experts selected and appointed by the Human Rights Council in the same way as special procedure mandate holders.

For members of the **Expert Mechanism on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples (EMRIP)**, candidates need to represent one of the Indigenous sociocultural regions for which vacancies have been advertised. Additional information about EMRIP can be found here: \[ [**Word**](https://www.ohchr.org/sites/default/files/documents/hrbodies/hrcouncil/faq-selection-emrip.docx) | [**PDF**](https://www.ohchr.org/sites/default/files/documents/hrbodies/hrcouncil/faq-selection-emrip.pdf) \]**.**

The work of independent mandate holders is unpaid. Those appointed as mandate holders serve in their personal capacities. They are not United Nations staff members, they are not based in United Nations offices in Geneva or at another United Nations location, and they do not receive salary or other financial compensation, except for travel expenses and daily subsistence allowance of “experts on mission”. Their specific functions are defined in the HRC resolutions creating or extending their mandate. Candidates must be available to perform effectively the functions of the mandate and to respond to its requirements, such as participating in Working Group and Human Rights Council sessions in Geneva, travelling on country missions, drafting reports according to established deadlines, organizing and participating in consultations and meetings, addressing allegations of human rights violations with all concerned, providing advice to States and other stakeholders on issues related to their mandate and engaging with a variety of stakeholders. Candidates should be able to dedicate an estimated time of four to six months per year to the work of a mandate depending on its workload.

**Annual Project Budget**

521,301 EURO

Hoffnungszeichen | Sign of Hope e.V. (SoH) is announcing **an open tender procedure for external independent financial audit services in Armenia**.

**Background and Organisational Setting**

SoH is a Christian motivated organisation for Human Rights, Humanitarian Assistance and Development Cooperation. Based in Constance, Germany, SoH is dedicated to helping those in distress and exploited people worldwide.

An audit is commissioned under the German Federal Ministry of Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) funding guidelines for development projects run by private German executing agencies.

SoH will be the private German executing agency and the contracting party, with Development Principles (DP) being the local implementing agency.

The project aims to support Armenian refugees from Nagorno-Karabakh and local youth through a diverse educational programme that promotes their social and economic integration. The project focuses on four key objectives: Acquisition of foundational skills for employment and future prospects: 180 participants acquire skills through six modules that enable access to employment and further education. Personal development and career guidance are integrated. Development of practical professional skills and integration into Companies: 60 participants enhance marketing visual content creation, graphic design, copywriting, and digital marketing skills in practice oriented trainings and apply them in companies during stages. Promotion of entrepreneurial activities and product development: 150 participants develop entrepreneurial skills, receive individual mentoring and are supported in creating 30 market-ready products. 5–10 outstanding business ideas will receive targeted financial support to foster economic self-reliance Establishment of a sustainable alumni network: A structured alumni network promotes knowledge exchange and secures project sustainability, with at least 150 alumni actively involved. The project strengthens employability, entrepreneurship, and social integration in Armenia. In the long term, it contributes to the socio-economic empowerment of refugees and local youth by fostering resilient communities that support Armenia’s development.

**Audit Objectives**

The purpose of the in-depth audit is to provide SoH with a sound basis for its accountability, transparency and accuracy in the financial disclosure towards the funding agency BMZ. The tasks of this recruitment relate to:

- An annual audit, with a detailed examination of all the supporting documents for the period of 01.10.2025 – 31.12.2026;

This in-depth audit will verify the compliance with standards of the funding agency BMZ, SoH, national regulations and the international accounting standards (ISA).

The auditor will review all of the project’s financial documents, receipts lists, records of transactions, all vouchers and receipts disbursed, and relevant project documents in order to come up with a professional, independent opinion on the financial accounting of the project “Humans of Tomorrow (HoT): Promotion of professional qualifications, entrepreneurship and integration of refugees” for all funds received and expended by DP from 01 October 2025 to 31 December 2026.

Additionally, the audit shall give recommendations on strengths, weaknesses, and required improvement in the project-related financial and human resources management systems of DP.

The audit will support the project quality assurance measures implemented by SoH and contribute to the decision-making process with regard to the project management and monitoring of finances by SoH and DP.

**Expected Deliverables**

The auditor is expected to produce an audit report, an audit certificate and a management letter, which will comprise the following:

1. Presentation of the scope and mandate of the audit, as well as the list of documents that formed the evidence for the audit,
2. An opinion whether financial statements (statement of accounts broken down for each year being audited) are issued in accordance with the financial reporting framework of the project, BMZ requirements and an internationally recognized accounting standard,
3. A checked, signed and stamped list of all (100%) project costs receipts, sorted by BMZ budget lines (list is provided by the local implementing partner).
4. Recommendations on identified shortcomings, and, if applicable, comments on the follow-up of audit observations and recommendations from previous years.

Audit documents can be issued in English or German.

**Scope of the Audit**

The audit should focus on the following:

- The correctness and completeness of the accounting records,
- The financial report, showing all project related income and expenditure structured by budget lines,
- Deviations of expenditure by budget lines. The expenditure, which exceeds or falls below the budget appropriations by more than 20 %, shall be explained separately, if the approval of the BMZ has not previously been obtained,
- That receipts and relevant supporting documents are available for all project related income and expenditures (100% verification),
- The management of the funds made available, which includes the transfer of project funds, all interest earned from the project funds during the reporting period and further income generated by the project,
- Reviewing the appropriate use of funds according to the project objectives,
- Evaluation of the efficiency and cost-effectiveness of the usage of funds,
- Budget adherence through the comparison between budgeted and actual costs in the currency in which the expenditure was incurred. The audit report will not convert the examined amounts into the Euro amounts,
- Reviewing if personnel costs and social security contributions conform to the regulations in the project country and are locally comparable,
- The economical use of the project equipment and assets,
- The inventory and the use of capital items, their whereabouts and their purposive usage,
- Compliance with the legal framework of the project (project agreements and annexes, contracts, etc.) and the donor requirements,
- Compliance with the policies of the local implementing partner regarding procurement, financial administration, human resources management and travel.

**Procedures and Communication**

The auditor will be given access to all necessary documents in the project offices through the local implementing partner DP as well as relevant donor documents through SoH.

The auditor will be responsible to set up a schedule in agreement with the local implementing partner DP. Any expenses for field trips, postal and translation services and other expenses shall be included in the auditor’s proposed budget. DP will support the auditor with logistics and arrangements, however, all payments of the contract will be made directly by SoH.

**Qualifications and Experience**

- Necessary qualification to serve as a recognized independent auditing authority,
- Minimum of five (5) years of experience conducting external independent audits of projects funded by international institutional donors in Armenia,
- Experience in conducting audits for BMZ-funded projects is desirable.

jobs.description:
INTERSOS est une Organisation Humanitaire Non Gouvernementale, à but non lucratif, qui a l’objectif d’assister les victimes de désastres naturels et de conflits armés. INTERSOS base son action sur les valeurs de la solidarité, de la justice, de la dignité humaine, de l’égalité des droits et des opportunités pour tous les peuples, du respect des diversités, de la cohabitation, de l’attention aux groupes sociales les plus vulnérables.

**Termes de référence**

**Intitulé du poste** : Coordinateur Logistique et Approvisionnement

**Code :** SR-38-10297

**Pays :** Democratic Republic of Congo

**Lieu d’affectation** : Goma with frequent mission in field location

**Date de prise de fonction** : 12/12/2026

**Durée du contrat** : 5 mois

**Sous la supervision de :** Chef de mission

**Supervision fonctionnelle :** Coordinatrice régionale de la logistique

**Personnes à charge :** Equipe logistique

**Lieu d'affectation:** sans famille

**Contexte général du projet**

La situation humanitaire en République démocratique du Congo (RDC) reste complexe et s’est globalement détériorée ces dernières années. Le pays est confronté à de multiples crises qui se chevauchent, en particulier dans les provinces de l’Est, qui font face à une violence endémique et à des conflits armés. L’insécurité a entraîné des déplacements massifs et répétés de populations. L’impact de la violence sur les civils demeure une préoccupation majeure, avec des violations régulières des droits humains et du droit international humanitaire, notamment des attaques ciblées contre les civils et une forte prévalence des violences basées sur le genre.

INTERSOS est présente en RDC depuis 2010 et intervient actuellement en Ituri, au Nord-Kivu et au Sud-Kivu à travers des programmes de protection, notamment des activités de monitoring de protection en partenariat avec le HCR. Ces interventions sont financées par différents bailleurs, notamment l’UNFPA, l’AICS, SV, ECHO, OCHA ainsi que d’autres partenaires financiers.

Une épidémie de maladie à virus Ebola a été déclarée en Ituri en mai 2026. Elle s’est ensuite propagée au Nord-Kivu, dans les zones contrôlées par le gouvernement de Kinshasa, ainsi qu’au Haut-Uélé et en Tshopo. INTERSOS contribue à la réponse à cette nouvelle urgence en partenariat avec différents bailleurs, notamment SV, l’AICS et le programme 8x1000 E.Vaudoise.

**Objectif général de la position**

Définir et mettre en œuvre l'ensemble des stratégies d'approvisionnement, de logistique et de TIC et d'appui à la mission, en veillant à la pertinence et à la cohérence des systèmes logistiques et d'approvisionnement, à l'adéquation des moyens mis à disposition et au respect des normes, protocoles et procédures d'INTERSOS pour favoriser le développement de la mission et optimiser l'impact des projets.

Travailler en étroite collaboration avec le personnel du programme et de l'administration afin d'assurer l'établissement de rapports, le soutien et l'assistance complets à l'égard de toutes les activités d'INTERSOS.

Est responsable de la gestion logistique du logiciel IMP et fait partie de la mission Senior Management Team (SMT).

**Principales responsabilités et tâches**

**Coordination et soutien**

- Participer activement à la définition et à la mise à jour de la planification et des budgets annuels des projets, en définissant des stratégies et en fournissant des conseils au chef de mission pour traduire les besoins identifiés en matière de logistique, d'approvisionnement et de TIC en objectifs, priorités et ressources nécessaires à la mission
- Est responsable du suivi de la mise en œuvre des activités de logistique, d'approvisionnement et de TIC dans la mission (construction et réhabilitation, stockage et fourniture de matériel non médical et médical, gestion de la flotte et transport, eau et assainissement, véhicules et moteurs, équipements/installations et infrastructures, règles de sécurité (mise en œuvre et application, TIC, biens, etc.)
- Assurer le respect des normes, protocoles et procédures d'INTERSOS, dans l'ensemble de la mission et conformément aux exigences des donateurs, y compris en matière d'approvisionnement. Rendre compte au chef de mission de l'élaboration des programmes en cours et proposer des stratégies de réorientation au besoin
- Est chargé d'assurer la référence technique et le soutien pour toutes les questions de logistique, d'approvisionnement et de TIC dans la mission, de fournir un encadrement au personnel logistique et de représenter INTERSOS lors de réunions avec les autorités, d'autres ONG et les réseaux de coordination pour les questions techniques et logistiques
- Assurer la production de SOP au niveau de la mission (si nécessaire) pour les besoins logistiques

**Gestion de l'information logistique**

- Fournir des rapports mensuels au chef de mission, au coordonnateur régional de la logistique et de l'approvisionnement (par l'intermédiaire du PGI) et aux personnes concernées sur l'évolution des projets et des missions du point de vue technique et logistique, et proposer des corrections si nécessaire.
- S'assurer que les données remontées dans le logiciel INTERSOS Logistics (Intersos Management Platform - IMP) sont correctement utilisées et exactes. Assurer la formation du personnel de la mission si nécessaire et soutenir la mise en œuvre du logiciel INTERSOS Logistics dans les missions

**Gestion de la chaîne d'approvisionnement et approvisionnement**

- Suivi de la performance globale de l'approvisionnement pour la mission. Assurer une planification efficace et rentable de l'approvisionnement en assurant la liaison avec le personnel technique, le coordonnateur sur le terrain et/ou les chefs de projet. Veiller à ce que les plans d'approvisionnement en ligne soient créés sur IMP et à jour, tout en garantissant le respect à tout moment des politiques et procédures d'approvisionnement d'INTERSOS et des bailleurs de fonds. Recherche pour déterminer les meilleurs produits et fournisseurs en termes de meilleur rapport qualité-prix, délais de livraison et qualité
- Assurer la coordination avec le département de l'administration et des finances pour s'assurer que les processus de paiement aux fournisseurs sont effectués à temps et dans le respect des systèmes financiers.
- Planifier et effectuer des vérifications sur le terrain pour s'assurer de l'uniformité du processus, de l'application et du maintien de la documentation et du classement appropriés.
- Élaborer et mettre en œuvre des instructions, des politiques et des procédures de gestion des contrats de service. Examiner et réévaluer les contrats de service existants et superviser les loyers réguliers, les paiements de services publics (c'est-à-dire l'électricité, l'eau, le gaz, etc.), les contrats d'entretien des bureaux et des maisons d'hôtes et les procédures relatives aux coûts de fonctionnement. Veiller à ce qu'ils soient correctement pris en charge par l'officier de la logistique et de l'approvisionnement et les assistants, l'administration et/ou les points focaux.
- Aperçu du fait que le gestionnaire de l'approvisionnement/adjoint et le coordonnateur sur le terrain (agent(e) de la logistique et de l'approvisionnement tiennent à jour une liste de fournisseurs préqualifiés par base
- Est responsable d'assurer le bon stockage de tous les matériaux du projet dans l'entrepôt/stock, dans le respect des SOP d'approvisionnement d'INTERSOS et des contrôles d'inventaire réguliers tous les trimestres
- Vérifier et coordonner avec le personnel logistique que les livraisons de marchandises sont effectuées comme prévu et correctement stockées
- Préparer et lancer les documents d'appel d'offres en coordination avec l'équipe d'approvisionnement

**Gestion des transports**

- S'assurer que le modèle de gestion de flotte d'INTERSOS, les protocoles de sécurité des mouvements et le manuel d'identité de la marque sont appliqués dans les missions - la flotte est vérifiée et régulièrement entretenue, les véhicules sont assurés et les taxes sont payées.
- Assurer le suivi de la surveillance adéquate de la consommation de carburant et de l'utilisation du carnet de bord des véhicules, du carnet d'entretien, du carnet d'huile et d'autres formats et modèles de flotte par le personnel logistique du coordonnateur sur le terrain. S'assurer que la documentation appropriée des véhicules (c.-à-d. location, assurance, inspection mécanique, etc.) est correctement gérée par le personnel de la logistique.
- Contribuer à l'élaboration d'approches durables en matière de gestion des transports en rationalisant la politique environnementale d'INTERSOS et les suggestions des bureaux régionaux.

**Gestion des installations et des communications**

- Superviser l'installation et l'entretien d'espaces de bureaux fonctionnels et d'installations de maisons d'hôtes avec des conditions de vie adéquates et conformément aux normes minimales et au manuel d'identité de marque d'INTERSOS. S'assurer de l'application des mesures de sûreté et de sécurité définies et effectuer des visites d'inspection pour évaluer les besoins de réhabilitation des installations
- Veiller à ce que les installations disposent d'une infrastructure et d'un équipement informatiques et de communication appropriés pour assurer la maintenance des plates-formes logicielles INTERSOS et conformément aux politiques et procédures - permettant une communication permanente entre les immobilisations, les projets, les bases et le siège et une bonne gestion des bases. S'assurer que tous les membres du personnel de la mission reçoivent une formation adéquate sur l'utilisation de l'équipement de communication disponible (p. ex., téléphones satellites, radios HF/VHF, ordinateurs, etc.)
- Contribuer à l'élaboration d'approches durables en matière de gestion des installations en rationalisant la politique environnementale d'INTERSOS et les suggestions des bureaux régionaux.

**Gestion d'actifs**

- Superviser l'achat, l'utilisation et l'entretien des actifs informatiques, de l'équipement de bureau et de projet, ainsi que des outils de communication, tout en veillant à ce que tous les actifs de la mission enregistrés dans le PGI soient documentés, qu'ils reçoivent des numéros d'actifs INTERSOS uniques, qu'ils soient étiquetés et enregistrés conformément aux politiques et procédures de gestion des actifs.
- Rapportez la liste des actifs à la fin du projet et supervisez le transfert des actifs en fonction de la destination définie avec le service des programmes
- Superviser la vérification régulière des immobilisations tous les trimestres

**Gestion des ressources humaines**

- Coordonner l'équipe logistique et participer aux processus RH (recrutement, formation, briefing/débriefing, évaluation, potentiel, détection, développement du personnel et communication interne) afin d'assurer à la fois le dimensionnement et la quantité de connaissances requises pour les activités dont il est responsable

**Sécurité appliquée**

- En collaboration avec le Chef de Mission et le Coordonnateur de la Sécurité (le cas échéant), il est chargé de co-définir et de suivre les aspects techniques de la politique de réduction des risques, du transport, de la communication, de la protection, de l'identification et de la préparation des aspects techniques de la politique et des directives de sécurité de la mission, du plan d'évacuation et du plan d'urgence, du suivi quotidien des règles de sécurité et du signalement au Chef de Mission de tout problème. À cette fin, en l'absence d'un point focal dédié à la sécurité, le coordonnateur logistique doit créer un environnement approprié pour faciliter l'échange d'informations sur les situations de sécurité. Il s'agit de la sauvegarde de sécurité en l'absence du chef de mission.

**Profil requis**

- Diplôme essentiel et spécialisation en logistique et/ou gestion de la chaîne d'approvisionnement
- Essentiellement, au moins quatre ans d'expérience professionnelle dans des postes logistiques pertinents et une expérience humanitaire antérieure avec des ONG dans des pays en développement.
- Expérience préalable souhaitable dans le domaine des situations d'urgence
- Connaissances essentielles en informatique (Word, Excel et Internet)
- Le langage de la mission est essentiel.
- Langue de travail locale souhaitable
- Vision stratégique
- Leadership
- Gestion et perfectionnement du personnel
- Orientation vers le service
- Flexibilité comportementale
- Orientation vers les résultats et la qualité
- Gestion du stress
- Engagement envers les principes d'INTERSOS

## **Conditions générales et avantages :**

- Fourchette de salaire : 12 - 3.690€ - 4.245€ monthly gross
- Hébergement :Shared Guesthouse
- R&R : 7 days of psycho-physical recovery every 12 weeks + 1000€ allowance.
- Congés annuels : 2,5 jours par mois
- Assurance médicale pour le personnel
- Transport et visa : billets d’avion aller-retour. Pour les missions d’une durée d’au moins 9 mois, un billet supplémentaire vers le pays de résidence et retour sur la mission est également fourni.
- Formation d’intégration : une semaine de formation en ligne avant le déploiement
