**Présentation de la mission**

TGH est active dans 13 pays et met en œuvre des programmes d'urgence, de réhabilitation et de développement depuis 1994, accumulant une expertise reconnue dans les secteurs de l’EHA, Sécurité Alimentaire et Moyens d’Existence, Protection de l’Enfance et Éducation.

TGH est présente au Tchad depuis novembre 2023, avec un bureau principal à N'Djamena, où est basée l’équipe de coordination, et un bureau dans le Ouaddai (Adré). En 2025, grâce à des financements de la DG ECHO et du gouvernement français (CDCS, IFSAN), TGH a ouvert des bureaux dans le Wadi Fira (Guéréda et Iriba).

Forte de son expérience au Soudan depuis 2004, TGH a acquis une connaissance approfondie du contexte local et des populations, un atout précieux pour ses interventions à l'Est du Tchad auprès des populations réfugiées venant du Darfour. Dans la province du Ouaddaï, TGH mène des activités d’assainissement et de gestion des déchets grâce au soutien de fondations privées via une approche incluant à la fois les populations hôtes, retournées et déplacées. Dans la province du Wadi Fira, TGH travaille à la fois dans les camps des réfugiés et dans les villages et mène des interventions intégrées en matière d’eau, hygiène et assainissement, en protection de l’enfance et en sécurité alimentaire.

Le bureau de TGH à N’Djaména accueille également une partie de coordination de la mission Soudan, et les missions Tchad et Soudan partagent certaines ressources humaines (Chargé de Liaison, Coordinateur Logistique, Superviseur Logistique, etc.).

**Description du poste**

La·le DP dirige les opérations, gère les équipes et représente l’organisation au Tchad. Elle·Il établit le lien entre la stratégie globale de TGH et la stratégie spécifique pays, et veille au respect des valeurs de TGH et des principes humanitaires. De ce fait, la·le DP travaille sous la responsabilité du Responsable géographique basé au siège.

La·le DP supervise directement le Coordinateur programme, la Coordinatrice Admin/RH/Finance et le Coordinateur Logistique.

Cette fiche de poste pourra évoluer en fonction du développement de la mission.

**Principales responsabilités**

**Représentation et coordination**

- Assurer la représentation de TGH au Tchad, tant en capitale que dans les provinces de l’Est, y compris au sein du Forum des ONGI.
- Développer et maintenir des relations de travail efficaces avec les parties prenantes au Tchad, y compris les ONG internationales et nationales, les ministères/autorités nationales et locales et les agences des Nations Unies.
- Participer activement aux réunions sectorielles et de coordination des Nations unies, les réunions de coordination du gouvernement et d'autres forums de programmation au Tchad, et déléguer les membres de l’équipe là où pertinent ou nécessaire.
- Contribuer à la complémentarité et aux synergies des programmes en entretenant des relations efficaces avec les organisations internationales et locales, en particulier celles qui travaillent dans les zones géographiques ciblées et les mêmes secteurs.
- Entretenir des relations efficaces avec les bailleurs et soutenir le suivi des opportunités de financement pour les programmes de TGH Tchad.
- Appuyer la mission TGH Soudan dans le déploiement des équipes et des programmes

**Conception et développement de programme**

- Appuyer à la conception et réalisation d'évaluations sur le terrain en fonction des besoins des populations, des priorités de TGH et des possibilités de financement afin de proposer des interventions sur le court, moyen et long terme.
- Collaborer avec le Desk au développement et l'affinement de la vision stratégique et de la programmation de TGH au Tchad.
- Diriger et coordonner l'élaboration et la révision des stratégies sectorielles et des plans de travail conformément à la stratégie nationale du Tchad.

**Gestion de la sécurité**

- Assurer une veille contextuelle politique, sécuritaire et socio-économique du pays et tirer des analyses
- Assurer la bonne diffusion de l’analyse et des informations sur la mission et au siège
- Actualiser régulièrement les outils de gestion de la sécurité de la mission en conformité avec les politiques et les formats de l’association
- Assurer la bonne diffusion, connaissance et respect par tout le personnel des règles et consignes de sécurité en vigueur
- Garantir un niveau et des modalités d’opérations adaptés au contexte
- Appuyer les responsables de bases ou les référents de zone dans la collecte d’information et l’analyse du contexte
- Intervenir auprès des acteurs de la sécurité politiques, militaires, groupes armés, religieux, leaders communautaires et d’opinions, etc. dans le cadre de la sécurité collective (développement de réseaux, négociation d’accès, renforcement de l’acceptation, etc.)
- Gérer, en lien avec le siège et si nécessaire l’ambassade de France et les UN, les incidents de sécurité et les situations d’urgence
- Maintenir un lien actif avec les organisations / instances en charge du suivi de la sécurité au Tchad ex. groupe WhatsApp sur la sécurité, INSO, réunions auprès de l’Ambassade de France, etc.

**Soutien général à la mission**

- Contribuer au respect des mesures de sécurité appliquées sur la mission et signaler rapidement toute violation de ces mesures.
- Soutenir la mise en œuvre des procédures internes en coordination avec les départements support et avec la mission Soudan.
- Soutenir les processus d'amélioration interne. Contribuer au partage des connaissances et des informations au sein de l'équipe TGH.
- Sensibiliser l'équipe programme aux valeurs humanitaires fondamentales que sont l'humanité, l'indépendance, la neutralité et l'impartialité, et promouvoir le respect de ces valeurs au sein de l'équipe.

**Gestion de programme**

- Soutenir l'équipe programme dans la mise en œuvre de la programmation et le suivi de l'avancement des indicateurs et des résultats du projet, en veillant à la conformité avec les exigences de la proposition de projet, les politiques des bailleurs et les normes sectorielles.
- Superviser le coordinateur programme dans la gestion des subventions, les rapports et les communications, en assurant la validation finale et la qualité avant la soumission des rapports externes, des mises à jour et d'autres publications destinées à des publics externes avec le desk et les référents techniques.
- Assurer la coordination du programme au sein de TGH (entre les différents projets, départements, régions) et avec les parties prenantes externes (ONG nationales et internationales, agences des Nations unies, etc.).
- Pour les nouveaux projets, en collaboration avec les référents techniques du siège, les équipes de terrain et les services support, veiller à ce que le processus de démarrage soit adapté (y compris les réunions de lancement) et à ce que les plans de travail et les plans d'approvisionnement et de recrutement soient élaborés dès le départ.
- Veiller à ce que les mécanismes de redevabilité soient en place et fonctionnels

**Gestion d’équipe**

- Superviser directement l’équipe de coordination.
- Identifier les besoins en matière de renforcement des capacités pour le personnel et les partenaires impliqués dans la réponse. Participer au renforcement des connaissances et des compétences de l'équipe programme et des partenaires.
- Réaliser les évaluations des membres de son équipe.

*Cette liste de responsabilités pourra être modifiée en fonction des besoins et de l'évolution du contexte.*

**Sécurité, conditions de travail et de vie**

La mission est actuellement logée dans des appartements au-dessus des bureaux. Sur le terrain, les conditions de vie sont plus rudimentaires. Le contexte actuel au Tchad peut entrainer un renforcement temporaire des procédures de sécurité (restrictions de mouvements, etc.). Il y a des vols réguliers vers et depuis le Tchad pour des destinations régionales.

**Priorités pour les 3 premiers mois**

- Contrôle et qualité des programmes en cours
- Développer le réseau de bailleurs et partenaires humanitaires et de développement
- Coconstruire la stratégie de la mission avec les équipes

**Profil**

- Expérience dans une ONG internationale
- Compétence d'analyse financière et de lecture budgétaire globale
- Expérience de travail dans des zones à haut risque, y compris les catastrophes et les États fragiles et touchés par des conflits (au moins 3 ans d'expérience sur le terrain)
- Compétences écrites et analytiques avérées
- Compétences très développées en matière de relations interpersonnelles, de collaboration et de communication, y compris en matière d'influence, de négociation et de mentorat
- Maîtrise indispensable de la langue française et de la langue anglaise à l’écrit comme à l’oral. L’arabe est un atout
- Compréhension conceptuelle approfondie de la gestion des risques de sécurité et des processus d'évaluation des risques.
- Une expérience préalable au Soudan ou au Tchad est un atout
- Capacité à travailler avec du matériel et des logiciels informatiques standard.
- Capacité avérée à utiliser la technologie et les outils numériques pour rationaliser la gestion des processus de sécurité (politiques, SOP, etc.) et le partage d'informations
- Volonté de travailler et de voyager fréquemment dans des environnements souvent difficiles et peu sûrs

**Conditions d’emploi**

Contrat salarié de droit français

Salaire brut mensuel de 3 400€ à 4 120€ selon expérience

Prime mensuelle de responsabilité 150€

Perdiem mensuel de 750€

Couverture médicale à 100% + assurance rapatriement + prévoyance

Prise en charge du logement et du transport international et local dans le cadre de la mission

Politique de repos - RnR de 06 jours ouvrés à 3 et 9 mois + allocation de 930€
25 jours de congés payés par an (prise en charge du transport par TGH tous les 6 mois)

Soutien psychologique (briefing/debriefing + 5 séances de suivi psychologique par an couvertes par la mutuelle santé)

Suivi RH individualisé et accompagnement du parcours professionnel

Poste non ouvert au départ en famille

TGH a opté pour une politique de rémunération volontairement simple et transparente, accessible sur notre site Internet [www.trianglegh.org](http://www.trianglegh.org). Les niveaux de salaire indiqués dans nos offres d'emploi sont fixés conformément à la grille de salaire TGH et ne sont pas négociables.

jobs.title: Research and Policy Coordinator - National
jobs.description:
**The Role: Research & Policy Coordinator**

**Oxfam Syria is looking for Research & Policy Coordinator**

**TEAM PURPOSE:** To amplify the voices of Syrians on matters of poverty and inequality, while increasing awareness of key issues affecting women, men, girls, and boys across Syria.

**JOB PURPOSE:** The Research and Policy Coordinator plays a central role in advancing Oxfam Syria's influencing agenda through evidence-based policy analysis, research, and strategic engagement. The position is responsible for operationalizing Oxfam Syria's policy work in line with the country influencing strategy, programmatic priorities, and evolving contextual dynamics. The position works closely with program teams in the field offices and the technical leads in the home office.

The role leads the generation of research and policy analysis, translates evidence into actionable recommendations, and supports the development of policy positions and influencing initiatives. It also fosters collaboration with partners and stakeholders, strengthens knowledge management and learning, and ensures that Oxfam's policy and advocacy work is informed by robust evidence, contextual understanding, and partner perspectives.

Through research, analysis, stakeholder engagement, and policy coordination, the Research and Policy Coordinator helps shape effective influencing strategies that advance Oxfam's objectives in Syria.

**What we are looking for:**

**Policy, Research, and Analysis:**

- Lead the direction and operationalization of Oxfam Syria's policy agenda, ensuring policy work is aligned with the influencing strategy, programmatic priorities, and evolving contextual trends.
- Monitor and analyze political, economic, social, humanitarian, and regulatory developments, identifying risks, opportunities, and implications for Oxfam Syria's work.
- Conduct qualitative and quantitative research and analysis to generate evidence that informs policy development, influencing priorities, strategic planning, and programme decision-making.
- Lead and coordinate research initiatives to address priority policy issues, emerging trends, and evidence gaps.
- Cultivate and manage strategic partnerships with civil society organizations, research institutions, and relevant networks to strengthen policy analysis, evidence generation, and influencing efforts.
- Ensure policy analysis reflects programme evidence, community perspectives, partner insights, and contextual realities across Oxfam Syria's areas of work.
- Produce and disseminate high-quality research and knowledge products, including policy briefs, situation analyses, reports, presentations, infographics, factsheets, talking points, and evidence summaries.
- Translate research findings into practical policy recommendations, advocacy messages, and audience-specific content to support decision-making and influencing objectives.
- Support internal learning and knowledge-sharing by documenting and disseminating key research findings, policy developments, lessons learned, and good practices.

**Stakeholder Engagement and Coordination:**

- Track and analyze stakeholders identified in the influencing strategy, including their priorities, positions, interests, and engagement dynamics, and integrate these insights into policy analysis and recommendations.
- Build and maintain effective relationships with partners, networks, institutions, and other stakeholders relevant to Oxfam Syria's policy and influencing objectives.
- Facilitate coordination and information-sharing between programme, MEAL, advocacy, communications, and external partners to support coherent policy, research, and influencing efforts.
- Identify and support strategic engagement opportunities that advance Oxfam Syria's policy and influencing priorities.
- Represent Oxfam Syria in meetings, coordination forums, consultations, and stakeholder engagements as required, and provide timely feedback on key developments, opportunities, and risks.

**Programme Support and Learning**

- Provide policy analysis, contextual insights, and evidence to inform programme design, implementation, adaptation, and learning.
- Support the integration of programme evidence, research findings, and emerging trends into policy work and influencing initiatives.
- Work closely with program teams in Research Coordinator Coordinator the field offices to identify evidence and learning needs and support research activities that strengthen programme quality and policy engagement.
- Contribute to the documentation of lessons learned, best practices, and evidence generated through programme implementation and policy engagement.

**General:**

- Demonstrate commitment to Oxfam's values, principles, and feminist approach, including the promotion of gender justice and women's rights.
- Adhere to humanitarian principles and support principled humanitarian action.
- Promote and uphold Oxfam's commitments to equity, diversity, inclusion, safeguarding, child safety, and staff health and wellbeing.
- Undertake any other duties consistent with the nature and level of the role as assigned by the line manager.

Person Specification:

Most importantly, every individual at Oxfam International Secretariat needs to be able to:

- Live our values of INCLUSION, ACCOUNTABILITY, EMPOWERMENT, COURAGE, SOLIDARITY and EQUALITY (read more about these [here)](https://oxfam.box.com/s/yfy4iyac8ulvoc01rkdg51awssv7ie1x)

Ensure you commit to our ORGANIZATIONAL ATTRIBUTES (including adhering to the Code of Conduct):

1. Be committed to our [feminist principles,](https://compass.oxfam.org/communities/gender-justice/wiki/feminism-practice) and to applying them in your day-to-day behaviour and your work. Be ready to keep learning, with

accountability to those who experience oppression as a result of their identities, such as their gender, race/ethnicity, disability, or class."

2. Be committed to undertaking Oxfam’s safeguarding training and adhering to relevant policies, to ensure all people who come into Oxfam are as safe as possible.

**Experience, Knowledge & Competencies**

**ESSENTIAL**

- Self-Awareness
- Sound judgement and decision-making
- Listening
- Vision Setting

**In addition:**

- Graduate qualification in a relevant field related to humanitarian and/or development programming and strategies.
- 3-5 years of research and policy work, both internationally and nationally.
- Proven capacity and experience in policy development and strategic analysis.
- Ability to engage with external stakeholders.
- Proven ability to communicate effectively in Arabic and English, both verbally and in writing, including the ability to convey complex realities in a simple yet engaging manner.
- Strong organizational and coordination skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities, stakeholders, and deadlines while maintaining high-quality standards.
- Collaborative and team-oriented, with the ability to work effectively across multidisciplinary teams and build constructive relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
- Team player, self-motivated, able to meet agreed deadlines with minimal supervision.
- Commitment to gender justice and ensuring issues of gender are an integral part of all work.
- Ability to travel around Syria, including for overnight stays.
- Ability to develop innovative approaches to research, policy analysis, knowledge products, and stakeholder engagement.

**Desirable**

- Knowledge of the sectors in which Oxfam works in Syria (Gender – WASH – Protection – FES)
- Experience working as part of the humanitarian response in Syria would be advantageous.
- Experience conducting socio-economic, inequality, poverty, or economic justice research and analysis in humanitarian or development contexts.

Safer recruitment: All offers of employment are subject to satisfactory references and appropriate screening checks (which can include counterterrorism, safeguarding and criminal records checks).

jobs.title: ILO External Collaboration Contract
jobs.description:
Terms of Reference
I. Background and purpose
The ‘PROSPECTS’ Partnership for improving prospects for host communities (HCs) and forcibly displaced persons (FDPs), was launched by the Government of the Netherlands in 2019 in response to forced displacement crises, bringing together the International Finance Corporation (IFC), the International Labour Organization (ILO), the UN Refugee Agency (UNHCR), the UN Children's Fund (UNICEF) and the World Bank. The partnership spans eight countries affected by forced displacement, namely Egypt, Ethiopia, Iraq, Jordan, Kenya, Lebanon, Sudan, and Uganda.
It employs a holistic approach whereby each partner focuses on their area of expertise to collaboratively enhance access to education, protection schemes, decent jobs and critical infrastructure for both FDPs and HCs. As of 2024, the partnership entered its Phase II, which that aims to build on the results and draw on the lessons learned from Phase I and maximize impact.
In Iraq, the PROSPECTS partnership aims to support national efforts to strengthen systems and develop/implement policies that promote inclusion and socio-economic development of forcibly displaced and host communities, whilst working closely with local authorities, business/private sector, and communities to identify, maximize, and realize opportunities on the ground. With a geographic focus on the Kurdistan Region and Ninawa, the partnership focuses on four pillars, namely: education and learning; economic inclusion and protection; and critical infrastructure.
Within the framework of the Education and Learning, the ILO’s focus is on supporting thousands of forcibly displaced persons and host community members to access more and better livelihoods and decent job opportunities. It is doing so through an integrated approach that support market-driven skills training; improve public employment services; implement labour intensive infrastructure projects; promote financial inclusion; and support business start-ups and micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs).
Through the PROSPECTS partnership in Iraq, the ILO and partners aim to leverage their comparative advantages and areas of expertise to program complementary and interdependent interventions that address education, employment, and protection challenges that negatively affect the livelihoods and well-being of host communities and forcibly displaced persons. The combined efforts of the organizations will endeavour to bolster the medium- and longer-term development goals for host communities and forcibly displaced persons to access quality and market-relevant education, and decent work and enterprise opportunities.
The partnership’s multi-agency and multidisciplined nature entail multiple levels of monitoring and evaluation to tracer its intended outcomes. Over the first year of the partnership, the ILO has invested in a robust monitoring and evaluation framework for operations in the Arab States. The framework relies on routine data collection with implementing partners, as well as a tracer study. Together these provide measures of progress against key indicators and short-term and medium-term outcomes. The current study provides a baseline analysis of ILO PROSPECTS beneficiaries’ progress towards key outcomes using the tracer study methodology.

Tracer studies1 get their name from the primary activity involved, which is to trace, find or locate a group of beneficiaries of the programme in Iraq. Tracer studies are sometimes referred to as follow-up studies because they trace individuals sometimes after an event has taken place and follow up on what has happened in their lives since then. Tracer study is an impact assessment approach and a survey methodology is developed by the ILO for assessing the PROSPECTS’ interventions in Iraq. The real challenge for the PROSPECTS programme is to produce lasting, long-term results in the lives of vulnerable hosts and forcibly displaced communities. This will be the ultimate measure of the success of PROSPECTS’ intervention. And because of this, the main reason for this tracer is to:
1\. To provide information on key performance indicators of the PROSPECTS partnership, that will help evaluate the impact of programme interventions on the learning and employment outcomes of the project’s target population.
2\. Able to weave a story of significant change in the lives and livelihoods of the beneficiaries of the PROSPECTS programme in Iraq
3\. Able to identify enabling and constraining factors to achieve more success for the PROSPECTS programme.
4\. Contribute to the betterment of PROSPECTS interventions in other parts of the country and other parts of the world.
The frequency of application of the tracer study to the same group of sampled beneficiaries will last until the end of the project. The tracer will be done in at least three rounds over the course of the programme providing a baseline, midline, and end-line estimates of the programme impact.
In 2027, The first-round data collection started with a number of sample telephone numbers selected from the sampling frame constructed from ILO database. This sample selected randomly among allocation across gender and nationality, aims to gather information on key performance indicators, enabling the evaluation of the program's impact on education, employment, and protection outcomes for the target population.

II. Scope of work
The assignment will focus on data collection for the first round of the ILO PROSPECT Iraq tracer study. The data will be collected through phone interviews with ILO PROSPECTS Iraq beneficiaries in Kurdish and Arabic, using a pre-defined survey.
The survey tool responds to short- and medium-term outcome indicators defined in the ILO PROSPECTS logical framework and corresponding data collection sheet. An orientation and training on the survey tool and data collection methodology will be arranged by the ILO PROSPECTS team at the outset of the assignment.
The survey was designed to be completed in 45 minutes. Experience conducting similar surveys in ILO PROSPECTS Jordan and Lebanon indicates that a survey tool with about 50 questions is appropriate for capturing the initial impacts of PROSPECTS programming.
The assignment will use smartphones/tablets for data collection and the Kobo toolbox2, which is an open-source suite of tools, compatible with Android and IOS.3
A random sample of refugee, and host community beneficiaries will be selected from different ILO PROSPECTS interventions. These consist of employment and access to finance services, and skills

1 Source: ILO tracer study manual Book 1 http://www.ilo.org/ipecinfo/product/download.do?type=document&id=19155
2 Kobo Toolbox | Data Collection Tools for Challenging Environments
3 Android devices are preferred, although IOS can be used if there is stable and uninterrupted internet connectivity training programmes. Total number of sample will be 1000 beneficiaries

III. Detailed tasks
The methods and processes for carrying out the data collection, entry, and validation, are detailed below:
Preparation for Field Work
1\. Induction and training on survey tools by ILO (remotely).
2\. Revise the Survey language.
3\. Pre-testing and adjustment of questionnaires, with clearance of changes from the ILO.

Data Collection
1\. Data collection and validation using phone calls with project beneficiaries and implementing partners. The contact details for the assigned sample will be shared at the outset of the assignment.
2\. Consistency checks of the questionnaire to ensure that questionnaires are fully consistent and complete.
3\. Obtain further information for incomplete entries.
4\. Enter data from source documents into a prescribed computer database, files, and forms (mostly by using Kobo/Excel Collect and/or Google Forms and similar kinds of Data Collection tools)
5\. Data entry using the relevant platform and associated tools (tablets, mobile applications etc.) The ILO will detail these prior to the start of the contract.

IV. Expected deliverables
Conduct 1000 phone calls, verified by the ILO M&E Officer. The assignment will be done in four rounds, and each round 250 phone calls.
The main deliverable shall be verified excel sheet with all phone calls conducted for each round.

V. Reporting arrangements
The external collaborators will perform the assignment under the overall supervision of the PROSPECTS Project Manager in Iraq and will report directly to the PROSPECTS Regional Monitoring and Evaluation Officer.

VI. Detailed qualifications, experience and skills required
• Education: An university degree in a related field, such as computer science or statistics or engineering.
• Experience in data entry, using applications and software such as Kobo, excel, and access.
• Exposure to work on livelihoods, employment decent work, entrepreneurship, and infrastructure would be an advantage
• Excellent speak and write level in Arabic, Kurdish, and English.
• Excellent attention to detail
• Ability to work independently and meet deadlines
• Proven excellent reporting, communication, and documentation in both English and Arabic languages.

2\. Consistency checks of the questionnaire to ensure that questionnaires are fully consistent and complete.
3\. Obtain further information for incomplete entries.
4\. Enter data from source documents into a prescribed computer database, files, and forms (mostly by using Kobo/Excel Collect and/or Google Forms and similar kinds of Data Collection tools)
5\. Data entry using the relevant platform and associated tools (tablets, mobile applications etc.) The ILO will detail these prior to the start of the contract.

IV. Expected deliverables
Conduct 1000 phone calls, verified by the ILO M&E Officer. The assignment will be done in four rounds, and each round 250 phone calls.
The main deliverable shall be verified excel sheet with all phone calls conducted for each round.

V. Reporting arrangements
The external collaborators will perform the assignment under the overall supervision of the PROSPECTS Project Manager in Iraq and will report directly to the PROSPECTS Regional Monitoring and Evaluation Officer.

VI. Detailed qualifications, experience and skills required
• Education: An university degree in a related field, such as computer science or statistics or engineering.
• Experience in data entry, using applications and software such as Kobo, excel, and access.
• Exposure to work on livelihoods, employment decent work, entrepreneurship, and infrastructure would be an advantage
• Excellent speak and write level in Arabic, Kurdish, and English.
• Excellent attention to detail
• Ability to work independently and meet deadlines
• Proven excellent reporting, communication, and documentation in both English and Arabic languages.

**Dünya Doktorları Derneği**

**Medecins du Monde Turkey (MDM-T) /** **Dünya Doktorları Dernegi (DDD)** is a Turkish based humanitarian non-governmental organisation that facilitates access to healthcare for populations affected by armed conflict, violence, natural disasters, disease, famine, poverty and exclusion.

Our organization collaborates with partners and key stakeholders to implement projects that facilitate access to primary and secondary-level healthcare services to respond to the medical needs of displaced population.

DDD is the 16th member of the Doctors of the World International Network that is committed to meeting the health needs of vulnerable people globally.

Please visit [www.dunyadoktorlari.org.tr](http://www.dunyadoktorlari.org.tr) to learn more.

**Organisation:**

DDD (MdM Türkiye)

**Duty Station:**

Istanbul, Türkiye

**Contract Duration:**

Full-time (duration to be confirmed)

**Reporting to:**

Istanbul Office Manager

**About the role**

DDD is recruiting a Human Resources Officer to manage day-to-day HR administration and support the effective implementation of HR processes at its Istanbul headquarters and across its domestic operations in Türkiye. The role covers personnel administration, recruitment support, payroll preparation, HR compliance and the implementation of DDD’s HR policies, contributing to reliable, consistent and compliant HR practices. We are looking for a hands-on HR professional with solid knowledge of Turkish labour legislation. Previous NGO or humanitarian experience is not required; candidates from the private sector or other structured institutional environments are equally encouraged to apply.

**Key responsibilities**

- **Personnel administration:** Maintain personnel files, employment contracts, amendments and HR databases; manage onboarding and offboarding; monitor leave, attendance and absences; handle social security registrations and prepare employment certificates and HR correspondence.
- **Recruitment and staffing:** Coordinate recruitment from vacancy announcement and screening to interviews, offers and contracts; support managers with job descriptions; maintain recruitment records and support workforce planning.
- **Payroll and compliance:** Prepare and verify monthly payroll inputs with Finance and external providers; monitor compliance with Turkish labour and social security legislation; follow up work permits for international staff where applicable; escalate issues for management or legal review.
- **HR policies and systems:** Implement DDD’s HR policies and procedures; improve HR processes, templates and tracking tools; prepare periodic HR reports; support performance appraisals; handle sensitive personnel information confidentially.
- **Staff support and capacity development:** Act as the point of contact for staff and managers on employment conditions, leave and HR procedures; coordinate induction and training; transfer HR knowledge to designated administrative staff to strengthen continuity.
- **Coordination:** Work with Finance, Office Management and operational teams; support management in implementing staffing decisions; ensure consistent HR practice across headquarters and domestic operations; liaise with external HR providers, legal advisers and administrative institutions.

**Required profile**

- University degree in Human Resources Management, Business Administration, Labour Relations or a related field.
- Minimum 3 years of relevant professional experience in HR administration or generalist HR functions, in the private sector, a nonprofit organisation or another structured institutional environment.
- Good practical knowledge of Turkish labour law, social security procedures and payroll administration.
- Experience in personnel administration, recruitment and payroll preparation.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel.
- Accuracy, discretion and attention to detail; ability to prioritise multiple tasks and to work independently while coordinating with different departments.
- Commitment to professional ethics, confidentiality and accountability.
- Turkish: fluent (required). English: good professional working proficiency, written and spoken (required).

**What we value**

We are particularly interested in candidates who demonstrate practical HR experience, reliability, autonomy and a service-oriented approach, and who can apply HR procedures consistently across the organisation.

**Compliance & Ethics**
Promote and encourage a culture of compliance and ethics throughout Dünya Doktorları Derneği. As applicable to the position, maintains a clear understanding of Dünya Doktorları Derneği and donor compliance and ethics standards and adheres to those standards. Conducts work with the highest level of integrity. Communicates these values to staff and to partners and requires them to adhere to these values.

**Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse**
Actively promote PSEA (Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse) standards within Dünya Doktorları Derneği and amongst beneficiaries served by Dünya Doktorları Derneği.

**NB:** Considering the purpose and values of the organisation, DDD requests to its employee complete flexibility in term of duties and commitment, as their job description and job title can be adjusted throughout the year according to needs and priorities.

Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. Please be advised that female candidates are highly encouraged.

*Dünya Doktorları Derneği is an equal opportunity employer whereby we ensure all hiring and employment decisions, and operates all programs, services, and functions without the practices that discriminate against any person employed or seeking employment based on race, colour, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national or ethnic origin, age, marital status, disability, genetic information or any other status or characteristic protected under applicable law.*

**Closure Date:30.11.2026**

Due to the urgency to fill this post, DDD reserves the right to review the CVs on a rolling basis and selected candidates may be interviewed prior to the closing dates listed, therefore early applications are encouraged.
DDD is not in a position to respond to every applicant individually due to the anticipated high number of applications.
Please note that only short-listed candidates will be contacted for the first interview.

Any offer made to the candidate in relation to this vacancy notice is subject to funding confirmation.

**General Information**
DDD retains the discretion to re-advertise the vacancy, to cancel the recruitment, to offer a contract with a modified job description or for a different duration, or to offer a contract at a lower grade.

Working closely with senior leaders, government representatives, academics, international partners and the wider Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement, you will build influential relationships, shape strategic priorities and ensure that IHL and humanitarian principles remain at the heart of decision-making.

jobs.title: Knowledge Translation Consultant
jobs.description:
## **1. Background**

Foundations is a multi-country initiative funded by Global Affairs Canada and implemented by Save the Children Canada in partnership with Save the Children International (Mali, Niger, Sierra Leone), the International Rescue Committee (IRC), Equipop, ODI and SickKids. The project focuses on empowering marginalized adolescent girls and advancing gender equality and adolescents’ sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR).

Foundations project works to transform harmful gender norms and improve adolescents’ access to SRHR information and services through a combination of education, community engagement, health system strengthening, and advocacy. Research and evidence generation are core components of the project and are used to inform programming and influence broader policy and social change efforts.

The project has supported research initiatives in the three West African countries. These studies have generated evidence on barriers, opportunities, and effective strategies to improve SRHR outcomes for adolescents, particularly girls. To maximize the impact of this research, Foundations project seeks to transform the evidence into accessible, actionable, and audience‑appropriate knowledge products that can be used for:

- Advocacy with policymakers and government actors
- Program design and adaptation by country teams
- Community engagement activities
- Feminist and women’s rights organizations’ advocacy efforts
- Webinars, events, and dissemination platforms
- Youth-friendly and adolescent-accessible formats

To support this work, the project is looking to recruit a bilingual Knowledge Translation (KT) Consultant who will lead the synthesis, translation, and packaging of evidence into compelling and usable communication products for diverse audiences.

Research reports to be reviewed:

- 8 research reports

Products to be developed:

- 2 communication products in French for Mali Country Office
- 2 communication products in French for Niger Country Office
- 2 communication products in English for SIerra Leone Country Office

## **2. Purpose of the Consultancy**

The purpose of this consultancy is to translate ASRHR research findings from the three country offices into a suite of high-quality knowledge translation products, tailored to different advocacy, community, and policy audiences. All knowledge products must be produced in the appropriate language for each country context, which may be either French or English, depending on the predominant language used in the target location.

The consultant will develop these products in close collaboration with country teams including Women and Girls Rights Organizations and will coordinate and contract a graphic designer familiar with SCC’s work (contact to be shared at a later stage), ensuring polished, visually appealing, and culturally relevant materials.

## **3. Objectives**

1. Review the 8 research reports and synthesize the complex research findings into clear, actionable messages for policymakers, communities, feminists, and youth audiences.
2. Produce a set of country-specific knowledge translation materials for the 3 countries (2 products per country) informed by consultations with local teams and partners.
3. Ensure all materials are designed and finalized through collaboration with a graphic designer hired by the consultant.

## **4. Scope of Work & Key Tasks**

The consultant will be responsible for the following tasks:

### **4.1 Inception Phase**

- Conduct an inception call with the Foundation’s project team.
- Review the research reports
- Hold a call with each of the 3 country offices
- Identify 2 products with each country based on country-specific needs and communication/advocacy priorities (audience, content of material, type of communication and advocacy products, etc...).
- Clarify messaging, target audiences, tone, formatting, and context.
- Develop a brief Inception Report including:
- Proposed KT approach
- Tentative list of products
- Timeline and workplan

### **4.2 Development of Knowledge Translation Products**

Products may include (to be finalized with country teams):

- **Policy briefs**
- **Short lay summaries**
- **Advocacy briefs for feminist and women’s rights organizations**
- **Community-friendly materials** (e.g., posters, info sheets)
- **Adolescent-friendly content**, such as:
- Comic-style educational materials
- Illustrated stories
- Youth-accessible summaries
- **Presentations** for:
- Policymaker engagement
- Community share-back sessions
- Webinars and global events

### **4.3 Design and Production**

- Coordinate with a graphic designer (contact to be shared by SCC at a later stage) who would be hired and paid directly by the consultant.
- Provide the designer with finalized content.
- Oversee layout, illustrations, translation (if needed), and branding compliance.
- Integrate feedback from project teams and obtain final clearance on content and design

**4.4 Finalization & Submission**

- Submit all final products in required formats (PDF, editable files, design packages).
- Prepare a short summary note on KT process followed and lessons learned during the process.

## **5. Expected Deliverables**

The consultant will deliver:

1. **Inception Report** with detailed workplan
2. **Set of 6 KT products** (exact type to be agreed during inception phase),
3. **Designed and polished versions** of all products (print and digital)
4. **A brief final report** summarizing the work completed

All deliverables must be submitted within 2–3 months of the start of the consultancy.

## **6. Timeframe and Level of Effort**

- Total consultancy days: **30 working days**
- Implementation period: **2–3 months** from contract signature
- Work will be conducted remotely, with virtual meetings with the Foundations project teams

## **7. Required Qualifications**

The consultant must have:

- Advanced degree in public health, SRHR, social sciences, communications, or a related field
- Demonstrated experience in knowledge translation, research communication, or evidence synthesis
- Strong background in SRHR advocacy, gender equality, and feminist approaches
- Excellent writing, editing, and storytelling skills
- Experience working or familiarity with international development or feminist organizations in West Africa (an asset)
- Language requirements:
- Fluency in English (spoken and written)
- Fluency in French (spoken and written)

## **8. Payment Terms**

Payment schedule may be structured as:

- 30% upon approval of Inception Report
- 30% upon submission of drafts of all KT materials
- 40% upon delivery of all final approved outputs

The consultant is responsible for contracting and covering fees for the graphic designer within this budget.

## **9. Application Requirements**

Interested applicants should submit:

- CV
- A brief statement confirming fluency in both English and French
- Short proposal (max 2 pages) outlining:
- Understanding of the assignment
- Proposed approach
- Proposed timeline
- Financial proposal inclusive of design costs
- Samples of work – i.e. presentations, briefs, posters, info-sheets, etc.

Applicants must disclose any actual, potential, or perceived conflict of interest that could affect the impartial performance of the assignment.

Save the Children Canada is committed to equitable and inclusive procurement practices. We encourage applications from qualified consultants and firms of diverse backgrounds, including women-led organizations, local and regional suppliers, and suppliers from historically underrepresented groups.

## **10. Other requirements**

The successful consultant or consultant team will be required to comply with all applicable Save the Children policies and donor requirements

Save the Children reserves the right to conduct due diligence, including reference checks and screening against applicable anti-terrorism and sanctions lists, prior to contract award.

**Consultant.e en transfert des connaissances pour les résultats d’une étude multinationale sur la santé et les droits sexuels et reproductifs (SDSR)**

## Cahier des charges (CC)

### **1. Contexte**

« FOUNDATIONS » est une initiative multinationale financée par Affaires mondiales Canada (AMC) et mise en œuvre par Save the Children Canada en partenariat avec Save the Children International (Mali, Niger, Sierra Leone), l’International Rescue Committee (IRC), Equipop, l’ODI et SickKids. Le projet vise à autonomiser les adolescentes marginalisées et à promouvoir l’égalité de genre ainsi que la santé et les droits sexuels et reproductifs (SDSR) des adolescents.

Le projet FOUNDATIONS vise à transformer les normes de genre néfastes et à améliorer l’accès des adolescentes aux informations et aux services en matière de SDSR grâce à une approche combinant éducation, engagement communautaire, renforcement des systèmes de santé et plaidoyer. La recherche et la production de données factuelles constituent des éléments centraux du projet ; elles servent à orienter la mise en œuvre des programmes et à influencer les efforts plus larges en matière de politiques et de changement social.

Le projet a soutenu des initiatives de recherche dans ces trois pays d’Afrique de l’Ouest. Ces études ont permis de recueillir des données factuelles sur les obstacles, les opportunités et les stratégies efficaces pour améliorer les résultats en matière de SDSR chez les adolescents, en particulier les filles. Afin de maximiser l’impact de ces recherches, le projet « FOUNDATIONS » cherche à transformer ces données factuelles en produits de connaissance accessibles, exploitables et adaptés au public visé, pouvant être utilisés pour :

- Le plaidoyer auprès des décideurs politiques et des acteurs gouvernementaux
- Concevoir et adapter des programmes par les équipes nationales
- Des activités d’engagement communautaire
- Les efforts de plaidoyer des organisations féministes et de défense des droits des femmes
- Des webinaires, des événements et des plateformes de diffusion
- Formats adaptés aux jeunes et accessibles aux adolescents

Pour soutenir ce travail, le projet cherche à recruter un.e consultant.e bilingue en transfert des connaissances (TC) qui sera chargé de la synthèse, de la traduction et de la mise en forme des données probantes afin d’en faire des supports de communication convaincants et exploitables destinés à divers publics.

Rapports de recherche à examiner :

- 8 rapports de recherche

Produits à développer :

- 2 supports de communication en français pour le bureau national du Mali
- 2 supports de communication en français pour le bureau national du Niger
- 2 supports de communication en anglais pour le bureau de Sierra Leone

### **2. Objectif de la mission de conseil**

L’objectif de cette mission de conseil est de traduire les résultats des recherches de SDSR des adolescents menées par les trois bureaux nationaux en une série de produits de transfert de connaissances de haute qualité, adaptés à différents publics : acteurs du plaidoyer, communautés et décideurs politiques. Tous les produits de transfert de connaissances doivent être rédigés dans la langue appropriée au contexte de chaque pays, à savoir le français ou l’anglais, en fonction de la langue principalement utilisée dans la région cible.

La.le consultant.e élaborera ces supports en étroite collaboration avec les équipes nationales, notamment les organisations de défense des droits des femmes et des filles, et se chargera de coordonner et de recruter un graphiste familiarisé avec le travail du SCC (coordonnées à communiquer ultérieurement), afin de garantir des supports soignés, visuellement attrayants et adaptés au contexte culturel.

### **3. Objectifs**

1. Examiner les 8 rapports de recherche et synthétiser les résultats complexes de ces recherches en messages clairs et exploitables à l’intention des décideurs politiques, des communautés, des féministes et des jeunes.
2. Produire un ensemble de supports de diffusion des connaissances spécifiques à chacun des trois pays (deux supports par pays), élaborés à partir des consultations menées avec les équipes et les partenaires locaux.
3. Veiller à ce que tous les supports soient conçus et finalisés en collaboration avec un graphiste engagé par la.le consultant.e.

### **4. Portée des travaux et tâches principales**

La.le consultant.e sera chargé des tâches suivantes :

#### **4.1 Phase de lancement**

- Organiser une réunion de lancement avec l’équipe de projet de la Fondation.
- Examiner les rapports de recherche
- Organiser une visioconférence avec chacun des trois bureaux nationaux
- Identifier deux produits avec chaque pays en fonction des besoins spécifiques à celui-ci et des priorités en matière de communication et de plaidoyer (public cible, contenu des supports, type de produits de communication et de plaidoyer, etc.).
- Précisez le message, les publics cibles, le ton, la mise en forme et le contexte.
- Élaborer un bref rapport initial comprenant :
- L'approche proposée en matière de transfert de connaissances
- Liste provisoire des produits
- Calendrier et plan de travail

#### **4.2 Élaboration des produits de transfert des connaissances**

Les produits peuvent inclure (à finaliser avec les équipes nationales) :

- **Notes d’orientation**
- **Résumés simplifiés destinés au grand public**
- **Notices de plaidoyer destinées aux organisations féministes et de défense des droits des femmes**
- **Supports adaptés aux communautés** (par exemple, affiches, fiches d’information)
- **Contenus adaptés aux adolescents**, tels que :
- Des supports pédagogiques sous forme de bandes dessinées
- Histoires illustrées
- Des résumés accessibles aux jeunes
- **Des présentations** destinées à:
- L'implication des décideurs politiques
- Séances de partage avec la communauté
- Webinaires et événements internationaux

#### **4.3 Conception et production**

- Coordonner avec un graphiste (dont les coordonnées seront communiquées ultérieurement par le SCC) qui sera engagé et rémunéré directement par la.le consultant.e.
- Fournir au graphiste le contenu finalisé.
- Superviser la mise en page, les illustrations, la traduction (si nécessaire) et le respect de l’identité visuelle.
- Intégrer les commentaires des équipes de projet et obtenir le feu vert définitif concernant le contenu et la conception

**4.4 Finalisation et remise**

- Soumettre tous les produits finaux dans les formats requis (PDF, fichiers modifiables, dossiers de conception).
- Rédiger une brève note de synthèse sur le processus de transfert de connaissances suivi et les enseignements tirés au cours du processus.

### **5. Livrables attendus**

La.le consultant.e devra fournir :

1. **Un rapport de lancement** accompagné d’un plan de travail détaillé
2. **Un ensemble de 6 produits de transfert de connaissances** (dont la nature exacte sera convenue lors de la phase de lancement),
3. **des versions finalisées et peaufinées** de tous les produits (au format papier et numérique)
4. **Un bref rapport final** résumant les travaux réalisés

Tous les livrables doivent être remis dans un délai de 2 à 3 mois à compter du début de la mission de conseil.

### **6. Calendrier et charge de travail**

- Nombre total de jours de mission : **30 jours ouvrés**
- Période de mise en œuvre : **2 à 3 mois** à compter de la signature du contrat
- Le travail sera effectué à distance, avec des réunions virtuelles avec les équipes de projet de FOUNDATIONS

### **7. Qualifications requises**

La.le consultant.e doit posséder :

- Un diplôme de niveau supérieur en santé publique, en santé et droits sexuels et reproductifs (SDSR), en sciences sociales, en communication ou dans un domaine connexe
- Une expérience avérée en transfert des connaissances, en communication de la recherche ou en synthèse des données probantes
- Une solide expérience en matière de défense des droits sexuels et reproductifs, d’égalité de genre et d’approches féministes
- D'excellentes compétences en rédaction, en révision et en narration
- Une expérience professionnelle ou une bonne connaissance des organisations de développement international ou féministes en Afrique de l’Ouest (un atout)
- Exigences linguistiques :
- Maîtrise de l'anglais (à l'oral et à l'écrit)
- Maîtrise du français (à l'oral et à l'écrit)

### **8. Conditions de paiement**

Le calendrier de paiement peut être structuré comme suit :

- 30 % à la validation du rapport de lancement
- 30 % à la remise des ébauches de tous les supports de transfert de connaissances
- 40 % à la livraison de tous les livrables finaux approuvés

La.le consultant.e est chargé de passer contrat avec le graphiste et de prendre en charge ses honoraires dans la limite de ce budget.

### **9. Conditions de candidature**

Les candidats intéressés doivent soumettre :

- un CV
- Une brève déclaration attestant de leur maîtrise de l’anglais et du français
- Une brève proposition (2 pages maximum) présentant :
- La compréhension de la mission
- Approche proposée
- Calendrier proposé
- Proposition financière incluant les coûts de conception
- Exemples de travaux – c'est-à-dire présentations, dossiers de synthèse, affiches, fiches d'information, etc.

Les candidats doivent signaler tout conflit d’intérêts réel, potentiel ou perçu susceptible d’affecter l’impartialité de la mission.

Save the Children Canada s'engage à respecter des pratiques d'approvisionnement équitables et inclusives. Nous encourageons les candidatures de consultant.e.s et de cabinets qualifiés issus de divers horizons, notamment les organisations dirigées par des femmes, les fournisseurs locaux et régionaux, ainsi que les fournisseurs issus de groupes historiquement sous-représentés.

### **10. Autres exigences**

La.le consultant.e ou l’équipe de consultants retenu(e) devra se conformer à l’ensemble des politiques applicables de Save the Children et aux exigences des bailleurs de fonds.

Save the Children se réserve le droit de mener une vérification préalable, y compris la vérification des références et le recoupement avec les listes antiterroristes et de sanctions applicables, avant l’attribution du contrat.

jobs.title: Shelter and WASH Specialist Lebanon
jobs.description:
**What we are looking for**

We're looking for an experienced **Shelter & WASH Specialist** to drive the technical vision and quality of our Shelter and WASH programmes in Lebanon. If you're a strategic humanitarian professional with strong technical expertise, leadership skills, and a passion for delivering innovative, people-centred solutions, this is your opportunity to shape impactful programming in a complex and evolving context.

You'll play a pivotal role in delivering high-quality humanitarian programmes that strengthen resilience, improve living conditions, and support vulnerable communities across Lebanon while leading a talented team of technical professionals.

Ready to drive lasting impact through Shelter and WASH programming? Apply today.

**What you will do**

- Lead the design, strategy, and technical quality of Shelter and WASH programmes across Lebanon.
- Provide technical guidance and capacity building to country and area office teams.
- Drive assessments, programme adaptation, learning, and evidence-based decision-making.
- Lead technical inputs for proposals, donor engagement, reporting, and programme growth.
- Strengthen partnerships with municipalities, government authorities, donors, UN agencies, and sector actors.
- Promote innovation, emergency preparedness, climate resilience, and market-based approaches.
- Represent NRC in relevant fora, working groups, and technical and sectorial coordination platforms.
- Champion safe, inclusive, and integrated programming across all interventions.

**What you will bring**

- Degree in Civil, Water, Environmental or Sanitary Engineering, Architecture, or a related field.
- Minimum 7 years' experience in Shelter and/or WASH programming, including 5 years in humanitarian settings, or related technical fields with at least 2 years in a technical advisor or specialist position.
- Experience across at least 3 contexts is highly preferred including Ukraine, and the middle east.
- Experience in technical leadership, programme design, quality assurance, and team capacity strengthening.
- Solid experience with project cycle management (PCM) and in project development; including ability to lead on assessments, design; with good skills in proposal writing/reporting.
- Strong understanding of emergency response, early recovery, cash-based programming, and market systems.
- Proven experience working with local authorities, ministries, donors, and coordination platforms.
- Excellent analytical, communication, and stakeholder engagement skills.
- Fluency in English; Arabic is an advantage.
- Experience in Lebanon, the Middle East, or similar humanitarian contexts is highly desirable.

Context related skills, knowledge and experience

- Understanding of the Lebanon context or similar contexts
- Experience in designing and implementing programming in both first line emergency response, and early recovery contexts, with a focus on household and community level infrastructure interventions.
- Technical knowledge and experience of the community engagement process in a humanitarian and early recovery contexts
- Understanding of Environment and Social Safeguarding is highly desirable.
- Skills in market analysis, sectorial cash-based interventions, and market-based programmes is required
- Experience supporting partner-led or localisation models.

Please download [the detailed job description](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:w:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQC2WZXieu4bQ7WzI5YAZdbIAUs0lNe9mdSFpJc8Zq0tMwM?e=9hIYoF) to learn more about the position.

**What we offer**

- Duty station: Beirut, Lebanon
- Fixed term contract: 12 months national contract, renewable based on performance, funding and need for the position
- Travel: 40%
- Salary/benefits: Grade 9 on NRC's grading structure.
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.

[Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

Important information about the application process

- We invite applications from qualified candidates matching the profile.
- Please ensure you attach copies of your academic and professional certificates.
- To apply as an internal candidate, log in with your official email address or click on Opportunity Marketplace.
- When creating your profile, include your full name as given on your passport. Complete all the system-required fields for experience, employment history and education.
- Submit your application and CV in English, taking care to attach your latest CV.
- Applications that do not meet the minimum standards in terms of experience or qualifications will generally not be considered. Unsolicited applications not related to this specific job advertisement will not be considered.
- Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. We receive many applicants for each vacant position.

**Why NRC?**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 15,000 staff work in crises across 40 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year.

[Watch this short video](https://vimeo.com/736782633) to see NRC in action.

We are looking for people who are passionate about helping refugees and people forced to flee. Are you one of those people? If you are, NRC offers you the opportunity to:

- do demanding and professional work, often in challenging contexts
- join a work culture that empowers every employee to share ideas and take responsibility
- be part of a welcoming and supportive community committed to human dignity

[Learn more about NRC](https://www.nrc.no/)

[Learn more about NRC Lebanon](https://www.nrc.no/countries/middle-east/lebanon)

jobs.title: Grants and Reporting Manager
jobs.description:
INTERSOS is an independent humanitarian organisation that assists the victims of natural disasters, armed conflicts and exclusion. Its activities are based on the principles of solidarity, justice, human dignity, equality of rights and opportunities, respect for diversity and coexistence, paying special attention to the most vulnerable people.

## **TERMS OF REFERENCE**

- **Job Title:** Grants and Reporting Manager
- **Code:** SR-34-10347
- **Duty station:** Beirut, Lebanon (with visits to field locations)
- **Starting date:** 01/02/2027
- **Contract duration:** 11 months
- **Reporting to:** Head of Programme (HoP)
- **Type of Duty Station:** Non-family duty station

## **GENERAL DESCRIPTION OF THE CONTEXT**

INTERSOS is an international non-profit humanitarian organization founded in 1992. INTERSOS works towards a world of equality, justice, peace, and solidarity. To achieve this, INTERSOS supports people in living with dignity and safety, alleviating suffering and responding to the needs of populations affected by crises, extreme poverty, disasters, and conflict.

INTERSOS began working in Lebanon in 2006 to support populations affected by the Lebanese-Israeli war. Since 2013, it has been assisting vulnerable populations impacted by the Syrian crisis, including Syrian refugees and Lebanese host communities, delivering protection, shelter, WASH, and education assistance. Currently, INTERSOS is responding to the ongoing escalation of hostilities with Israel through emergency protection, shelter, and WASH interventions, while continuing its regular programming. INTERSOS operates from three main bases—South (Tyre), Bekaa (Zahle), and Beirut and Mount Lebanon (Beirut) —as well as a shared office in the North, covering all governorates in Lebanon

## **GENERAL PURPOSE OF THE POSITION**

In coordination with the SMT, MEAL, Head of Bases/Programme Managers, Project Managers and Technical Coordinators, timely support the design and development of new project proposals, high-quality reporting, and regular grants management activities in line with INTERSOS' programmatic goals, objectives and indicators, and respecting donor requirements.

## **MAIN RESPONSIBILITIES AND TASKS**

**Project/Programme Design and Development**

- Support the Head of Programme on the drafting and updating of the donor mapping and donor strategies
- Support the Go/No-go process through the analysis of calls for proposals and their relevant elements
- In coordination with the SMT, Heads of Bases/Programme Managers, Technical Coordinators, Project Managers and MEAL, support the design and development of new project proposals, ensuring that those are structured according to INTERSOS' programatic goals and objectives, and in line with donor templates and requirements
- Regularly update Mission Work Plan document ensuring internal and external deadlines are respected and promptly communicated to relevant colleagues
- Regularly and ad hoc liaise with the Regional Office, specifically with the Regional Programme and Grants Manager, to ensure project design meets donor guidelines and submission process respects the defined workflow
- Under the guidance of the Head of Programme lead the internal coordination of the proposal writing process, ensuring clear division of roles and responsibilities, engagement of relevant departments, and adherence to the agreed timeline
- Ensure the matching and consistency of the information and budget figures across proposal documents, including financial components
- Ensure the final submission package is complete, consistent, and compliant with donor requirements
- Promptly flag any challenge or delays to relevant colleagues at mission and regional level

**Quality Reporting**

- Under the supervision of the Head of Programme, promote periodic revision and harmonisation of templates and formats used for monitoring, follow-up, and reporting of activities in coordination with Heads of Bases/Programme Managers, Project Managers and Technical Coordinators
- Liaise with HQ Grants and Compliance Unit and Regional Office to receive and keep abreast of donor templates and guidelines
- Regularly update Mission Work Plan document (Reporting Tracker) ensuring internal and external deadlines are followed as per Grant Agreements and promptly communicated to relevant colleagues at mission and regional level
- Under the supervision of the Head of Programme and in coordination with the Regional Office and HQ Grants and Compliance Unit, ensure the compilation, review, and submission of timely, compliant and consistent reports in line with INTERSOS and donor requirements
- Ensure matching and consistency of information and budget figures across reporting documents (including programme, finance and logistics components)
- Ensure correct storage of Reports and related annexes on INTERSOS Management Platform (IMP) and shared drive

**Grants Management and Other Responsibilities**

- Under the supervision of the Head of Programme and in coordination with the Heads of Bases/Programme Managers, Project Managers and relevant SMT members, prepare and conduct project kick-off, review and close-out meetings
- Contribute to the review and revision of grant agreements in coordination with the Head of Programme, Head of Mission, Finance Coordinator, and HQ Grants and Compliance Unit
- Lead on due diligence and capacity assessments of selected partners, support the development of partner capacity building plans together with the responsible Project Managers
- Coordinate and contribute to the review and revision of MoUs / partnership agreements and liaise with partners on reporting requirements
- Conduct, with the support of the Regional Programme and Grants Manager, information sessions (also integrated in project kick-off meetings) on main donor guidelines, involving all the relevant departments (Programme, MEAL, Finance, Logistics, HR, and HQ Grants and Compliance Unit)
- Support field monitoring of performance indicators, conducting compliance spot checks on ongoing projects and partners (e.g., local partners)
- Conduct a periodical review of project documentation, ensuring correct uploading and archiving on mission drive and IMP
- Ensure projects' amendment requests (where needed) are in line with donor guidelines and procedures
- Support the analysis of data and visualisation of programmatic outputs for monitoring and reporting purposes, and report any deviation in terms of achievements/trends to the Head of Programme and MEAL Coordinator
- Ensure the Mission Communication Plan is regularly updated; support the drafting of communication materials and social media posts, manage INTERSOS Lebanon's Facebook page, and liaise with the HQ Communication Department in coordination with the Head of Mission and Head of Programme
- Coordinate with Project Managers to collect photo and video documentation of project activities and results, ensuring compliance with donor and organisational visibility requirements in coordination with the HQ Communication Department

## **REQUIRED PROFILE AND EXPERIENCE**

### **Education**

- BA in International Affairs, Development, International Political Economy or other relevant field

### **Professional experience**

- Minimum 3 years of relevant work experience in programme or grants departments in the humanitarian sector
- Experience with grants management of institutional donors (ECHO, UNHCR, AICS, CBPF, among others) and understanding of donor requirements and compliance

### **Professional requirements**

- Capacity to work in teams with different backgrounds and expertise
- Result-oriented and attention to detail
- Analytical, communication and reporting skills
- People management and development, team player

### **Languages**

- Fluency in English, spoken and written
- Knowledge/Fluency in Italian and/or Arabic (desirable)

### **Personal requirements**

- Understanding of humanitarian principles, standards and best practices
- Commitment to INTERSOS values and principles
- Capacity to work under pressure

## **GENERAL CONDITIONS AND BENEFITS**

- **Salary range:** 09 - 3.172€ - 3.577€ monthly gross
- **Accommodation:** House allowance
- **R&R:** Rest and Recuperation (R&R) is not applicable.
- **Remuneration:** The monthly remuneration is defined, for each position, according to the standard salary grid and function grid, taking into account the experience of the selected candidate. It is communicated during the HR interview, or at any rate during the first stage of the selection process.
- **Transportation:** Round-trip flights for the humanitarian. For any mission lasting at least 9 months, an additional flight ticket to the Country of residence and return to the mission is covered by the Organisation for the humanitarian worker.
- **Medical insurance:** Injuries and death insurance; civil liability insurance; reimbursement for vaccines, medical certificate and PCR test for deployment; psychosocial support on request for the humanitarian worker.
- **Visa:** INTERSOS covers the costs and visa support for the humanitarian worker.
- **Annual Leave:** 2.5 days per month
- **Induction:** Online orientation course: each new staff member receives preparatory training before departure, adequate to provide the necessary information related to the structure of INTERSOS and the main decision-making processes and working tools, in order to facilitate entry into the Organisation.
- **Note 1:** INTERSOS applies a “Learning & Development Policy” which includes the possibility to receive capacitation and participate in internal and external training. Priority will be given to the staff working for INTERSOS for over two years.
- **Note 2:** The categorisation of Accompanied, RnR, and Unaccompanied Duty stations is subject to security criteria, access to health and education services, and is non-negotiable.
