Programme Associate (Grant Performance and Monitoring) [Open to internal and external applicants]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) is the UN’s global development network, advocating for change and connecting countries to knowledge, experience and resources to help people build a better life. We are on the ground in 170 countries and territories, working with governments and people on their own solutions to global and national development challenges to help empower lives and build resilient nations.

As a trusted, long-term partner of The Global Fund (GF), UNDP’s value proposition lies in providing an integrated package of development solutions to strengthen institutions to deliver health services. Through its contributions as interim Principal Recipient (PR) and provider of technical assistance in over 53 countries since 2003, UNDP’s provision of integrated policy, implementation and capacity development support to countries has yielded significant health and development results in challenging operating environments. Proactive risk management and investing in sustainability are the cornerstones of UNDP’s portfolio management approach and providing technical assistance to national counterparts during all phases of implementation, strengthening legislation, policies and regulatory frameworks, and building capacities across key functional areas, including programme and financial management, integrated health information systems, procurement and supply chain management.

In Zimbabwe, UNDP is the Principal Recipient (PR) for the Global Fund GC8 HIV grant and is also providing Support Services (Fund Administration) to the Ministry of Health and Childcare (MOHCC) as the continuing Global Fund PR for the Tuberculosis (TB), Malaria and Resilient and Sustainable Systems for Health (RSSH) grants. Additionally, UNDP has been designated the ‘CCM Funding Recipient’ responsible for receiving and managing CCM funding on its behalf. The HIV grant for 2027-2029 aims to contribute towards the achievement of the vision and goals of Zimbabwe National HIV Strategic Plan, 2026-2030.

UNDP Zimbabwe manages Global Fund grants through a dedicated Programme Management Unit (PMU), which provides overall programme oversight, coordination, and operational management to ensure effective, compliant, and results-driven implementation. The PMU oversees financial management, risk management, procurement and supply chain operations, monitoring and evaluation, health information systems, integrated capacity development and reporting in line with Global Fund and UNDP policies and procedures.

Working in close partnership with the Ministry of Health and Child Care (MoHCC), National AIDS Council (NAC), national disease programmes, NatPharm, MCAZ, civil society and community organizations, technical partners, donors, UN agencies, the Country Coordinating Mechanism (CCM), LFA and the Global Fund, the UNDP’s PMU strengthens national health systems and ensures the uninterrupted delivery of quality health commodities and services. This contributes to improved prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and health outcomes for HIV, tuberculosis, malaria, and broader health system resilience.

Duties and Responsibilities

Under the overall guidance of the Programme Manager and direct supervision of the Head of Programmes, the Grant Performance and Monitoring Associate will support the effective implementation, performance monitoring, coordination, and reporting of the Global Fund HIV Grant. The incumbent will serve as the focal point for integrated grant performance monitoring and management reporting, ensuring timely tracking of implementation progress across Programme, Finance, Procurement and Supply Management (PSM), Health Products Management, Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E), and Sub-Recipient (SR) performance.

The position will support evidence-based decision-making by consolidating and analysing programmatic, financial, procurement, supply chain, epidemiological, and performance data; monitoring progress against approved targets, budgets, workplans, and key performance indicators; tracking implementation bottlenecks and management actions; and producing high-quality performance dashboards, management reports, and grant implementation updates.

1. Ensures effective grant implementation monitoring support and performance management

• Monitor implementation progress against approved workplans, budgets, procurement plans, targets, milestones, and grant deliverables.

• Track grant performance across Programme, Finance, PSM, Health Products Management, M&E, and Operations functions and identify implementation bottlenecks, delays, risks, and performance gaps.

• Maintain an integrated grant implementation and performance tracking system to monitor key actions, deliverables, commitments, and management decisions.

• Follow up on implementation issues and agreed management actions and ensure timely resolution by responsible teams and stakeholders.

• Support routine programme performance reviews, implementation review meetings, and grant monitoring missions.

________________________________________

2. Ensures integrated portfolio monitoring, analysis, and reporting

• Consolidate and analyse programmatic, financial, procurement, supply chain, and M&E data to assess grant performance and implementation progress.

• Monitor expenditure trends, absorption rates, procurement status, commodity delivery performance, and implementation milestones against approved plans.

• Analyse programme performance against approved targets, indicators, workplans, and budgets and highlight areas requiring management attention.

• Conduct grant performance trend analysis and provide recommendations to accelerate implementation and improve results.

• Support development and monitoring of implementation acceleration plans and corrective actions.

________________________________________

3. Ensures strategic information management and performance analytics

• Produce monthly integrated grant performance reports summarizing programmatic, financial, procurement, supply chain, and M&E performance.

• Develop and maintain dashboards, scorecards, trackers, and management information tools for monitoring grant performance and implementation status.

• Analyse epidemiological, service delivery, and programme data to assess progress toward grant objectives and national HIV priorities.

• Track achievement of performance indicators and prepare variance analyses against approved targets and performance frameworks.

• Prepare management briefs, presentations, decision-support reports, and implementation updates for leadership and stakeholders.

________________________________________

4. Ensures effective Sub-Recipient performance monitoring and coordination

• Serve as the focal point for monitoring and tracking implementation issues, requests, and actions involving Sub-Recipients and implementing partners.

• Monitor timeliness of responses to SR requests, approvals, procurement actions, disbursements, reporting requirements, and technical support needs.

• Maintain and regularly update action trackers, issue logs, and follow-up matrices for management review.

• Coordinate collection of implementation updates, supporting documentation, and performance information from SRs and implementing partners.

• Escalate unresolved issues, implementation delays, risks, and bottlenecks to management for timely action.

________________________________________

5. Ensures support to grant management, compliance, and portfolio optimization

• Support preparation of Progress Updates and Disbursement Requests (PUDRs), donor reports, management briefs, grant reviews, and performance monitoring reports.

• Monitor implementation of grant commitments, management actions, audit recommendations, and agreed corrective measures.

• Support grant reprogramming, portfolio optimization, implementation acceleration, and performance improvement initiatives.

• Contribute to responses to audits, assurance reviews, oversight missions, and information requests from the Global Fund and other stakeholders.

• Support maintenance of grant monitoring tools and systems to strengthen accountability, compliance, and results management.

________________________________________

6. Ensures knowledge management, coordination, and stakeholder engagement

• Facilitate coordination across Programme, Finance, PSM, Health Products Management, M&E, and Operations teams to support integrated grant implementation.

• Maintain implementation monitoring tools, reporting templates, action trackers, and knowledge repositories.

• Document and disseminate lessons learned, best practices, innovations, and implementation challenges.

• Support organization of programme review meetings, performance review sessions, and stakeholder consultations.

• Promote effective information sharing and collaboration among PMU teams, Sub-Recipients, implementing partners, and stakeholders.

• Perform any other duties assigned by the Head of Programmes or Programme Manager.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organisation.

4. Institutional Arrangement

The Programme Associate (Grant Performance and Monitoring) will work under the direct supervision of the Head of Programmes and under the overall guidance of the Programme Manager within the UNDP Global Fund Programme Management Unit (PMU).

The incumbent will promote a collaborative, client-oriented, quality, and results-focused approach to programme implementation and will work closely with Sub-Recipients (SRs), government counterparts, PMU functional teams, and UNDP Country Office colleagues to ensure effective delivery of the Global Fund HIV Grant. The position requires strong cross-functional collaboration with programme, monitoring and evaluation, procurement and supply chain management, finance, and operations teams to strengthen grant performance, compliance, accountability, and achievement of programme results.

The Programme Associate (Grant Performance and Monitoring) will serve as the primary focal point for HIV programme implementation and performance management and will maintain close working relationships with SRs, the Ministry of Health and Child Care (MoHCC), the National AIDS Council (NAC), communities, and other key stakeholders. To strengthen implementation support and accelerate programme delivery, the incumbent is expected to dedicate approximately 50% of their time to direct engagement with SRs and implementing partners, including regular field missions and on-site support. This engagement will focus on identifying and resolving implementation bottlenecks, improving grant absorption, strengthening risk management and compliance, enhancing programme performance, and supporting the sustainability of HIV programme interventions

Achieve Results: Level 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to detail, and delivers quality outputs within established deadlines.

Think Innovatively: Level 1: Demonstrates openness to new ideas and seeks practical improvements in monitoring, reporting, and performance management systems.

Learn Continuously: Level 1: Actively seeks learning opportunities, shares knowledge, and applies lessons learned to improve performance.

Adapt with Agility: Level 1: Responds positively to change, manages competing priorities, and remains flexible in a dynamic programme environment.

Act with Determination: Level 1: Demonstrates initiative, accountability, and persistence in delivering results.

Required Skills and Experience

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

OFFICE/UNIT/PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) is the UN’s global development network, advocating for change and connecting countries to knowledge, experience and resources to help people build a better life. We are on the ground in 170 countries and territories, working with governments and people on their own solutions to global and national development challenges to help empower lives and build resilient nations.

As a trusted, long-term partner of The Global Fund (GF), UNDP’s value proposition lies in providing an integrated package of development solutions to strengthen institutions to deliver health services. Through its contributions as interim Principal Recipient (PR) and provider of technical assistance in over 53 countries since 2003, UNDP’s provision of integrated policy, implementation and capacity development support to countries has yielded significant health and development results in challenging operating environments. Proactive risk management and investing in sustainability are the cornerstones of UNDP’s portfolio management approach and providing technical assistance to national counterparts during all phases of implementation, strengthening legislation, policies and regulatory frameworks, and building capacities across key functional areas, including programme and financial management, integrated health information systems, procurement and supply chain management.

In Zimbabwe, UNDP is the Principal Recipient (PR) for the Global Fund GC8 HIV grant and is also providing Support Services (Fund Administration) to the Ministry of Health and Childcare (MOHCC) as the continuing Global Fund PR for the Tuberculosis (TB), Malaria and Resilient and Sustainable Systems for Health (RSSH) grants. Additionally, UNDP has been designated the ‘CCM Funding Recipient’ responsible for receiving and managing CCM funding on its behalf. The HIV grant for 2027-2029 aims to contribute towards the achievement of the vision and goals of Zimbabwe National HIV Strategic Plan, 2026-2030.

UNDP Zimbabwe manages Global Fund grants through a dedicated Programme Management Unit (PMU), which provides overall programme oversight, coordination, and operational management to ensure effective, compliant, and results-driven implementation. The PMU oversees financial management, risk management, procurement and supply chain operations, monitoring and evaluation, health information systems, integrated capacity development and reporting in line with Global Fund and UNDP policies and procedures.

Working in close partnership with the Ministry of Health and Child Care (MoHCC), National AIDS Council (NAC), national disease programmes, NatPharm, MCAZ, civil society and community organizations, technical partners, donors, UN agencies, the Country Coordinating Mechanism (CCM), LFA and the Global Fund, the UNDP’s PMU strengthens national health systems and ensures the uninterrupted delivery of quality health commodities and services. This contributes to improved prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and health outcomes for HIV, tuberculosis, malaria, and broader health system resilience.

SCOPE OF WORK

Under the direct supervision of the Finance Specialist, the Finance Manager will provide leadership and oversight of financial management, fiduciary assurance, budget management, financial reporting, compliance monitoring, audit coordination, and financial risk management for the Global Fund portfolio managed by UNDP Zimbabwe.

The incumbent will support UNDP's dual role as Principal Recipient (PR) for the HIV Grant; and Funding Administrator (FA) for the TB, Malaria, and RSSH Grants implemented by the Ministry of Health and Child Care (MoHCC).

The Finance Manager will supervise Finance Associates (NPSA-7) and Finance Assistants (NPSA-5) and ensure full compliance with UNDP and Global Fund financial rules, regulations, policies, procedures, and fiduciary assurance requirements.

1. Ensures strategic financial management and oversight of the Global Fund portfolio

- Lead financial planning, forecasting, budget monitoring, and fiduciary oversight for the HIV, TB, Malaria, and RSSH grants.

- Monitor financial performance, budget utilization, absorption rates, cash flow requirements, commitments, and expenditure trends and advise management on appropriate corrective actions.

- Ensure compliance with UNDP financial regulations, Global Fund financial management guidelines, grant agreements, and Funding Administrator Terms of Reference.

- Provide strategic financial analysis and recommendations to support management decision-making and grant performance optimization.

- Identify financial risks and strengthen mitigation measures to safeguard grant resources.

2. Ensures effective budget management, financial reporting, and grant financial performance monitoring

- Lead development, review, monitoring, revision, and reprogramming of grant budgets and funding requests.

- Ensure proper management of project structures, baseline budgets, reprogramming budgets, shadow budgets, authorized spending limits, and grant financial allocations within Quantum.

- Analyze budget variances and monitor financial performance by grant, implementer, intervention, and cost category.

- Lead preparation and review of financial reports, Progress Updates and Disbursement Requests (PUDRs), cash-flow forecasts, donor reports, and management financial reports.

- Produce weekly and monthly financial performance reports, including prepayments, open purchase orders, pending invoices, delivery performance, payroll costs, VAT balances, and cash positions.

- Monitor monthly payroll expenditure under the HIV grant and advise management on budget implications and financial trends.

3. Ensures effective financial resources management, internal controls, and fiduciary assurance

- Maintain robust financial management systems and effective internal controls across the Global Fund portfolio.

- Lead verification of HIV Sub-Recipient expenditures and review MoHCC financial reports under the Funding Administrator arrangement.

- Review and verify financial transactions, disbursement requests, expenditure reports, advances, acquittals, and supporting documentation.

- Monitor ageing advances, prepayments, liquidations, and outstanding balances and ensure timely clearance and recovery of funds.

- Conduct periodic financial reviews, spot checks, and compliance assessments and follow up on corrective actions.

- Ensure timely resolution of non-compliant expenditures, financial exceptions, audit findings, and fiduciary concerns.

4. Ensures sound project accounting, cash management, and financial systems administration

- Lead project and award creation, maintenance, financial revisions, and closure in Quantum.

- Coordinate timely project closure and submission of Financial Closure Reports (FCRs) and liaise with GSSC and corporate finance teams as required.

- Ensure financial transactions are properly recorded, posted, reconciled, and reported in Quantum.

- Review Chart of Accounts (COA), VAT coding, asset classifications, e-requisitions, and financial coding structures for accuracy and compliance.

- Monitor financial exception reports, investigate anomalies, and recommend corrective measures.

- Oversee cash-flow forecasting, liquidity management, disbursement planning, and cash availability across grants.

5. Ensures effective implementation of Funding Administrator financial assurance responsibilities

- Lead implementation of UNDP's financial assurance responsibilities under the Funding Administrator arrangement for TB, Malaria, and RSSH grants.

- Conduct quarterly spot checks of MoHCC financial systems, expenditure records, internal controls, supporting documentation, and grant-funded assets.

- Coordinate preparation of Funding Administrator Service Reports and monitor implementation of agreed management actions and recommendations.

- Support MoHCC in strengthening financial management systems, internal controls, budget monitoring, VAT recovery processes, and fiduciary compliance.

- Monitor VAT reimbursement claims, VAT receivables, tax compliance documentation, and GLOC-related obligations.

- Conduct periodic asset verification exercises and ensure compliance with UNDP and Global Fund asset management requirements.

6. Ensures effective audit coordination, capacity development, team leadership and knowledge sharing

- Coordinate internal, external, Global Fund, and Office of Audit and Investigations (OAI) audits and assurance reviews.

- Ensure timely implementation of audit recommendations, management actions, and risk mitigation measures.

- Supervise Finance Associates and Finance Assistants and provide quality assurance of financial outputs and processes.

- Build the capacity of PMU personnel, Sub-Recipients, MoHCC counterparts, and implementing partners on financial management, fiduciary assurance, internal controls, asset management, and donor compliance.

- Facilitate knowledge sharing, dissemination of lessons learned, and adoption of best practices in grant financial management.

- Participate in relevant financial management, audit, fiduciary assurance, and grant implementation forums as requested d by the Finance Specialist.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENT

The Finance Manager will work under the direct supervision of the Finance Specialist and will supervise Finance Associates (NPSA-7) and Finance Assistants (NPSA-5) supporting the Global Fund portfolio.

The incumbent will lead financial management, budget oversight, fiduciary assurance, financial reporting, compliance monitoring, and audit coordination for UNDP Zimbabwe's Global Fund grants, supporting both the HIV Grant under the Principal Recipient (PR) arrangement and the TB, Malaria, and RSSH Grants under the Funding Administrator (FA) arrangement.

Working closely with the MoHCC, NAC, Sub-Recipients, programme and procurement teams, and key stakeholders, the Finance Manager will oversee grant financial performance, compliance, risk management, financial reporting, and implementation of assurance and audit actions. The position will contribute to accountable, compliant, and efficient grant implementation through strong financial controls, effective fiduciary oversight, and timely financial analysis and decision support.

COMPETENCIES

Core competencies

Achieve Results: LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences

Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands

Act with Determination: LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results

Engage and Partner: LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration

Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

Finance - Financial planning and budgeting: Ability to create and manage processes to achieve UNDP's long and short-term financial goals, including through planning, budgeting, forecasting, analysing and reporting.

Finance - Financial reporting and analysis: Understands changes in regulatory, legal and ethical frameworks and standards for financial reporting in the public sector. Ability to extract, evaluate financial data, derive relevant findings and present them in a meaningful and coherent manner to facilitate effective decision making and performance monitoring. Understands the benefits of integrated reporting, including nonfinancial resources such as human, social and intellectual capital, and environmental and governance performance.

Finance - Financial risk management: Ensures financial resilience through proactive assessment of risk, implementation of controls and taking mitigating action. Understands risk and reward in relation to collaborative and commercial projects. Ensures a culture of positive risk management.

Finance - Audit Risk Management: Ability to address risks and audit issues raised in the course of an audit and propose solutions in order to ensure a true and fair audit opinion is achieve.

Business Management - Risk Management: Identify and organize action around reducing, mitigating and proactively managing risks

Finance - Technology and data in Finance: Ability to understand developments, opportunities and challenges in technology relating to public finance.

Business Direction and Strategy - System Thinking: Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated

elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS OF THE SUCCESSFUL NPSA

Min. Education requirements

• A professional accounting qualification from an internationally accredited institute of accountancy, and/or Advanced university degree (master’s degree or equivalent) in Finance and/or Accounting is required.

• A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the areas stated above, in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

• Candidates with professional accounting qualifications from an internationally accredited institute of accountancy will have a distinct advantage.

• Candidates with no professional accountancy qualifications, but with degrees that major in accountancy and/or finance, must complete the Finance Training and Certification Programme (FTCP), if recruited.

• Candidates satisfying the two above criteria are exempted from undertaking the UNDP Advanced Accountancy and Finance Test (AAFT).

• Candidates with MBA or master's in finance with no accountancy qualification but with relevant experience must successfully undertake the UNDP Advanced Accountancy and Finance Test (AAFT) to be eligible for shortlisting.

Min. years of relevant work experience

A minimum of five (5) years (with master’s degree) or seven (7) years (with bachelor’s degree) of progressively responsible professional experience in financial management, grant finance, budgeting, financial reporting, audit coordination, fiduciary assurance, financial compliance, donor-funded programmes, or related fields is required.

Required skills

• Demonstrated experience managing financial resources, budgets, expenditures, and financial performance of complex projects or donor-funded programmes.

• Proven experience in budget monitoring, forecasting, variance analysis, and management reporting.

• Experience conducting financial reviews, expenditure verification, risk assessment, fiduciary assurance activities, compliance assessments, and spot checks.

• Demonstrated experience coordinating internal and external audits and monitoring implementation of audit recommendations.

• Experience managing grants, Sub-Recipients, implementing partners, or government-funded programmes.

• Experience reviewing and monitoring cash flows, advances, commitments, obligations, and financial risks.

• Experience using ERP systems and financial management platforms, including Quantum, Atlas, Oracle, SAP, PeopleSoft, or equivalent.

• Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel, financial modelling, data analysis, dashboards, and financial reporting tools.

• Experience supporting Global Fund, UNDP, UN agencies, PEPFAR, USAID, World Bank, Gavi, or other donor-funded programmes.

• Experience preparing and reviewing PUDRs, grant closure reports, donor financial reports, cash-flow forecasts, and budget revisions.

• Experience supervising finance personnel and managing finance teams.

• Experience and knowledge of Global Fund financial management and assurance requirements.

• Experience and knowledge of UNDP financial policies and grant management procedures.

• Experience working with government institutions, development partners, auditors, and oversight bodies.

• Experience and knowledge of Zimbabwe public financial management systems and processes.

Required Language(s)

Fluency in English and national language (Shona and/or Ndebele) is required.

Professional Certificates

Professional Certification in IPSAS, Grant Management, Financial Management, Internal Audit, Risk Management, or Public Financial Management is an added advantage.

Professional Certification or advanced training in Quantum ERP, SAP, Oracle Financials, PeopleSoft, or similar ERP systems is desirable.

- Maintain procurement tracking systems covering all procurement actions from initiation to completion.

- Provide procurement guidance and operational support to programme teams, Sub-Recipients, and implementing partners on procurement policies, procedures, and requirements.

jobs.title: Analista Proyecto en Cadenas de Valor (Presencial para Tegucigalpa) [Abierto a candidatos internos y externos]
jobs.description:
Enfoque por niveles

En línea con el compromiso de salvaguardar la capacidad y apoyar al personal ya existente en la Organización, la mayoría de las vacantes de PNUD/UNCDF/UNV se publican utilizando un proceso de postulación por niveles, mediante el cual:

• Nivel 0: Personal internacional del PNUD/UNCDF/VNU con nombramientos permanentes (PA) y de plazo fijo (FTA), cuyos puestos séran abolidos, o cuyos contratos serán rescindidos o no renovados durante el año 2026

• Nivel 1: Otro personal del PNUD/UNCDF/VNU con nombramientos permanentes (PA) y de plazo fijo (FTA)

• Nivel 2: Personal del PNUD/UNCDF/VNU con nombramientos temporales (TA), personal con contratos PSA regulares y Voluntarios Expertos y Especialistas de las Naciones Unidas

• Nivel 3 o sin nivel indicado: Todos los demás tipos de contratos del PNUD/UNCDF/VNU y de otros organismos, y demás candidatos externos

Por favor, tome nota del(los) nivel(es) indicado(s) en el título de la vacante, si corresponde, y asegúrese de cumplir con los requisitos de elegibilidad para postular.

Descripción de la oficina/unidad/proyecto:

El PNUD en Honduras facilita el acceso a asesorías en políticas, finanzas y programas para crear soluciones innovadoras y audaces que aceleren los esfuerzos nacionales para abordar los complejos desafíos del desarrollo. Emplea un enfoque integrador, involucrando activamente y forjando alianzas con diversos actores en la sociedad comprometidos con los Objetivos de Desarrollo Sostenible y el bienestar del país.

El PNUD está presente en unos 170 países y territorios, ofrece una perspectiva global y un conocimiento local. La ventaja comparativa del PNUD en la implementación de proyectos consiste en el aseguramiento de una ejecución presupuestaria (fondos nacionales, préstamos y donaciones, etc.) rápida, eficaz y transparente, con uso eficiente de los recursos, al mismo tiempo que desarrollan y fortalece capacidades en las instituciones de gobierno. El PNUD tiene una capacidad probada de gestión basada en la obtención de resultados, y de transferencia de conocimientos con un expertise de nivel mundial.

La Unidad de Crecimiento Inclusivo del PNUD Honduras forma parte del área de Prosperidad para Todas las Personas y Crecimiento Inclusivo, promoviendo iniciativas orientadas a reducir desigualdades mediante la generación de oportunidades económicas sostenibles, fortalecimiento institucional y mejora de los servicios públicos.

En este contexto, el proyecto Honduras Crece Sostenible busca fortalecer las capacidades institucionales de la Secretaría de Desarrollo Económico (SDE) para mejorar la competitividad, impulsar la transformación productiva y fortalecer el ecosistema empresarial. El proyecto contempla actividades de fortalecimiento institucional, estudios, consultorías, eventos, capacitaciones, mesas de diálogo, cadenas de valor y mecanismos de competitividad que requieren una gestión administrativa, documental y logística eficiente

Alcance del trabajo

Objetivo:

Contribuir técnica y estratégicamente al fortalecimiento de cadenas de valor prioritarias, promoviendo la articulación público-privada, la competitividad, la productividad y la inclusión económica de mujeres y jóvenes.

El/la candidato/a seleccionado/a para esta asignación tendrá las siguientes tareas a cumplir:

1. Co - Liderar la planificación y coordinación técnica de las iniciativas asignadas:

a. Coordinar técnicamente la implementación de las intervenciones piloto en cadenas de valor priorizadas por el proyecto.

b. Redactar reportes de alta calidad con la periodicidad que requieran las iniciativas asignadas.

c. Incorporar transversalmente enfoques de género, juventudes, sostenibilidad, inclusión económica y trabajo decente.

d. Gestionar el desempeño del personal asignado a su cargo, desarrollando evaluaciones periódicas y acompañando la construcción de capacidades de capacidades.

e. Supervisar la ejecución presupuestaria, el cumplimiento de metas y la gestión de riesgos de los componentes e iniciativas bajo su responsabilidad.

2. Contribuir a la gestión de las partes interesadas en las iniciativas asignadas.

a. Apoyar el establecimiento y funcionamiento de mesas sectoriales y mecanismos de diálogo público-privado.

b. Brindar asistencia técnica a actores públicos, privados y organizaciones empresariales participantes.

c. Mantener relaciones colaborativas con las contrapartes o interesados clave en la implementación de las iniciativas.

d. Apoyar en la organización y ejecución de reuniones técnicas periódicas y talleres con socios y contrapartes gubernamentales y otros.

3. Contribuir a la gestión administrativa, financiera y adquisiciones de las iniciativas asignadas.

a. Redactar términos de referencia y liderar el desempeño de consultorías relacionadas con las iniciativas asignadas.

b. Coordinar estudios especializados y actividades de fortalecimiento de capacidades vinculadas con las iniciativas bajo su responsabilidad.

c. Participar como especialista técnico en comisiones de evaluación, que permita la adjudicación de contratos.

d. Acompañar en el seguimiento de contratos adjudicados en las iniciativas asignada.

4. Facilitar el desarrollo de conocimientos y capacidades, y el intercambio de conocimientos.

a. Identificar oportunidades de agregación de valor, innovación, diversificación productiva y acceso a mercados.

b. Elaborar análisis, estudios, diagnósticos y propuestas técnicas para fortalecer cadenas de valor estratégicas.

c. Dar seguimiento a indicadores, resultados y lecciones aprendidas de las intervenciones productivas.

d. Apoyar la generación de evidencia, casos de éxito y productos de conocimiento.

e. Identificar, sintetizar y documentar las mejores prácticas y las lecciones aprendidas que se generen a partir del proyecto y de los socios ejecutores.

El titular desempeña otras funciones dentro de su perfil funcional que se consideren necesarias para el funcionamiento eficiente del PNUD.

Acuerdo Institucional

El/la candidato/a seleccionado/ha seleccionado/a reportará directamente a la coordinación del proyecto.

Competencias

Lograr Resultados:

Nivel 2: Escala soluciones y simplifica procesos, alcanza un balance entre rapidez y precisión al hacer el trabajo.

Pensar Innovadoramente:

Nivel 2: Ofrece nuevas ideas/tiene apertura a nuevas aproximaciones, demuestra pensamiento sistémico/integrado.

Aprender Continuamente:

Nivel 2: Sale de la zona de confort, aprende de los demás y apoya su aprendizaje.

Adaptarse con Agilidad:

Nivel 2: Adapta procesos/aproximaciones a nuevas situaciones, involucra otros en el proceso de cambio.

Actuar con Determinación:

Nivel 2: Capaz de perseverar y lidiar simultáneamente con múltiples fuentes de presión.

Comprometerse y Asociarse:

Nivel 2: Es un facilitador/integrador, une a las personas, construye/mantiene coaliciones/alianzas.

Facilitar la Diversidad y la Inclusión:

Nivel 2: Facilita conversaciones para concertar diferencias, considera opiniones en el proceso de toma de decisiones.

Competencias técnicas y multifuncionales

Gestión Institucional - Gestión basada en los resultados:

• Capacidad para gestionar la puesta en marcha de estrategias, programas y proyectos que se centren en la mejora del rendimiento y los resultados demostrables. Conocimiento y comprensión de las teorías, los conceptos, las metodologías, los instrumentos y las herramientas relevantes.

Gestión de asociaciones - Movilización de recursos:

• Capacidad para identificar fuentes de financiación, emparejar las necesidades (tales como programas, proyectos, o iniciativas) con las oportunidades de financiación y establecer un plan para satisfacer los requisitos de financiación.

Finanzas - Planificación financiera y presupuestación:

• Capacidad para poner en marcha y gestionar procesos que ayuden a lograr los objetivos financieros del PNUD a largo y corto plazo, mediante la planificación, la presupuestación, la previsión, el análisis y la presentación de informes.

Agenda 2030: Compromiso y eficacia - Innovación:

• Monitoreo, evaluación y aprendizaje para carteras de proyectos

Agenda 2030: Personal - Género:

• Gestión del conocimiento y aprendizaje sobre igualdad de género

Requisitos mínimos para el NPSA

Requisitos mínimos de educación

• Título universitario de nivel avanzado (Maestría o equivalente) en Economía, Desarrollo Económico, Agronegocios, Competitividad, Desarrollo Empresarial, Ingeniería Industrial, Administración de Empresas o áreas afines es requisito, o

• Título universitario de primer nivel (Licenciatura) en las áreas anteriores, en combinación con dos (2) años adicionales de experiencia relevante, se dará debida consideración en lugar de una Maestría.

Años mínimos de experiencia laboral relevante

• Los aplicantes con título de maestría (o equivalente) en un campo de estudio relevante no necesitan tener experiencia laboral profesional. Los aplicantes con título de licenciatura (o equivalente) deben tener mínimo dos (2) años de experiencia profesional relevante en procesos relacionados con el impulso y liderazgo en cadenas de valor, articulando los diferentes actores a los eslabones de dichas cadenas.

Habilidades deseables

• Experiencia en análisis y fortalecimiento de cadenas de valor, desarrollo productivo o competitividad.

• Experiencia trabajando con sector privado, MIPYMES, cámaras empresariales o asociaciones productivas.

• Experiencia en formulación de diagnósticos, estudios económicos o análisis sectoriales.

• Experiencia en coordinación interinstitucional y facilitación de espacios multi actor.

• Experiencia aplicando enfoques de género, inclusión económica y desarrollo sostenible.

• Experiencia en proyectos de cooperación internacional o desarrollo.

Idioma(s) requerido(s)

• Fluidez en español es requerido.

• Conocimiento técnico de inglés es requisito

Igualdad de Oportunidades

Como empleador que ofrece igualdad de oportunidades, el PNUD valora la diversidad como una expresión de la multiplicidad de naciones y de las culturas en las que operamos y, como tal, invitamos a todo/as los/las candidato/as calificado/as de diferentes orígenes a aplicar a los diferentes roles en nuestra organización. Nuestras decisiones de empleo están basadas en el mérito y la idoneidad para el puesto, sin discriminación alguna.

El PNUD también está comprometido con la creación de un ambiente laboral inclusivo donde todo el personal esté empoderado para contribuir a nuestra misión, sea valorado, pueda prosperar y se beneficie de oportunidades laborales abiertas a todo/as.

Acoso sexual, explotación y abuso de autoridad

El PNUD no tolera el acoso, acoso sexual, explotación, discriminación y abuso de autoridad. Por lo tanto, todo/as los/las candidato/as seleccionado/as, pasan por verificaciones exhaustivas y se espera que se adhieran a los respectivos estándares y principios.

Derecho a seleccionar múltiples candidato/as

El PNUD se reserva el derecho de seleccionar uno/a o más candidato/as a partir de este anuncio de vacante. También podremos conservar las aplicaciones y considerar a los/las candidato/as que apliquen a este puesto para otros puestos similares en el PNUD con el mismo nivel y con descripciones de puesto, requisitos de experiencia y formación académicas similares.

Uso de IA por parte de los candidatos

Se invita a los postulantes a leer la guía del PNUD para candidatos sobre el uso responsable de inteligencia artificial en los procesos de reclutamiento y selección del PNUD.

Alerta de estafa

El PNUD no cobra ninguna tarifa en ninguna etapa de sus procesos de reclutamiento. Para mayor información, visite www.undp.org/scam-alert.

jobs.title: Asociado(a) de Proyecto en Monitoreo Estratégico y Gestión del Conocimiento para Proyectos de Desarrollo
jobs.description:
Descripción de Proyecto:

El objetivo general del proyecto Sinergia+ es generar procesos de gestión que fortalezcan a la CONANP y que le permitan convertirse en una institución que planea con base en resultados, con finanzas fuertes y mecanismos de gobernanza y alianzas estratégicas eficaces, que contribuyan a incrementar la conectividad entre ecosistemas representativos para salvaguardar su biodiversidad y equilibrio ecológico.

El proyecto Sinergia+ tiene seis resultados estratégicos: 1) Fortalecimiento institucional y gestión para la conservación efectiva en las ANP; 2) Gobernanza y fortalecimiento de redes de colaboración; 3) Enfoque de género y fortalecimiento de la participación ciudadana; 4) Incremento de superficie de conservación con enfoque de conectividad ecológica; 5) Conservación y recuperación de especies en riesgo; 6) Proyectos Estratégicos

En el marco del Proyecto Sinergia+, la persona a contratar contribuirá al fortalecimiento de la Coordinación del Proyecto Sinergia+ para fortificar el monitoreo estratégico y la gestión integral del Proyecto, mediante el análisis y seguimiento de los avances, resultados e indicadores establecidos en la Matriz de Resultados y el Documento de Proyecto (PRODOC); la identificación de riesgos y oportunidades de mejora, así como la integración de informes, generando información que fortalezca la toma de decisiones basada en evidencia, la rendición de cuentas y la visibilidad de los resultados e impactos alcanzados por la CONANP y el PNUD en materia de conservación, desarrollo sostenible y gobernanza ambiental.

Este puesto contribuye al logro de metas del Resultado 6 “Proyectos Estratégicos”

Alcance de Trabajo:

- Asesorar en la planeación e implementación de herramientas que permitan mejorar y hacer más eficiente el se-guimiento y cumplimiento puntual al Programa Operativo Anual.

- Diseñar y coordinar la estrategia y acciones específicas para consolidar la integración de los entregables (medios de verificación), reportes e indicadores definidos en la matriz de resultados del proyecto, PRODOC, así como cola-borar en la integración de los informes de medio término y finales que tenga que reportar el proyecto.

- Establecer y conducir estrategias y acciones específicas para consolidar la integración de los entregables (medios de verificación).

- Analizar y sistematizar la información e insumos disponibles para consolidar la integración de los entregables e informes.

- Coordinar y supervisar el seguimiento a las actividades de las y los colaboradores, asegurando su vinculación con la Matriz de Resultados.

- Consolidar y validar la integración de los indicadores requeridos en la Matriz de Resultados.

- Revisar y emitir recomendaciones técnicas sobre la documentación generada en el y para el Proyecto (lineamien-tos, términos de referencia, entre otros).

- Articular y facilitar la comunicación y coordinación entre consultores, equipo técnico y áreas involucradas.

- Identificar, formular y promover propuestas de mejora en los procesos de seguimiento y elaboración de reportes de monitoreo.

- Identificar, analizar y dar seguimiento a los riesgos que puedan afectar el cumplimiento de los resultados del Proyecto, manteniendo actualizado el registro de riesgos y las correspondientes medidas de mitigación.

Acuerdo Institucional:

El o la persona contratada trabajará bajo la supervisión técnica del/la Coordinador(a) General del Proyecto.

Competencias Esenciales:

Logro de Resultados: Nivel 1: Planifica y monitorea el trabajo propio, presta atención a los detalles, entrega trabajo de calidad en los límites establecidos.

Pensar Innovadoramente: Nivel 1: Tiene apertura a ideas creativas/riesgos conocidos, resuelve problemas de manera pragmática, realiza mejoras.

Aprender Continuamente: Nivel 1: Tiene mente abierta y curiosidad, comparte conocimiento, aprende de los errores, pide retroalimentación.

Adaptarse con Agilidad: Nivel 1: Se adapta al cambio, maneja la ambigüedad/incertidumbre de manera constructiva, es flexible.

Actuar con Determinación: Nivel 1: Muestra determinación y compromiso, capaz de responder calmadamente ante la adversidad, confiado.

Participar y Asociarse: Nivel 1: Demuestra compasión/entendimiento hacia los demás, forma relaciones positivas.

Facilitar la Diversidad y la Inclusión: Nivel 1: Aprecia/respeta las diferencias, reconoce los sesgos inconscientes, confronta la discriminación.

Requisitos Académicos Mínimos:

- Certificado de Preparatoria/Bachillerato, es requisito.

- Estudios Universitarios de primer nivel Licenciatura en: Ciencias Ambientales, Gestión Ambiental, Turismo, Turismo Sustentable, Biología y afines, no es requisito, pero se dará debida consideración.

Años Mínimos de Experiencia Requerida:

- Para candidatos/as con certificado de preparatoria/bachillerato se requieren 7 años de experiencia comprobable en gestión, análisis y sistematización de información e indicadores; y gestión de proyectos vinculados con la conservación, manejo y operación de Áreas Naturales Protegidas, incluyendo coordinación interinstitucional y trabajo con equipos multidisciplinarios.

- Para candidatos/as con Estudios Universitarios de primer nivel Licenciatura, se requiere 4 años de experiencia en los temas antes mencionados.

Habilidades Requeridas:

- Experiencia en: Elaboración de informes de calidad.

Habilidades Deseadas:

•Conocimiento / Experiencia en: conservación de la biodiversidad y gestión de Áreas Naturales Protegidas.

•Conocimiento / Experiencia en: elaboración y análisis de indicadores, matrices de resultados y medios de verificación.

•Conocimiento / Experiencia en: Identificación y gestión de riesgos, así como medidas de mitigación de proyectos.

•Conocimiento / Experiencia en: métodos y herramientas de monitoreo y evaluación de proyectos.

Al ser una contratación nacional al aplicante debe ser ciudadana/o mexicana/o en pleno ejercicio de sus derechos, o extranjera/o, cuya condición migratoria permita la función a desarrollar

jobs.title: Laboratory Systems Specialist [Open to internal and external applicants]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

2. Office/Unit/Project Description

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) is the UN’s global development network, advocating for change and connecting countries to knowledge, experience and resources to help people build a better life. We are on the ground in 170 countries and territories, working with governments and people on their own solutions to global and national development challenges to help empower lives and build resilient nations.

As a trusted, long-term partner of The Global Fund (GF), UNDP’s value proposition lies in providing an integrated package of development solutions to strengthen institutions to deliver health services. Through its contributions as interim Principal Recipient (PR) and provider of technical assistance in over 53 countries since 2003, UNDP’s provision of integrated policy, implementation and capacity development support to countries has yielded significant health and development results in challenging operating environments. Proactive risk management and investing in sustainability are the cornerstones of UNDP’s portfolio management approach and providing technical assistance to national counterparts during all phases of implementation, strengthening legislation, policies and regulatory frameworks, and building capacities across key functional areas, including programme and financial management, integrated health information systems, procurement and supply chain management.

In Zimbabwe, UNDP is the Principal Recipient (PR) for the Global Fund GC8 HIV grant and is also providing Support Services (Fund Administration) to the Ministry of Health and Childcare (MOHCC) as the continuing Global Fund PR for the Tuberculosis (TB), Malaria and Resilient and Sustainable Systems for Health (RSSH) grants. Additionally, UNDP has been designated the ‘CCM Funding Recipient’ responsible for receiving and managing CCM funding on its behalf. The HIV grant for 2027-2029 aims to contribute towards the achievement of the vision and goals of Zimbabwe National HIV Strategic Plan, 2026-2030.

UNDP Zimbabwe manages Global Fund grants through a dedicated Programme Management Unit (PMU), which provides overall programme oversight, coordination, and operational management to ensure effective, compliant, and results-driven implementation. The PMU oversees financial management, risk management, procurement and supply chain operations, monitoring and evaluation, health information systems, integrated capacity development and reporting in line with Global Fund and UNDP policies and procedures.

Working in close partnership with the Ministry of Health and Child Care (MoHCC), National AIDS Council (NAC), national disease programmes, NatPharm, MCAZ, civil society and community organizations, technical partners, donors, UN agencies, the Country Coordinating Mechanism (CCM), LFA and the Global Fund, the UNDP’s PMU strengthens national health systems and ensures the uninterrupted delivery of quality health commodities and services. This contributes to improved prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and health outcomes for HIV, tuberculosis, malaria, and broader health system resilience.

3. Scope of Work

Under the direct supervision of the Health Products Management Specialist (NPSA-11), the Laboratory Systems Specialist will support the Ministry of Health and Child Care (MoHCC), Directorate of Laboratory Services, NatPharm, and implementing partners in strengthening laboratory commodity management, supply chain performance, laboratory information systems, equipment functionality monitoring, and commodity security. The incumbent will provide technical support in laboratory forecasting and quantification, procurement and inventory management, data analytics and reporting, systems strengthening, and capacity development to ensure uninterrupted availability and effective management of laboratory commodities and services.

Key Duties and Responsibilities

1. Guide and Support Laboratory Commodity Forecasting, Quantification and Supply Planning

• Coordinate the forecasting and quantification of laboratory commodities, reagents, consumables, and diagnostic products.

• Support the development, review, and monitoring of national laboratory supply plans.

• Analyse consumption, testing volumes, stock levels, and service utilization data to inform forecasting and supply planning.

• Monitor supply pipelines and identify risks that may affect commodity availability and continuity of laboratory services.

• Prepare quantification analyses, forecasts, and supply planning reports to support national decision-making.

2. Strengthen Laboratory Supply Chain Analytics and Reporting

• Collect, validate, analyse, and interpret laboratory logistics and commodity management data.

• Maintain laboratory commodity databases and logistics management information systems.

• Monitor reporting completeness, timeliness, accuracy, and data quality.

• Produce routine laboratory logistics reports, dashboards, bulletins, and performance analyses.

• Present commodity status updates and analytical findings during technical review meetings and stakeholder forums.

3. Contribute to the Laboratory Procurement and Upstream Supply Chain Management

• Contribute to procurement planning for laboratory commodities, diagnostic products, and equipment.

• Track procurement implementation, purchase orders, shipments, delivery schedules, and associated risks.

• Liaise with procurement units, suppliers, donors, and implementing partners to facilitate timely commodity availability.

• Monitor customs clearance, shipment status, and receipt of laboratory commodities and equipment.

• Analyse procurement performance and recommend actions to mitigate supply chain bottlenecks.

4. Strengthen Inventory Management and Commodity Security

• Monitor national stock status and inventory performance for laboratory commodities.

• Analyse stock-on-hand, consumption trends, months of stock, expiry risks, and supply gaps.

• Develop recommendations to prevent stock-outs, overstocking, expiries, and wastage.

• Support commodity redistribution and emergency response interventions where required.

• Reconcile inventory data across health facilities, NatPharm, and laboratory information systems.

5. Enhance Laboratory Systems and Data Quality Management

• Support the strengthening and optimization of laboratory logistics management information systems and reporting tools.

• Conduct routine data quality assessments, validations, and data verification activities.

• Support the implementation of laboratory logistics digital solutions and system improvements.

• Develop and update standard operating procedures (SOPs), reporting tools, and operational guidelines.

• Promote compliance with national laboratory supply chain policies, standards, and best practices.

6. Monitor Laboratory Equipment Functionality and Maintenance

• Maintain national databases and tools for laboratory equipment functionality monitoring.

• Track equipment uptime, maintenance schedules, warranties, and service contracts.

• Coordinate preventive maintenance activities with service providers and implementing partners.

• Analyse equipment functionality data and identify risks affecting laboratory service delivery.

• Prepare routine reports on equipment performance, maintenance status, and service continuity.

7. Facilitate Capacity Development, Knowledge Sharing, Coordination and Partner Engagement

• Provide mentorship, supportive supervision, and on-the-job training to laboratory and logistics personnel.

• Support coordination between MoHCC, NatPharm, implementing partners, and other stakeholders on laboratory logistics activities.

• Contribute to the implementation and monitoring of laboratory supply chain strengthening initiatives.

• Participate in technical working groups, commodity security committees, review meetings, and partner coordination forums.

• Support grant planning, resource mobilization, forecasting exercises, and other strategic laboratory system strengthening activities.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organisation

Expected Results

The Laboratory Systems Specialist contributes to strengthened laboratory systems through improved forecasting and quantification, enhanced laboratory supply chain performance, reliable logistics information systems, effective equipment monitoring, strengthened commodity security, high-quality reporting and analytics, and increased national capacity to manage laboratory commodities and services. This contributes to uninterrupted laboratory service delivery and improved health outcomes under the Global Fund-supported programmes.

4. Institutional Arrangement

The Laboratory Systems Specialist will work under the direct supervision of the Health Products Management Specialist (NPSA-11).

The Specialist will serve as the technical focal point for strengthening laboratory commodity management, forecasting and quantification, procurement monitoring, laboratory logistics information systems, supply chain analytics, and equipment functionality monitoring. The position will work closely with the MoHCC Directorate of Laboratory Services, NatPharm, laboratory networks, National Disease Programmes, and implementing partners to support uninterrupted availability of laboratory commodities and functional laboratory systems.

To strengthen national capacity and institutional sustainability, the Analyst is expected to spend approximately 70% of his/her level of effort embedded within the MoHCC Directorate of Laboratory Services and NatPharm, working closely with laboratory logistics, supply chain, and equipment management counterparts to strengthen laboratory commodity security, data quality, supply chain performance, and laboratory systems management.

5. Competencies

Core

Achieve Results - LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact

Think Innovatively - LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems

Learn Continuously - LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences

Adapt with Agility - LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands

Act with Determination - LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results

Engage and Partner - LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration

Enable Diversity and Inclusion - LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

Thematic Area Name Definition

Business Management - Results-Based Management: Ability to manage the implementation of strategies, programmes, and projects with a focus at improved

performance and demonstrable results. Knowledge and understanding of relevant theories, concepts, methodologies, instruments, and tools

Business Management - Risk Management: Identify and organize action around reducing, mitigating and proactively managing risks

Partnership Management - Relationship Management: Ability to engage with a wide range of public and private partners, build, sustain and/or strengthen working

relations, trust and mutual understanding

Business Direction and Strategy - System Thinking: Ability to understand and strengthen complex health products and supply chain systems and identify interdependencies across forecasting, supply planning, warehousing, distribution, and information systems.

Business Development - Knowledge Facilitation: Ability to animate individuals and groups, internally and externally, and to design and facilitate activities, to share and exchange knowledge, information and ideas. Knowledge of tools and approaches to stimulate active participation,contribution, and exchange.

Procurement - Category Management: Ability to segment spend into areas which contain similar or related products enabling focus opportunities for consolidation and efficiency

2030 Agenda - People: Health Support to Global Fund and other Health Programmes

6. Minimum Qualifications of the Successful NPSA

Min. Education requirements: Advanced University Degree (Master's Degree or equivalent ) in Medical Laboratory Sciences, Public Health, Biomedical Sciences, Supply Chain Management, Health Logistics, Health Informatics, or related fields are required. Or

A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the areas stated above in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Min. years of relevant work experience: A minimum of 5 years (with a master’s degree) or 7 years (with a bachelor’s degree) of relevant experience in at least four of the following areas is required.

• Global Fund, PEPFAR, CDC, WHO or donor-funded laboratory programmes.

o Proven experience analyzing stock status, consumption trends, pipeline performance, inventory levels, and supply chain risks to inform decision-making and prevent stock-outs, overstocks, and expiries.

o Demonstrated experience preparing and reviewing quantification reports, stock status reports, pipeline analyses, supply plans, procurement implementation reports, and supply chain performance reports.

o Experience monitoring implementation of health products management workplans, procurement plans, budgets, purchase orders, and supplier delivery performance.

o Demonstrated experience developing and monitoring supply chain performance indicators, dashboards, analytics, and management information systems.

o Proven experience in capacity building, mentoring, and institutional strengthening of government and partner personnel in health products and supply chain management.

o Experience in stakeholder coordination and report-writing skills.

Desired skills in addition to the competencies covered in the Competencies section

• Experience supporting Global Fund, PEPFAR, USAID, WHO, UNICEF, or other donor-funded health supply chain programmes.

• Experience participating in national forecasting, quantification, supply planning, Health Products Management Team (HPMT), or supply chain technical working groups.

• Experience supporting implementation and optimization of ERP, eLMIS, warehouse management systems, or other digital supply chain solutions.

• Experience working with MoHCC, NatPharm, National Disease Programmes, or similar public health institutions.

• Experience and knowledge of Zimbabwe's health products management and supply chain systems.

Required Language(s):Fluency in English and national language (Shona and/or Ndebele) is required

jobs.title: Human Resources Associate (Nationals only)
jobs.description:
Background

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) is the UN’s global development network, working in 177 countries and territories. UNDP opened its representative office in Ulaanbaatar in 1976 after more than a decade of successful cooperation with Mongolia. Ever since, UNDP has worked for equitable and sustainable development for the benefit of all Mongolians. UNDP is committed to helping the Government and the people of Mongolia achieve the Sustainable Development Goals as well as other national development priorities. UNDP's country programme is anchored in Mongolia's national priorities. From 2023-2027, the UN Country Team’s partnership with the Government of Mongolia will be guided by the new United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF).

UNDP is looking for a Human Resource Associate to support the HR function for the Country Office in Mongolia.

This assignment is intended to provide maternity leave cover.

Duties and Responsibilities

Ensure effective administration and implementation of HR strategies and policies.

• Ensure full compliance of records and reports with UN rules, regulations, and UNDP policies, procedures, and strategies; effective implementation of the internal controls; and proper functioning of the HR management system and practices.

• In consultation with the direct supervisor and office management, support CO HR business processes mapping, and provide input to content elaboration and update of internal HR Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) where needed in CO to supplement SOPs issued by GSSC/OHR. Adapt processes and procedures where necessary to meet the needs of CO.

• Provide information to management and personnel on the implementation of HR policies, corporate strategies, rules and regulations, HR business processes, and proper use of contractual modalities.

• Collect information and support to UNDP’s participation in inter-agency exercises and surveys, such as comprehensive and interim local salary survey, hardship, and place-to-place surveys, in coordination with the direct supervisor.

• Collect information on the risk management of Country Office HR activities to proactively manage and mitigate the risk.

Provide HR services to the UNDP CO and other UN agencies, including recruitment and staffing.

• Implement recruitment processes in coordination with GSSC and locally with Hiring Managers that includes drafting job descriptions, providing input to job classification process, drafting vacancy announcements, screening candidates, participating in interview panels, providing support for the submission of compliance reviews as per the actions delegated to the CO. In coordination with Hiring Managers, submit requests and appropriate documentation to GSSC for non-delegated actions.

• Facilitate creation and update of positions in ERP (or create positions if delegated) and association and update of positions to chart fields, in coordination with budget owners.

• Follow up with Finance staff and GSSC on Global Payroll issues.

• Monitor and track all transactions related to positions, recruitment, benefits, earnings/deductions, retroactivities, recoveries, adjustments, and separations through ERP and other relevant corporate platforms.

• Process timely contract management actions, in close coordination with supervisors and senior management.

• Provide support to process benefits and entitlements delegated to the CO, as applicable and in coordination with the direct supervisor and management, such as medical evacuations, R&R, safety and security interventions.

• Maintain CO staffing table and local rosters where relevant.

• Validate cost-recovery charges in ERP for HR services provided by UNDP to other Agencies.

• Provide assistance to the contract management, payroll, and separations in coordination with GSSC in accordance with the delegation of authority given to the CO.

• Provide HR support and services to the UN system, including provision of information on personnel benefits and entitlements to UN agencies in line with UNDP policies and in coordination with GSSC as applicable.

• Provide administrative support to retirees as applicable.

Ensure proper staff performance management, talent management and career development in CO.

• Provide background information and maintain related data acting as Secretary to formal CO management groups responsible for collectively reviewing and discussing CO staff performance, talent, and development needs.

• Provide assistance to Performance Management reporting and monitoring.

• Provide input to the CO-wide Learning plan’s preparation in consultation with the Senior Management.

Ensure facilitation of knowledge building and knowledge sharing in the CO.

• Organize training for the Operations and projects staff on HR issues.

• Assist in the creation and implementation of a local onboarding plan, leveraging corporate resources.

• Synthesize lessons learned and best practices in HR.

• Make sound contributions to knowledge networks and communities of practice.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

Under the overall guidance and direct supervision of the Operations Manager, the HR Associate ensures execution of transparent and efficient HR services in the CO. The HR Associate promotes a collaborative, client-oriented approach and supports the maintenance of high staff morale.

The HR Associate may supervise and lead clerical and support staff in the HR Unit. The HR Associate works in close collaboration with the Programme, Operations, and project teams in the CO, UNDP HQ OHR Business Partners, and staff in GSSC and other UN Agencies to exchange information and resolve complex HR-related issues.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

Competencies

Core Competencies

Achieve Results: LEVEL 2: Scale up solutions and simplifies processes, balances speed and accuracy in doing work

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 2: Offer new ideas/open to new approaches, demonstrate systemic/integrated thinking

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 2: Go outside comfort zone, learn from others and support their learning

Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 2: Adapt processes/approaches to new situations, involve others in change process

Act with Determination: LEVEL 2: Able to persevere and deal with multiple sources of pressure simultaneously

Engage and Partner: LEVEL 2: Is facilitator/integrator, bring people together, build/maintain coalitions/partnerships

Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 2: Facilitate conversations to bridge differences, considers in decision making

Cross-Functional & Technical Competencies

Business Development

- Knowledge Facilitation Ability to animate individuals and communities of contributors to participate and share, particularly externally

Business Management

- Operations Management Ability to effectively plan, organize, and oversee the Organization’s business processes in order to convert its assets into the best results in the most efficient manner. Knowledge of relevant concepts and mechanisms

- Working with Evidence and Data Ability to inspect, cleanse, transform and model data with the goal of discovering useful information, informing conclusions and supporting decision-making.

HR - Assessment and Selection

- Knowledge and ability to apply various candidate assessment and selection methodologies, tools and platforms; ability to effectively align them with specific recruitment needs

HR - Recruitment

- Recruitment design and management Knowledge of, ability to design and manage end to end recruitment processes.

HR- Talent management

- Performance management Knowledge of and ability to guide the application of performance management theory, systems and tools, incl. articulation of expectations.

HR - Learning and development

- Ability to design compensation plans which are aligned to current and future organization needs and market conditions; knowledge of and ability to apply the ICSC compensation methodologies and principles. Knowledge of and ability to design benefits-related processes, programmes, and tools, including benefit enrolment and amendments

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Secondary education with specialized certification in HR is required.

- A university degree in Human Resource, Business Administration, Public Administration, or an equivalent field will be given due consideration, but it is not a requirement.

Experience:

- Minimum of 6 years (with high school diploma) or 3 years (with bachelor’s degree) of progressively responsible HR and/or administrative experience at the national or international level is required.

- Demonstrated ability to handle confidential information with discretion and professionalism is required.

- Experience in the use of computers and office software packages (MS Word, Excel, etc.) and advanced knowledge of web-based management systems such as ERP is required.

- Experience working in an international organization and/or UN system is desired.

- Experience working in a multicultural environment and providing client-oriented HR services is desired.

Professional Certificates

- Professional Certificate in human resources management or project management is advantageous.

Required language(s):

- Fluency in English and Mongolian is a requirement.

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.
