jobs.title: Auxiliar Operativo de Proyecto en Análisis de Decretos de Áreas Naturales Protegidas
jobs.description:
Descripción de Proyecto:

El objetivo general del proyecto Sinergia+ es generar procesos de gestión que fortalezcan a la CONANP y que le permitan convertirse en una institución que planea con base en resultados, con finanzas fuertes y mecanismos de gobernanza y alianzas estratégicas eficaces, que contribuyan a incrementar la conectividad entre ecosistemas representativos para salvaguardar su biodiversidad y equilibrio ecológico.

El proyecto Sinergia+ tiene seis resultados estratégicos: 1) Fortalecimiento institucional y gestión para la conservación efectiva en las ANP; 2) Gobernanza y fortalecimiento de redes de colaboración; 3) Enfoque de género y fortalecimiento de la participación ciudadana; 4) Incremento de superficie de conservación con enfoque de conectividad ecológica; 5) Conservación y recuperación de especies en riesgo; 6) Proyectos Estratégicos.

En el marco del Proyecto Sinergia+, la persona a contratar contribuirá al fortalecimiento de la Dirección de Asuntos Jurídicos de la CONANP para fortificar la atención y el seguimiento de los asuntos jurídico relacionados con la gestión y conservación de las Áreas Naturales Protegidas, mediante el apoyo en la integración y revisión de instrumentos jurídicos, la gestión documental, el seguimiento de los procedimientos para la publicación de decretos, la atención de requerimientos de información y el análisis de disposiciones normativas y asuntos legislativos de competencia de la Comisión.

Este puesto contribuye al logro de metas del Resultado 1 “Fortalecimiento institucional y gestión para la conservación efectiva en las ANP”.

Alcance de Trabajo:

Apoyar en la integración y seguimiento de instrumentos técnico-jurídicos relacionados con la gestión, regulación y conservación de las Áreas Naturales Protegidas y otras modalidades de conservación.

Realizar la expedición de copias certificadas y la gestión documental pertinente.

Elaboración y seguimiento de las publicaciones de los Decretos de creación o modificación de las ANP.

Apoyar en las diligencias de campo y en el seguimiento de procedimientos relacionados con las ANP, incluyendo la comunicación formal de asuntos a propietarios o poseedores de predios.

Analizar disposiciones normativas, propuestas de instrumentos jurídicos y asuntos legislativos vinculados con las atribuciones de la CONANP, así como preparar insumos documentales para la atención de consultas y requerimientos jurídicos.

Acuerdo Institucional:

El o la persona contratada trabajará bajo la supervisión técnica de la Dirección de Asuntos Jurídicos, así como de la Coordinación General del Proyecto Sinergia+.

Competencias Esenciales:

Logro de Resultados: Nivel 1: Planifica y monitorea el trabajo propio, presta atención a los detalles, entrega trabajo de calidad en los límites establecidos.

Pensar Innovadoramente: Nivel 1: Tiene apertura a ideas creativas/riesgos conocidos, resuelve problemas de manera pragmática, realiza mejoras.

Aprender Continuamente: Nivel 1: Tiene mente abierta y curiosidad, comparte conocimiento, aprende de los errores, pide retroalimentación.

Adaptarse con Agildad: Nivel 1: Se adapta al cambio, maneja la ambigüedad/incertidumbre de manera constructiva, es flexible.

Actuar con Determinación: Nivel 1: Muestra determinación y compromiso, capaz de responder calmadamente ante la adversidad, confiado.

Participar y Asociarse: Nivel 1: Demuestra compasión/entendimiento hacia los demás, forma relaciones positivas.

Facilitar la Diversidad y la Inclusión: Nivel 1: Aprecia/respeta las diferencias, reconoce los sesgos inconscientes, confronta la discriminación.

Requisitos Académicos Mínimos:

- Certificado de preparatoria/Bachillerato, es requisito.

- Estudios Universitarios de primer nivel Licenciatura en: Derecho o áreas afines, no es requisito, pero se dará debida consideración

Años Mínimos de Experiencia Requerida:

- Para candidatos/as con certificado de preparatoria/bachillerato se requieren 4 años de experiencia comprobable en: Marco Jurídico y Gestión documental para el análisis y seguimiento de decretos de creación o modificación de Áreas Naturales Protegidas. Derecho ambiental y Administración Pública

- Para candidatos/as con Estudios Universitarios de primer nivel Licenciatura, se requiere 1 años de experiencia en los temas antes mencionados.

Habilidades Requeridas:

- Experiencia en: Elaboración de informes de calidad Experiencia en: Manejo de información jurídica ambiental.

Habilidades Deseadas:

- Conocimiento / Experiencia en: Opiniones Jurídicas y análisis normativo

- Conocimiento / Experiencia en: Redacción y comprensión de documentos jurídicos.

- Conocimiento / Experiencia en: Integración documental y normativa

- Conocimiento / Experiencia en: Instrumentos jurídicos ambientales.

- Se dará ventaja si cuenta con conocimiento en Áreas Naturales Protegidas.

Al ser una contratación nacional al aplicante debe ser ciudadana/o mexicana/o en pleno ejercicio de sus derechos, o extranjera/o, cuya condición migratoria permita la función a desarrollar

jobs.title: Project Associate
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers- Tier 3 or no tier indicated: All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidatesPlease make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

UNDP helps Kazakhstan honor its Paris Agreement commitments by supporting the expansion of the "green economy" to tap into new opportunities for jobs and businesses. It partners with other United Nations agencies to provide technical expertise to translate strategies into action, establish a monitoring framework for climate change adaptation and mitigation, and develop plans for transition to green energy, land management, climate-proof agriculture, biodiversity, reforestation, disaster risk reduction, and waste management. By catalyzing SDG and Paris-aligned investments (public and private), UNDP delivers client-focused solutions that respond to immediate, mid and long-term recovery and socio-economic development priorities, and; by leveraging on-the-ground presence and networks, we unlock bottom-up solutions towards lasting impacts at the country level, benefitting most disadvantaged and leaving no one behind.

To enhance programme efficiency, Project Associate within UNDP will support project teams by providing essential financial, procurement, and administrative services to help achieve project goals. Key responsibilities include managing project finances and budgets, supporting procurement, organizing events, maintaining records, and offering additional administrative support as needed, in line with UNDP’s Programme and Operations Policies and Procedures (POPP).

Duties and Responsibilities

1.Support project planning and implementation

• Support effective project planning and implementation.

• Compile and summarize data for work plans, budgets, proposals, and implementation arrangements.

• Ensure activities follow project documents, agreements, and UNDP POPP/SOP; guide staff on procedures when needed.

• Provide administrative and logistical support: organize events, coordinate procurement, Docusign Envelope ID: A0A3EDEA-6DCE-86CD-8320-0346D2D2C998

maintain records, support recruitment and contracting.

2. Support building partnerships

• Maintain collaboration with UN agencies, government, NGOs, academia, and other stakeholders; update partner databases.

• Ensure regular communication, coordination, and feedback mechanisms with partners and beneficiaries.

3 .Support monitoring, evaluation, and reporting

• Collect, analyze, and present data for progress tracking, reporting, and audits; identify gaps and support corrective actions.

• Help organize missions, field visits, workshops, and conferences.

• Monitor budget expenditures and commitments; provide financial updates and draft related correspondence.

• Support the preparation and timely consolidation of project reports in line with donor requirements.

4. Support knowledge sharing and capacity building

• Support training, briefings, and development of tools and materials.

• Share lessons learned and best practices within the CO.

• Contribute to knowledge networks and ensure project knowledge products are documented and shared.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organisation.

Competencies

Achieve Results: LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible

Act with Determination: LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident

Engage and Partner: LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships

Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination

Business Management

Working with Evidence and Data: Ability to inspect, cleanse, transform and model data with the goal of discovering useful information, informing conclusions, and supporting decision-making

Digital Awareness and Literacy: Ability to monitor new and emerging technologies, as well as understand their usage, potential, limitations, impact, and added value. Ability to rapidly and readily adopt and use new technologies in professional activities, and to empower others to use them as needed. Knowledge of the usage of digital technologies and emerging trends.

Customer Satisfaction/Client Management: Ability to respond timely and appropriately with a sense of urgency, provide consistent solutions, and deliver timely and quality results and/or solutions to fulfil and understand the real customers' needs. Provide inputs to the development of customer service strategy. Look for ways to add value beyond clients’ immediate requests. Ability to anticipate client’s upcoming needs and concerns.

Communication: Ability to communicate in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience. Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media, and other appropriate channels.

Monitoring & Evaluation: Ability to systematically monitor results of strategies, programmes, and activities with a view to make sure that they are being implemented

effectively; Ability to provide managers and key stakeholders with regular feedback and reporting on the consistency or discrepancy between planned activities and programme management and results. Ability to make independent judgment of the management and results of strategies, programmes and activities based on set criteria

and benchmark, keeping in mind the needs and concerns of client, current and upcoming. Knowledge and understanding of monitoring and evaluation frameworks, concepts, methodologies, systems, processes, and tools. Ability to make an independent judgement based on set criteria and benchmarks. Ability to anticipate client's upcoming

needs and concerns.

Finance

Required Skills and Experience

Secondary education is required. Or A university Degree (bachelor’s degree) in Business Administration, Public Administration, or equivalent field will be given due consideration, but it is not a requirement.

Experience:

Minimum of 6 years (with secondary education) or 3 years (with bachelor’s degree) of progressively responsible experience in general administration or project management is required.

Required skills:

Experience in the use of computers, office software packages (MS Word, Excel, etc.) and web-based management systems, and advanced knowledge of spreadsheet and database packages.

Desired skills in addition to the competencies covered in the Competencies section:

Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNDP is also committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, are valued, can thrive, and benefit from career opportunities that are open to all.

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

jobs.title: iCOAST Global Coordination Project Manager (Home-Based) (Open to Tier 0,1 & 2)
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Office/Unit/Project Description

UNDP is the knowledge frontier organization for sustainable development in the UN Development System and serves as the integrator for collective action to realize the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). UNDP’s policy work carried out at HQ, Regional and Country Office levels, forms a contiguous spectrum of deep local knowledge to cutting-edge global perspectives and advocacy. In this context, UNDP invests in the Global Policy Network (GPN), a network of field-based and global technical expertise across a wide range of knowledge domains and in support of the signature solutions and organizational capabilities envisioned in the Strategic Plan.

Within the GPN, the Bureau for Policy and Programme Support (BPPS) have the responsibility for developing all relevant policies and guidance to support the results of UNDP’s Strategic Plan. BPPS’s staff provides technical advice to Country Offices, advocates for UNDP corporate messages, represents UNDP at multi-stakeholder fora including public-private dialogues, government, and civil society dialogues, and engages in UN inter-agency coordination in specific thematic areas. BPPS works closely with UNDP’s Crisis Bureau (CB) to support emergency and crisis response. BPPS ensures that issues of risk are fully integrated into UNDP’s development programmes. BPPS assists UNDP and partners to achieve higher quality development results through an integrated approach that links results-based management and performance monitoring with more effective and new ways of working. BPPS supports UNDP and partners to be more innovative, knowledge and data driven including in its programme support efforts.

The Planet Hub is a key strategist, architect, enabler, and implementer that supports the achievement of the Strategic Plan 2026-2029 of UNDP. The Planet Hub drives UNDP’s vision of a world where economies and ecosystems thrive together — where energy systems are clean and accessible, nature is protected and restored, communities are resilient to climate impacts, and pollution is minimized.

Cooling, Circularity & Pollution Prevention (C2P) is a key pillar in the Planet Hub which focuses on greening the supply chain of various industries and products to eliminate harmful chemicals, reducing plastic and waste pollution, and promoting sustainable cooling and circular economy. The team manages the portfolio of UNDP for the Multilateral Fund of the Montreal Protocol, providing policy and technical support on projects funded by the Global Environment Facility (GEF) in the Chemicals and waste focal area, and relevant bilateral projects.

The position will be located in the C2P Pillar. UNDP is partnering with the GEF for sound chemicals and waste management, eliminating the hazardous chemicals and waste from key value chains, facilitating the transition to sustainable production and consumption patterns towards circularity.

In June 2026, UNDP’s Global Coordination Project (GCP) for iCOAST (Integrated Collaborative Approaches for Sustainable Tourism) (“iCOAST”) was approved by the GEF. The objective of iCOAST is to transform the tourism sector by fostering an enabling policy and regulatory environment—supported by targeted financial mechanisms and products—that incentivizes governments, the private sector, and local communities to adopt and benefit from sustainable tourism practices. The programme promotes the development of local, sustainable supply chains linked to tourism and makes it easy and attractive for tourists to choose sustainable options without compromising quality, affordability, or comfort. Ultimately, iCOAST seeks to reduce pollution of water, soil, and air; cut greenhouse gas emissions; curb the overconsumption of natural resources, products, and materials; and reverse tourism‑driven biodiversity loss, while generating equitable livelihoods and jobs for local communities. iCOAST is a global programme implemented through national activities in fourteen countries (11 national projects and 1 regional) —Belize, Dominican Republic, Egypt, Honduras, Indonesia, Jamaica, Maldives, Mexico, Morocco, Seychelles, Tanzania, Trinidad & Tobago, Türkiye and Vanuatu—complemented by a global child project (GCP) that delivers technical assistance and facilitates coordination across the national projects.

The global coordination project of iCOAST+ will be implemented by the UNDP C2P Pillar. This position will be responsible for the implementation of the GEF iCOAST GCP and other related contributions to the C2P Pillar.

Scope of work

The iCOAST Global Coordination Project Manager heads the Project Management Unit (PMU) of the Global Coordination Project (GCP). This person will ensure adequate technical, administrative, logistic, and financial support for project execution. He/she will be responsible for the day-to-day management of the project on behalf of UNDP. This includes the mobilization of resources, contract management, budget management, bookkeeping, procurement and supervision of project staff, consultants, subcontractors, and responsible parties (in case these are designated during project execution). This person will ensure adequate project implementation, and the generation of the outputs and outcomes set in the project document. He/she will closely work with the GCP project´s partners (i.e., UN Tourism and UNDP Sustainable Finance Hub), the coordinators of the iCOAST child projects, and other relevant actors to ensure that the project deliverables are technically sound.

Guide and support the overall management of the iCOAST GCP

- Guide and support the iCOAST Project Steering Committee (PSC) for overall management of project activities and decision making.

- Oversee and provide strategic guidance for the operation of the global working groups and the communities of practice.

- Promote innovative approaches under low-carbon, low-chemical, zero-waste, and zero-pollution sustainable tourism, including among others adressing marine and coastal pollution, including circular economy solutions and improving waste management systems.

- Provide secretarial support to the Programme Advisory Committee and facilitate its collaboration with the Project Steering Committee.

- Lead the preparation of the global inception workshop, annual work plan and global events, determined in the project monitoring plan and update the plan as required.

- Perform regular progress reporting to the PSC as agreed with the members, including measures to address challenges and opportunities.

- Monitor progress, watch for plan deviations and make course corrections when needed within project PSC-agreed tolerances to achieve results.

- Expand partnerships on low-carbon, low-chemical, zero-waste, and zero-pollution sustainable tourism at regional and international levels.

- Lead knowledge management and communication on low-carbon, low-chemical, zero-waste, and zero-pollution sustainable tourism.

Coordinate the implementation in the 14 participating countries (including non-UNDP child projects)

- Conduct regular meetings with implementing partners in the fourteen countries through the child projects’ project managers to monitor progress of activities in the field and collect information.

- Respond to the questions from local partners and provide necessary technical support and training to the country teams.

- Facilitate south-south cooperation and information exchange

- Support and guide the integration of circular economy approaches, sustainable consumption and production, and pollution reduction strategies within project activities and partnerships.

Manage a project management unit to support the implementation of the GCP of iCOAST

- Engage with international technical and financial experts, and responsible parties to provide support to 14 countries in line with the iCOAST global coordination project document.

- Execute activities by managing personnel, goods and services, training and low-value grants, including drafting terms of reference and work specifications, and overseeing all contractors’ work.

- Monitor financial resources and accounting to ensure the accuracy and reliability of financial reports.

- Manage requests for the provision of UNDP financial resources through funding advances, direct payments or reimbursement using the FACE form, in coordination with the project assistant.

- Prepare and submit financial reports to the Senior Technical Advisor in LAC of the C2P Pillar on a quarterly basis.

Perform monitoring and evaluation

- Monitor events as determined in the project monitoring plan, and update the plan as required.

- Provide support for completion of assessments required by UNDP, spot checks and audits.

- Manage and monitor the project risks – including social and environmental risks - initially identified and submit new risks to the PSC for consideration and decision on possible actions if required; update the status of these risks by maintaining the project risks log;

- Ensure that the indicators included in the project results framework are monitored annually, prepare the annual GEF Project Implementation Report (PIR);

- Monitor implementation plans including the gender action plan, stakeholder engagement plan, and any environmental and social management plans;

- Visit project sites as and when required to appraise project progress on the ground and validate written progress reports.

- Monitor and track progress against the GEF Core indicators.

- Oversee and ensure the implementation of the project’s M&E plan, including periodic appraisal of the Project’s Theory of Change and Results Framework with reference to actual and potential project progress and results;

- Oversee/develop/coordinate the implementation of the stakeholder engagement plan;

- Oversee and guide the design of surveys/ assessments commissioned for monitoring and evaluating project results;

- Support the Mid-term review and Terminal Evaluation process, including the management response.

Ensure Partnership Development, Communication and facilitate Knowledge Management

- Engage with other UN agencies for collaboration and collective advocacy on low-carbon, low-chemical, zero-waste, and zero-pollution sustainable tourism.

- Capture lessons learned during project implementation.

- Contribute to communications and knowledge management work of the C2P Pillar.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

The iCOAST Global Coordination Project Manager will work under the direct supervision of the C2P MPU/Chemicals Regional Coordinator for LAC.

Competencies Core

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands

- Act with Determination:LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results

- Engage and Partner:LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

2030 Agenda: Planet Chemicals & Waste Hub

- Chemicals and Waste: Waste to Energy

Business Management -Project Management

- Ability to plan, organize, prioritize and control resources, procedures and protocols to achieve specific goals.

Partnership management-Relationship management

- Ability to engage with a wide range of public and private partners, build, sustain and/or strengthen working relations, trust and mutual understanding

Business Management - Monitoring and Evaluation

- Ability to systematically monitor results of strategies, programmes, and activities with a view to make sure that they are being implemented effectively; Ability to provide managers and key stakeholders with regular feedback and reporting on the consistency or discrepancy between planned activities and programme management and results.

- Ability to make independent judgment of the management and results of strategies, programmes and activities based on set criteria and benchmark, keeping in mind the needs and concerns of client, current and upcoming.

- Knowledge and understanding of monitoring and evaluation frameworks, concepts, methodologies, systems, processes, and tools. Ability to make an independent judgement based on set criteria and benchmarks. Ability to anticipate client's upcoming needs and concerns.

2030 Agenda: People Gender

- Gender Equality and Institutional Transformation

2030 Agenda: Planet Chemicals & Waste Hub

- Chemicals and Waste: Secondary metals

Business Direction and Strategy -System Thinking

- Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system

Required Skills and Experience

Academic Education

- Advanced university degree (master's degree or equivalent) in Environment, Environmental Economics, Chemicals, or other closely related field is required, or

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the areas stated above, in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Min. years of relevant Work experience

- Minimum of 5 years (with a Master’s degree) or 7 years (with a Bachelor’s degree) of relevant professional experience in at least two geographic regions, with a strong track record in portfolio management, resource mobilization, and the design and implementation of national and multi-country projects/programmes related to environment, climate, and energy, particularly in chemicals and waste management, circular economy, marine and coastal pollution, and sustainable tourism.

Required skills

- Experience managing and coordinating complex environmental portfolios, programmes, or projects involving multiple stakeholders, including governments, international organizations, implementing partners, and donors.

- Experience in the design, development, implementation, and quality assurance of GEF-funded and other international environmental projects, including monitoring, evaluation, and results-based management.

Desired additional skills and competences

- Demonstrated experience in leadership and coordination experience in the chemicals and waste sector, including the development and implementation of global and multi-country initiatives.

- Experience supporting the implementation of Multilateral Environmental Agreements (MEAs), particularly those related to chemicals and waste, biodiversity conservation, or marine and coastal pollution, is an asset.

- Technical experience in one or more of the following areas: circular economy, sustainable consumption and production, pollution prevention and reduction, marine litter, or resource efficiency.

- Experience in UNDP policies and frameworks related to gender equality, environmental and social safeguards, and mainstreaming of cross-cutting issues.

Required Language(s)

- Fluency in English is required.

- Working knowledge of another UN language desired

Travel

The Contractor will be expected to travel to client countries, international meetings for UNDP events when needed.

UNDP will cover the cost of travel of the individual to the duty station, as well as their return to their home upon completion of their services. Travel costs are covered only in the event that the function will be undertaken physically in the duty station and excludes working from home arrangement

Equal opportunity

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNDP is also committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, are valued, can thrive, and benefit from career opportunities that are open to all.

Sexual harassment, exploitation, and abuse of authority

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

Right to select multiple candidates

UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement. We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.

Use of AI by candidates

Applicants are invited to read UNDP’s guidance for candidates on using AI responsibly in UNDP recruitment and selection

Scam alert

UNDP does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process. For further information, please see www.undp.org/scam-alert.

jobs.title: Cientista de Dados (Office Based) [Open to internal and external applicants]
jobs.description:
Descrição do Tier

Tier 0: Funcionários IP do UNDP/UNCDF/UNV que possuem nomeações permanentes (PA) e por prazo determinado (FTA), cujos contratos serão rescindidos ou não renovados durante 2026

Tier 1: Outros funcionários do UNDP/UNCDF/UNV que possuem nomeações permanentes (PA) e por prazo determinado (FTA) (definidos como candidatos “internos”)

Tier 2: Funcionários do UNDP/UNCDF/UNV que possuem nomeações temporárias (TA), pessoal com contratos PSA regulares e Voluntários da ONU Expert e Specialist

Tier 3: Todos os demais tipos de contrato do UNDP/UNCDF/UNV e de outras agências, e outros candidatos externos”

Descrição do Escritório/Unidade/Projeto

O PNUD oferece soluções integradas de programas, políticas e financiamento para alcançar os Objetivos de Desenvolvimento Sustentável (ODS). Nesse contexto, o PNUD criou a Rede Global de Políticas (Global Policy Network – GPN), uma rede de especialização técnica, de campo e global, em uma ampla gama de áreas de conhecimento e em apoio às soluções-chave (signature solutions) e às capacidades organizacionais previstas no Plano Estratégico. O Birô de Políticas e Apoio a Programas (BPPS) e o Birô de Crises (CB) são os dois birôs âncora da GPN. Nesse contexto, o Hub de Governança, Estado de Direito e Construção da Paz (GRP), um esforço conjunto com o BPPS, oferece liderança e serviços de assessoria para ampliar o impacto do PNUD em governança e construção da paz, assegurando a integração da governança democrática e dos direitos humanos na resposta e na recuperação em situações de crise.

Os governos locais e regionais já são responsáveis por mais de 65% das metas dos ODS, a maioria delas ligada à prestação de serviços básicos, como água, saneamento, mobilidade, ação climática, saúde ou educação. Cidades e territórios têm um papel central na implementação dos ODS, que estão se tornando um novo instrumento de planejamento estratégico e orçamentação no médio e longo prazo. Desde 2015, os governos locais e suas associações têm atuado de forma cada vez mais ativa na promoção dos ODS, por meio de advocacy e do trabalho com a população local e com parceiros para transpor o espírito da Agenda 2030 para cidades e territórios. Os governos locais também passaram a usar os ODS como marco estratégico para oferecer serviços públicos melhores e mais inovadores, vinculados às metas e aos indicadores dos ODS. No âmbito do projeto SDG Local Action, o PNUD é um dos parceiros implementadores do Mayors Challenge, uma iniciativa global para repensar os serviços mais essenciais que as cidades prestam aos seus moradores.

Nesse contexto, o projeto SDG Local Action busca contratar um(a) Cientista de Dados para apoiar a implementação do projeto Mayors Challenge 2025 no Rio de Janeiro, Brasil. O projeto implementa uma metodologia de política pública orientada por dados para antecipar as necessidades dos cidadãos e oferecer serviços de forma proativa, com potencial de replicação em diferentes públicos-alvo. Sua aplicação inicial se dá por meio da Plataforma Pequenos Cariocas, iniciativa prioritária da Prefeitura do Rio de Janeiro voltada à primeira infância. O projeto utiliza o Registro Municipal Integrado (RMI), base de dados consolidada no data lake municipal que integra informações de Saúde, Educação e Assistência Social, possibilitando análises avançadas e uma visão mais integrada dos cidadãos. Com base nessa infraestrutura, o projeto combina modelos analíticos e comunicação proativa, especialmente via WhatsApp, para ampliar o acesso aos serviços e gerar dados que apoiem políticas públicas mais efetivas.

O(A) Cientista de Dados será responsável por liderar iniciativas analíticas e garantir a qualidade e a confiabilidade dos dados que orientam as decisões de políticas públicas, atuando principalmente com o RMI (Registro Municipal Integrado) – data warehouse estratégico que consolida informações de saúde, educação, assistência social e dezenas de outros sistemas municipais – no desenvolvimento de análises, métricas estratégicas e visualizações que apoiem a tomada de decisão baseada em evidências.

Escopo de trabalho

A. Garantir análises exploratórias e estatísticas para apoiar decisões

- Liderar análises exploratórias para identificar padrões, anomalias e oportunidades de melhoria nas bases municipais (saúde, educação e assistência social).

- Criar queries analíticas complexas em SQL (BigQuery) para extrair insights e validar hipóteses.

- Realizar análises estatísticas para apoiar a alocação de recursos e a identificação de vulnerabilidades.

B. Garantir métricas, indicadores e visualizações estratégicas

- Desenvolver e manter métricas estratégicas, KPIs e dashboards que monitorem a efetividade de programas e políticas públicas.

- Criar visualizações e narrativas baseadas em dados para públicos técnicos e executivos.

C. Garantir a qualidade, a confiabilidade e a governança dos dados

- Identificar inconsistências nos dados e propor melhorias sistêmicas.

- Estabelecer e documentar padrões de qualidade de dados, metodologias analíticas e boas práticas para o time.

D. Garantir a articulação com as equipes e os gestores públicos

- Colaborar com as equipes de engenharia de dados, produto e gestores públicos para traduzir requisitos em soluções analíticas robustas.

E. Apoiar a construção e o compartilhamento de conhecimento

- Realizar análises que identifiquem lacunas, oportunidades de integração e necessidades de dados do RMI.

O(A) ocupante da posição desempenha outras atividades compatíveis com seu perfil funcional, conforme necessário para o bom funcionamento do projeto.

Arranjo institucional

Esta posição reporta ao Gerente de Projeto, Rio Mayors Challenge. O(A) ocupante trabalhará em estreita colaboração com a IplanRio, as secretarias municipais relevantes, as equipes técnicas e as contrapartes do PNUD para apoiar a implementação, a coordenação e a elaboração de relatórios do projeto.

Competências

Essenciais (Core)

Alcançar resultados: NÍVEL 1: Planeja e monitora o próprio trabalho, presta atenção aos detalhes, entrega trabalho de qualidade no prazo

Pensar de forma inovadora: NÍVEL 1: Aberto(a) a ideias criativas/riscos conhecidos, resolve problemas de forma pragmática, promove melhorias

Aprender continuamente: NÍVEL 1: Mente aberta e curiosa, compartilha conhecimento, aprende com os erros, pede feedback

Adaptar-se com agilidade: NÍVEL 1: Adapta-se a mudanças, lida de forma construtiva com ambiguidade/incerteza, é flexível

Agir com determinação: NÍVEL 1: Demonstra iniciativa e motivação, consegue entregar com calma diante de adversidades, tem confiança

Engajar e construir parcerias: NÍVEL 1: Demonstra compaixão/compreensão em relação aos outros, constrói relações positivas

Promover diversidade e inclusão: NÍVEL 1: Valoriza/respeita as diferenças, tem consciência de vieses inconscientes, enfrenta a discriminação

Competências transversais e técnicas

DATA Data analysis

Capacidade de extrair, analisar e visualizar dados (incluindo dados em tempo real) para gerar insights relevantes e apoiar a tomada de decisão eficaz.

DIGITAL Data governance

Conhecimento de ciência de dados, habilidade para desenvolver ferramentas de gestão de dados, organizar e manter bancos de dados e operar tecnologias de visualização de dados.

DIGITAL Data storytelling and communications

Habilidade para construir uma narrativa em torno de um conjunto de dados e de suas visualizações, de modo a transmitir o significado desses dados de forma poderosa e convincente.

DIGITAL Data strategy and management

Conhecimento para elaborar ou executar uma estratégia de dados ou um marco de gestão de dados.

BUSINESS MANAGEMENT Working with Evidence and Data

Capacidade de examinar, limpar, transformar e modelar dados com o objetivo de descobrir informações úteis, embasar conclusões e apoiar a tomada de decisão.

BUSINESS MANAGEMENT Communication

· Comunicar-se de forma clara, concisa e inequívoca, tanto por escrito quanto oralmente; adaptar as mensagens e escolher os métodos de comunicação conforme o público;

· Capacidade de gerir a comunicação interna e externa, por meio da mídia, das redes sociais e de outros canais apropriados.

Qualificações mínimas do(a) NPSA selecionado(a)

Requisitos mínimos de formação

Diploma universitário de nível avançado (mestrado ou equivalente) em Ciência de Dados, Estatística, Ciência da Computação, Matemática, Economia, Políticas Públicas ou área afim é requisito. Ou

Diploma universitário de primeiro nível (graduação/bacharelado) nas áreas mencionadas acima, combinado com dois anos adicionais de experiência qualificada, será considerado em substituição ao diploma de nível avançado.

Anos mínimos de experiência profissional relevante

Candidatos com mestrado (ou equivalente) em uma área de estudo relevante não são obrigados a ter experiência profissional. Candidatos com bacharelado (ou equivalente) são obrigados a ter um mínimo de dois (2) anos de experiência profissional relevante em análise e ciência de dados.

Habilidades desejáveis, além das competências previstas na seção Competências

- Experiência em SQL para queries analíticas complexas, otimização de performance e modelagem de dados (BigQuery).

- Sólida experiência com Python para análise de dados (Pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib, Seaborn).

- Experiência em Base estatística forte: análise exploratória de dados (EDA), estatística descritiva e inferencial e testes de hipóteses.

- Experiência comprovada com qualidade de dados, validação, governança e boas práticas de documentação.

- Experiência em ferramentas de visualização e BI (Looker, Metabase, Power BI ou similar) para a criação de dashboards estratégicos.

- Experiência em traduzir perguntas de negócio complexas em análises técnicas e comunicar resultados para diferentes públicos.

- Experiência com versionamento (Git), reprodutibilidade de análises e boas práticas de desenvolvimento analítico.

- Experiência com dbt para transformação, modelagem e documentação de dados.

- Experiência em Google Cloud Platform (BigQuery, Looker Studio, Cloud Functions).

- Experiência com dados governamentais, políticas públicas ou projetos de impacto social.

- Experiência em ferramentas de qualidade e observabilidade de dados (Great Expectations, dbt tests ou similar).

- Experiência com análise de séries temporais, análise de coorte ou análise geoespacial.

- Experiência com orquestração de pipelines (Airflow, Prefect, Dagster).

- Experiência prévia em definição de padrões, documentação técnica ou mentoria de analistas.

Idioma(s) exigido(s)

Fluência em português é requisito.

Conhecimento funcional de inglês é um diferencial.

Igualdade de oportunidades

Como empregador que oferece igualdade de oportunidades, o UNDP valoriza a diversidade como uma expressão da multiplicidade de nações e culturas onde operamos e, como tal, incentivamos candidatos qualificados de todas as origens a se candidatarem a funções na organização. Nossas decisões de emprego são baseadas no mérito e na adequação à função, sem discriminação.

O UNDP também está comprometido em criar um ambiente de trabalho inclusivo, onde todo o pessoal seja capacitado a contribuir para nossa missão, seja valorizado, possa prosperar e se beneficiar de oportunidades de carreira abertas a todos.

Assédio sexual, exploração e abuso de autoridade

O UNDP não tolera assédio, assédio sexual, exploração, discriminação e abuso de autoridade. Todos os candidatos selecionados, portanto, passam por verificações relevantes e espera-se que cumpram os respectivos padrões e princípios.

Direito de selecionar múltiplos candidatos

O UNDP reserva-se o direito de selecionar um ou mais candidatos a partir deste anúncio de vaga. Também podemos reter candidaturas e considerar candidatos que se candidatem a este posto para outras posições semelhantes no UNDP, no mesmo nível de classificação e com descrição de funções, experiência e requisitos educacionais semelhantes.

Alerta de fraude

O UNDP não cobra nenhuma taxa em nenhuma etapa do seu processo de recrutamento. Para mais informações, consulte www.undp.org/scam-alert.

jobs.title: Partnership Analyst (Open to Tier 0, 1 & 2 applicants Only)
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Office/Unit/Project Description

The UNV Field Units (FU) are mainly accountable for the mobilization and placement of UN Volunteers in UN Agencies, Funds, and Programmes focused on peace, development and humanitarian needs. The UNV Field Units represent and position UNV in the respective countries and bring UNV’s services and solutions closer to its partners from governments, UN entities, civil society and private sector.

Scope of Work

1. Coordinate Country-level partnership development, demand analysis and volunteer mobilization

- Proactively develop and sustain partnerships at the country level with UN agencies, government institutions, civil society and partners to advance UNV’s mandate, identify collaboration opportunities, and ensure effective integration of volunteer solutions into programme delivery.

- Participate in UN collective planning processes (CCA, UNSDCF, humanitarian response plans, thematic task forces) to integrate volunteerism in their implementation.

- Analyze the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework, Country Programme Documents, and sectoral strategies to identify priority entry points for integrating UNV volunteer solutions.

- Analyze partner demand and contribute to the development and execution of country-level volunteer mobilization strategies in line with UNV’s Strategic Framework.

- Identify and assess opportunities for the deployment of onsite and online Volunteers across development, humanitarian, and peace portfolios, in line with partner priorities.

- Promote volunteerism at the field level by organizing outreach activities, supporting awareness campaigns, and engaging partners and communities to integrate volunteer solutions into local development and humanitarian initiatives.

- Articulate and present UNV’s value proposition and volunteer modalities to partners through data‑driven briefing materials, presentations, and analytical notes.

- Support national talent attraction and pipeline management based on country demand forecasts and recruitment priorities, in coordination with the Regional Talent Acquisition Analyst.

2. Ensure Business intelligence, demand analysis and planning

- Develop and maintain structured country‑level business intelligence on UN partner mandates, programme pipelines, and emerging priorities relevant to volunteer mobilization.

- Monitor mobilization trends, track key performance indicators, and use corporate tools (CRM, BI reports, UVP) to support planning, forecasting, and strategic decision making.

- Contribute to adapting regional volunteer mobilization priorities into country-specific recommendations, based on partner needs, data analysis, and local context.

- Contribute to the identification of thematic volunteer solutions, pilot initiatives, and joint approaches aligned with national needs and UN priorities in the country.

3. Ensure Duty of Care

- Coordinate closely with the Field Security Officer and host entities to ensure that UN Volunteers are adequately informed of, and compliant with, all applicable security policies, procedures, and risk‑mitigation measures.

- Ensure timely and compliant medical evacuation support for UN Volunteers, ensuring coordination with medical providers, host entities, and relevant offices at UNV

- Ensure the well‑being and performance of serving UN Volunteers by maintaining regular contact, conducting periodic field visits to duty stations, and engaging with supervisors and counterparts to address emerging issues and support effective service delivery.

- In consultation with relevant sections, provide timely support to the UN Volunteers throughout their volunteer’s journey

4. Ensure Management, knowledge building and sharing

- Develop and manage the implementation of the Field Unit’s annual work plan and set performance indicators, including management and reporting on UNV operational support funds and budget;

- Facilitate the effective functioning of the UNV country presence by ensuring coordinated service delivery and promoting a supportive and collaborative work environment that supports learning, professionalism.

- Manage any UNV assigned personnel within the FU including supervision, performance assessment and capacity development.

- Facilitate knowledge and capacity building, knowledge sharing and advocacy

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization

Supervisory/Managerial Responsibilities: May supervise the Communications personnel in the Regional Office.

Institutional Arrangement

Reporting to the Portfolio Manager/Specialist, Regional Office, the Partnership Analyst leads country‑level analytical and partnership support to advance UNV’s volunteer mobilization agenda in the country. The position combines strategic partnership analysis, business intelligence, and operational coordination, while overseeing the team of UN Volunteers supporting Field Unit activities.

The incumbent is responsible for strengthening UNV’s positioning as a solution provider for UN partners, supporting increased and diversified volunteer mobilization, and ensuring coherence between country‑level engagement and regional and global UNV priorities.

As UNV is a systemwide service administered by UNDP, FUs are hosted within relevant UNDP offices, collaborating closely with the UNDP Resident Representative and the UN Resident Coordinator. The Partnership Analyst ensures compliance with UNV and UNDP policies, rules and regulations.

Competencies

CORE

Achieve Results

- Scale up solutions and simplifies processes, balances speed and accuracy in doing work

Think Innovatively:

- Offer new ideas/open to new approaches, demonstrate systemic/integrated thinking

Learn Continuously:

- Go outside comfort zone, learn from others and support their learning

Adapt with Agility:

jobs.title: Regional Energy Policy Analyst [Open to internal and external applicants]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

UNDP is the knowledge frontier organization for sustainable development in the UN Development System and serves as the integrator for collective action to realize the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). UNDP’s policy work carried out at HQ, Regional and Country Office levels, forms a contiguous spectrum of deep local knowledge to cutting-edge global perspectives and advocacy. Within this context, UNDP invests in a network of field-based and global technical expertise across a wide range of knowledge domains and in support of the signature solutions and organizational capabilities envisioned in the Strategic Plan.

As per UNDP’s new Strategic Plan 2026-2029, UNDP aims to catalyze unprecedented action and partnerships to provide access to sustainable, affordable, and reliable energy to people and accelerate the transition to renewable energy through systemic changes that lead to inclusive green economies. UNDP’s Regional Bureau for Asia and the Pacific (RBAP) responds to these challenges and harness networks, experience, and innovation through its Bangkok Regional Hub (BRH) and Country Offices. It focuses on three pillars of sustainable energy for development:

- Close the gap in energy access so that marginalized people and communities gain access to sustainable, clean energy and the dignity and opportunities it brings;

- Accelerate the energy transition through systemwide changes that support a green economy by bringing together the best ideas from the worlds of government, business, finance, digital, and most importantly, from people, communities and civil societies;

- Scale up energy finance with the public and private sector, across global, regional and local ecosystems for finance, innovation and investment.

To provide our client governments, communities and people with context-based, technically-sound, and demand-driven interventions to realize the three pillars above through the implementation of the Strategic Plan 2026-2029 and the Regional and Country Programmes, RBAP works closely with the Global Policy Network (GPN) of UNDP.

The Regional Energy Policy Analyst will work closely with GPN Technical Specialists and Policy Advisors supporting the Asia-Pacific region to advance the sustainable energy agenda, while engaging with country offices in the region and enabling strategic partnerships with regional organizations and partner UN agencies, under the overall guidance of the Regional Team Leader for Asia and the Pacific of the Planet Team. In close collaboration with other Specialists and Advisors, the Regional Energy Policy Analyst will provide policy and programme support to:

- de-risk energy investments.

- scale up energy finance;

- promote innovation, technology, and data for sustainable energy,

- enable SDGs through an inclusive, just energy transition,

- advance energy access and transition policies and the enabling policy environment e.g. on carbon pricing, energy audits and fossil fuel subsidy reform; and

- expand energy access for poor and displaced communities, among other activities.

The Regional Energy Policy Analyst will be supervised by Regional Technical Specialist for Climate Change Mitigation based in Bangkok Regional Hub.

Duties and Responsibilities

The incumbent will be based at the Bangkok Regional Hub (BRH), Thailand, and will report to and work under the direct supervision of the Regional Technical Advisor for Climate Change Mitigation based in BRH, who will serve as the primary supervisor. The incumbent will work in close collaboration with the Decarbonization and Sustainable Energy Pillar of the Planet Hub and will be provided with access to relevant information necessary to carry out the assignment.

i. Ensure Strategic Leadership, Programme Support, Policy Advice and Innovation

- Contribute to the strategic approaches for UNDP’s work on sustainable energy and climate change mitigation, drawing on UNDP’s existing work under RBAP and the Planet Hub’s Decarbonization and Sustainable Energy Pillar with strategic linkages with a Vertical Fund-financed portfolio of projects as well as analysis of the global/regional policy context;

- Support development of sustainable energy policies and tools, including for crisis contexts (where relevant and as requested, as these efforts may vary);

- Support UNDP’s work in the RBAP to assist countries at the regional level in designing strategies and policies to support energy access priorities, promote the energy transition, and foster low carbon growth in the context of their sustainable development efforts;

- Contribute to the development and implementation of new strategic programming and partnerships in areas of energy access and the energy transition to achieve results set within UNDP’s Strategic Plan, Energy Offer, SIDS Offer, and the work plans of Planet Hub;

- Collaborate with global, regional, national, and sub-national staff to promote UNDP’s de-risking approach and implementation of the corporate sustainable energy strategy;

- Work collaboratively with colleagues across and beyond RBAP colleagues to identify policy issues regarding the implementation of energy-related SDGs and the nationally determined contributions (as they relate to energy).

ii. Policy Positioning and Promote Strong Partnerships

- Support to mobilize, foster, and strengthen strategic partnerships with UN entities, and other relevant bodies at the regional level, and provide inputs to those partnerships in support of UNDP initiatives;

- Prepare briefing notes and speeches. Advocate the importance of the thematic area in various fora at the regional level, including academia and civil society, with a view to deepen related political commitment and related reforms;

- Provide regional support to UNDP’s Planet Hub, where needed;

- Support the Environment Regional Team Leader in engagement in UN interagency coordination in relevant policy areas by organizing and participating in regional meetings.

iii. Facilitate Research and Knowledge Management

- Provide inputs for HQ policy briefs/position papers prepared in collaboration with other practices that address links between energy and development;

- Coordinate and conduct analysis of data, case evidence and research findings to distil relevant lessons from regional projects and programmes to inform policy formulation and guidance and other products;

- Contribute to the relevant analysis on issues related to energy, including on emerging issues of significance to the region, and contribute to new research, technical paper, or reports, as needed by RBAP;

- Collect and compile information on the energy profiles of countries in the region, including key indicators and policies, and identify areas of strategic significance for programming and policy work;

- Contribute to the corporate knowledge management activities, at region-specific level to help influence/advance policy dialogue in the thematic area in collaboration with policy teams;

- Contribute to the regional energy insights and programming priorities to knowledge networks and communities of practice;

- Support knowledge extraction, analysis, documentation, codification of results/lessons learned in the specific thematic area and verify that knowledge sharing, and content management is in line with guidelines and performed using corporate tools;

- Provide inputs for energy programming outputs (e.g. work-plans, project documents, inception missions, workshops, technical working papers, methodologies).

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination

Ability to apply existing concepts to new situations, and to develop new concepts to generate workable solutions and new approaches. Knowledge of relevant concepts, conceptual models, and theories that can be useful in addressing new situations

Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media, and other appropriate channels

- Partnerships Management: Build and maintain partnerships with wide networks of stakeholders, Governments, civil society and private sector partners, experts, and others in line with UNDP strategy and policies

Business Direction and Strategy

- System Thinking: Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system

Ethic

2030 Agenda: Partnerships

Education:

- Advanced university degree (master’s degree or equivalent) in Energy, Engineering, Environment, Economics, Business Administration, Social Sciences, or related discipline is required OR: A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the areas mentioned above, in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree

Experience:

- Minimum 2 years (with master´s degree) or 4 years (with bachelor´s degree) of progressively responsible administrative or programme experience is required at the national or international level.

Required skills:

- Experience in providing policy advisory services related to sustainable energy;

- Experience working with developing countries;

- Experience in the usage of IT, use of internet/intranet, and office software packages (MS Word, Excel, etc).

Desired skills:

- Experience in supporting work in multiple countries in the Asia and the Pacific region;

- Experience in working with multilateral organizations and/or the UN system;

- Experience in addressing energy issues in SIDS, and fragile and crisis contexts;

- Experience in working with a wide set of energy stakeholders, such as the private and financial sector, government, and civil society;

- Experience in energy finance, including financial risk assessment and analysis of energy projects and portfolios

Background

At the country level, UNV Field Units (FUs) and designated UNV personnel are responsible for promoting volunteerism through the mobilization of UN Volunteers across the UN system in the areas of peace, development, human rights and humanitarian assistance. FUs represent and position UNV within the respective countries, particularly within the UN country team, adopting a client-oriented and solutions-based approach.

As UNV is the systemwide service administered by UNDP, FUs are hosted within relevant UNDP offices, collaborating closely with the UNDP resident representative and the UN resident coordinator system. The UNV country coordinator ensures compliance with UNV and UNDP policies, rules, and regulations.

Scope of Work

- Promote Volunteer Mobilization

- Position UNV as a system-wide service provider supporting UN partners to achieve their programmes and UNSDCF goals. Develop and implement country-level volunteer mobilization strategies aligned with UNV’s Strategic Framework and partner demand.

- Participate in UN collective planning processes (CCA, UNSDCF, humanitarian response plans, thematic task forces) to integrate volunteerism in their implementation.

- Present UNV’s value proposition to maximize contributions of UN Volunteers, and guide partners in developing volunteer assignment descriptions.

- Support local talent outreach and acquisition efforts in alignment with corporate strategies.

- Promote Online Volunteering as a core component of UNV’s offer.

- Monitor mobilization trends, track key performance indicators, and use corporate tools (CRM, BI reports, UVP) for informed decision-making.

- Facilitate executive, operational, and partnership missions by UNV.

2. Build Strategic Partnerships

- Build and sustain effective relationships with UN partners to promote UNV’s mandate and services.

- Analyze country strategies (UNSDCF, agency strategies) to identify opportunities for volunteer mobilization.

- Maintain business intelligence on UN programming, funding and workforce trends to diversify partnerships and forecast volunteer demand.

- Engage regularly the heads of agencies, their management teams and senior programme and operations staff to support volunteer mobilization, collaborating proactively to identify opportunities.

- In coordination with the RO and ERCS, map and pursue SVF mobilization opportunities.

- Engage with government, civil society, private sector, and development partners in close coordination with other UN entities as may be required to realize agreed objectives.

3. Ensure Duty of Care

- Support host entities with guidance and best practices to ensure successful volunteer assignments.

- Work closely with UNDSS, the UN Designated Official for security, and host agencies to ensure the safety, security, and inclusion of UN Volunteers. Provide timely support during security evacuations.

- Ensure volunteers receive appropriate briefings, orientation, and guidance from host entities on arrival and benefit from appropriate supervision throughout their assignment.

- Brief the volunteer on expected code of conduct and other relevant factors for a successful experience; be available to answer questions.

- Conduct regular field visits to volunteer locations and monitor volunteer well-being and provide guidance on critical administrative aspects.

- Facilitate regular engagement with and among volunteers (e.g., town halls, networking, and community activities) to strengthen volunteer experience and well-being.

4. Promote advocacy on volunteerism

- Align communications with volunteer mobilization and talent acquisition goals, develop impactful volunteer stories in collaboration with the RO and External Relations and Communications Section (ERCS), promote UNV at national, regional and global levels.

- Stay informed of national volunteer initiatives, policies and strategies, including those supported by the UN system, and share relevant updates with Volunteer Advisory Services Section.

- Stay informed of host countries’ aspirations to promote national volunteer talent through fully funded UNV assignments domestically and abroad, share relevant updates with ERCS on emerging demand for UNV solutions, and support their implementation if needed.

- Stay informed of the International Volunteer Day and other volunteer recognition efforts by national counterparts and, where appropriate, collaborate around respective activities in close coordination with UN country teams and upon advice from the RO and ERCS.

- Encourage volunteers to act as advocates and disseminate their experiences as advocates and ambassadors of volunteer action.

5. Ensure Effective Field Unit Management

- Lead and coordinate the FU to ensure effective and efficient service delivery and a collaborative work environment.

- Supervise, empower and ensure performance and accountability of FU team members. Provide coaching and oversight to ensure consistency and client orientation in the FU’s communication with all clients.

- Develop, monitor, and manage the FU’s annual work plan and budget in compliance with performance targets and UNDP regulations.

- Liaise with UNDP programme and operations teams to ensure administrative support, alignment with local protocol, and facilitate cooperation on critical issues such as visas for international volunteers.

- Ensure that the FU undertake assigned transactions in the Volunteer Management Cycle in accordance with corporate SOPs. Escalate operational and reputational risks and other significant issues promptly to the RO.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

Under the overall guidance of the regional manager and direct supervision of the portfolio manager or specialist in the Regional Office (RO), the country coordinator manages the FU and leads UNV’s engagement at the country level.

The role’s primary purpose is to ensure that UNV effectively anticipates and responds to the needs of the UN system and partners by mobilizing qualified volunteers and promoting volunteerism across sectors. This includes strategic positioning, partnership building, advocacy, and contribution to UNV’s Strategic Framework implementation.

The country coordinator works under the general guidance of the UN resident coordinator to position UNV and its services within the UN system and liaises regularly with the UNDP resident representative for support. The incumbent also collaborates closely with the UNDP country office for administrative matters, participates in UN country team activities as invited (including joint UN programme, operations, communications teams and other subsidiary groups of UNCT), and may represent UNV in joint coordination mechanisms with government and non-government stakeholders.
