jobs.title: Administrative Support Intern
jobs.description:
Background

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) is dedicated to eradicating poverty, reducing inequalities, and building resilience to help countries achieve sustainable progress. To support the efficient delivery of its services, the UNDP Ghana Country Office is seeking an Administrative Support Intern. Under the overall supervision of the Operations Manager, the intern will assist with key administrative and operational tasks within the Operations Unit.

This internship offers practical experience in office administration within a dynamic operational environment. The intern will support the day-to-day functions of the Operations Unit through documentation, records management, data entry and logistical coordination. This support will contribute to accurate record-keeping, improved administrative efficiency and the timely delivery of services.

Duties and Responsibilities

1.) Assist with registry and records management, including filing, scanning, data entry, document tracking, and archiving both physical and electronic records such as scan, register, file and distribute incoming correspondence, and maintain an organized filing system.

2.) Assist with the issuance of office supplies, monitor stock levels and maintain updated inventory records such as record requests for office supplies, issue items as authorized and update stock records to support timely replenishment.

3.) Support logistical arrangements by updating vehicle schedules and related trackers, maintaining fleet documentation and assisting with the coordination of transport requests such as update vehicle and driver rosters, fuel records, maintenance schedules and insurance documentation as required.

4.) Assist with preparing and tracking payment and cost recovery documentation, checking that supporting documents are organized and available for review before submission e.g. preparation of non-PO documentation and invoices for services provided to UNDP projects and other UN agencies

5.) Assist with maintaining facilities records, logging reported maintenance issues and following up on outstanding requests under the guidance of the Administrative Assistant e.g. update the facilities maintenance log, record reported issues and track the status of maintenance requests and contractor visits.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organisation.

Competencies

- Achieve Results: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline

- Think Innovatively: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

- Learn Continuously: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

- Adapt with Agility : Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible

- Act with Determination : Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident

- Engage and Partner : Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion : Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

Applicants to the UNDP internship programme must at the time of application meet one of the following requirements:

(a) Be enrolled in a postgraduate degree programme (such as a master’s programme, or higher);

(b) Be enrolled in the final academic year of a first university degree programme (such as bachelor’s degree or equivalent);

(c) Have recently graduated with a university degree (as defined in (a) and (b) above) and, if selected, must start the internship within one-year of graduation.

(d) Be enrolled in a postgraduate professional traineeship program and undertake the internship as part of this program.

Experience:

- Good organizational skills and attention to detail.

- Clear written and verbal communication skills in English.

- Basic proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel, Outlook and other standard office applications.

- Ability to maintain accurate records, handle routine data entry and follow established procedures.

- Willingness to learn, take feedback and work collaboratively with colleagues.

- Professionalism, discretion and respect for confidentiality.

- Demonstrated commitment to gender equality, diversity, inclusion and a workplace free from harassment.

Skills.

- Records Management

- Data Entry

- Administrative Support

- Logistics Coordination

- Document Processing

Disclaimer

Important information for US Permanent Residents ('Green Card' holders)

Under US immigration law, acceptance of a staff position with UNDP, an international organization, may have significant implications for US Permanent Residents. UNDP advises applicants for all professional level posts that they must relinquish their US Permanent Resident status and accept a G-4 visa, or have submitted a valid application for US citizenship prior to commencement of employment.

UNDP is not in a position to provide advice or assistance on applying for US citizenship and therefore applicants are advised to seek the advice of competent immigration lawyers regarding any applications.

Applicant information about UNDP rosters

Note: UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement. We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.

Non-discrimination

UNDP has a zero-tolerance policy towards sexual exploitation and misconduct, sexual harassment, and abuse of authority. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous reference and background checks, and will be expected to adhere to these standards and principles.

UNDP is an equal opportunity and inclusive employer that does not discriminate based on race, sex, gender identity, religion, nationality, ethnic origin, sexual orientation, disability, pregnancy, age, language, social origin or other status.

Scam warning

The United Nations does not charge any application, processing, training, interviewing, testing or other fee in connection with the application or recruitment process. Should you receive a solicitation for the payment of a fee, please disregard it. Furthermore, please note that emblems, logos, names and addresses are easily copied and reproduced. Therefore, you are advised to apply particular care when submitting personal information on the web.

jobs.title: Associado(a) de Projetos de Tecnologia e Gestão do Conhecimento (2 vagas) (Office based- Brasilia) [Open to internal and external applicants]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

Em linha com o compromisso de preservar a capacidade institucional e apoiar o pessoal já presente na Organização, a maioria das vagas do PNUD/UNCDF/UNV é publicada utilizando um processo de candidatura em camadas, no qual:

• Tier 0: Funcionários internacionais do PNUD/UNCDF/UNV com contratos permanentes (PA) e de prazo fixo (FTA), cujos postos serão abolidos ou cujos contratos serão encerrados ou não renovados durante 2026.

• Tier 1: Outros funcionários do PNUD/UNCDF/UNV com contratos permanentes (PA) e de prazo fixo (FTA).

• Tier 2: Funcionários do PNUD/UNCDF/UNV com contratos temporários (TA), pessoal com contratos PSA regulares, e Voluntários da ONU nas categorias Especialista e Expert.

• Tier 3 ou sem tier indicado: Todos os demais tipos de contrato do PNUD/UNCDF/UNV e de outras agências, bem como candidatos externos.

Por favor, observe o(s) Tier(s) indicado(s) no título da vaga, se aplicável, e certifique-se de que atende aos critérios de elegibilidade para candidatura.

Escritório/Unidade/Descrição do Projeto

A Unidade de Gestão de Projetos (UGP) de Justiça e Direitos Humanos, vinculada à Unidade de Governança e Justiça para o Desenvolvimento, está recrutando dois(as) Associados(as) de Projetos de Tecnologia e Gestão do Conhecimento para atuação em Brasília.

A Unidade atua de forma integrada às demais áreas do PNUD, promovendo e apoiando iniciativas nas áreas de Justiça, Governança e Direitos Humanos. Seu portfólio reúne parcerias estratégicas com instituições do sistema de justiça brasileiro, incluindo o Conselho Nacional de Justiça (CNJ), o Superior Tribunal de Justiça (STJ), a Defensoria Pública da União (DPU), a Escola Nacional de Formação e Aperfeiçoamento de Magistrados (ENFAM) e a Justiça Federal do Ceará (JFCE).

Recentemente, a Unidade firmou uma nova parceria com o STJ voltada ao fortalecimento da capacidade institucional da Corte, por meio do desenvolvimento de estratégias, estudos, modelos de governança, arquiteturas tecnológicas e soluções inovadoras. A iniciativa contempla temas como transformação digital, inteligência artificial, ciência e governança de dados, modernização tecnológica e aprimoramento da atividade jurisdicional.

Deveres e responsabilidades

Serão ofertadas duas vagas para Associado(a) de Projetos de Tecnologia e Gestão do Conhecimento, com perfis complementares. Uma posição terá foco prioritário no fortalecimento dos processos internos da UGP, incluindo gestão e sistematização do conhecimento, análise de dados, aprimoramento de fluxos de trabalho e desenvolvimento de soluções digitais para ganho de eficiência institucional. A outra posição terá atuação mais voltada ao acompanhamento estratégico dos projetos e ao relacionamento com parceiros externos, com especial atenção à nova parceria com o STJ e às iniciativas de transformação digital, inovação e gestão do conhecimento desenvolvidas no âmbito da Unidade de Governança e Justiça para o Desenvolvimento.

Ambos(as) os(as) profissionais atuarão sob a supervisão da Gerência de Projetos, prestando suporte técnico e operacional às iniciativas da Unidade. Entre suas atribuições estarão o aprimoramento de processos, a gestão e disseminação do conhecimento, a análise e utilização estratégica de dados, o desenho e aperfeiçoamento de soluções digitais e iniciativas de inovação, bem como o apoio administrativo e operacional necessário à implementação dos projetos e ao atendimento das demandas dos parceiros institucionais.

As atividades previstas para este posto incluem:

Principais Atividades e Responsabilidades

I. Planejamento, Monitoramento e Governança de Projetos

a. Apoiar o planejamento, a execução, o monitoramento e a avaliação de projetos e iniciativas de transformação digital, inovação e gestão do conhecimento, garantindo alinhamento aos objetivos estratégicos da Unidade, dos projetos e às normas e procedimentos do PNUD.

b. Monitorar cronogramas, entregas, indicadores, riscos e resultados, propondo medidas corretivas e oportunidades de melhoria para assegurar a efetiva implementação das atividades.

c. Utilizar metodologias e ferramentas de gestão de projetos para apoiar o acompanhamento técnico e gerencial das iniciativas sob responsabilidade da Unidade.

d. Elaborar e revisar planos de trabalho, relatórios de progresso, apresentações, notas técnicas e demais instrumentos de gestão e monitoramento de projetos.

e. Apoiar a identificação, análise e gestão de riscos operacionais, tecnológicos e institucionais, propondo estratégias de mitigação e aprimoramento da execução dos projetos.

II. Transformação Digital, Inovação e Gestão de Soluções Tecnológicas

a. Mapear, analisar e aprimorar processos organizacionais, identificando oportunidades de inovação, automação e transformação digital.

b. Levantar, analisar e sistematizar necessidades e requisitos técnicos e funcionais relacionados ao desenvolvimento, aquisição ou aprimoramento de soluções digitais.

c. Apoiar o desenho, estruturação, implementação, testes, validação e melhoria contínua de ferramentas, plataformas, fluxos digitais, automações, painéis gerenciais e outras soluções tecnológicas.

d. Aplicar metodologias ágeis, centradas no usuário e orientadas à inovação para apoiar a concepção e implementação de soluções digitais.

e. Identificar oportunidades para utilização de inteligência artificial, ciência de dados, automação e tecnologias emergentes na gestão de projetos, processos e conhecimento institucional.

f. Acompanhar a execução e a qualidade de produtos e soluções tecnológicas desenvolvidos no âmbito dos projetos, assegurando aderência aos requisitos definidos, às boas práticas e às necessidades dos parceiros.

III. Pesquisa Aplicada, Gestão do Conhecimento e Inteligência Institucional

a. Realizar pesquisas, diagnósticos, levantamentos e análises sobre temas relacionados à transformação digital, inovação, inteligência artificial, governança de dados, gestão do conhecimento e modernização institucional.

b. Produzir estudos, notas técnicas, relatórios analíticos, documentos conceituais e produtos de conhecimento para subsidiar a tomada de decisão e o desenvolvimento de iniciativas estratégicas.

c. Identificar, sistematizar e disseminar evidências, tendências, boas práticas nacionais e internacionais e experiências inovadoras relevantes para os projetos e parceiros institucionais.

d. Organizar, tratar e analisar dados quantitativos e qualitativos, transformando informações operacionais em conhecimento estratégico para apoio à gestão.

e. Desenvolver e aprimorar indicadores, dashboards, visualizações de dados e instrumentos de monitoramento para acompanhamento de resultados e apoio à tomada de decisão.

f. Estruturar e manter bases de conhecimento, repositórios digitais, metodologias, fluxos, registros de boas práticas e lições aprendidas.

g. Utilizar ferramentas digitais, recursos de automação e inteligência artificial para apoiar atividades de pesquisa, análise de informações, produção de conhecimento e inteligência institucional.

h. Apoiar a elaboração, revisão e disseminação de publicações, estudos, pesquisas e demais produtos técnicos produzidos no âmbito dos projetos.

IV. Gestão Contratual, Aquisições e Apoio à Implementação

a. Apoiar a elaboração de Termos de Referência, especificações técnicas, escopos de trabalho e demais documentos necessários à contratação de bens e serviços, especialmente na área de tecnologia, dados e inovação.

b. Apoiar processos de aquisição e contratação, acompanhando cronogramas, documentação, entregas e interlocução com áreas internas, consultores e fornecedores.

c. Acompanhar a execução de contratos, produtos e consultorias, monitorando prazos, qualidade das entregas, conformidade contratual e alcance dos resultados previstos.

d. Apoiar atividades relacionadas à gestão orçamentária, financeira, administrativa e operacional dos projetos, em conformidade com as normas e procedimentos do PNUD.

e. Acompanhar instrumentos de gestão de projetos de cooperação internacional, incluindo PRODOCs, revisões, relatórios, Cartas Acordo (LoAs) e demais documentos de gestão.

V. Articulação Institucional, Comunicação e Fortalecimento de Capacidades

a. Promover a articulação entre equipes do PNUD, Unidades de Gestão de Projetos, parceiros institucionais, fornecedores e demais partes interessadas, assegurando adequada comunicação e fluxo de informações.

b. Organizar e participar de reuniões, missões, oficinas, eventos e grupos de trabalho, elaborando atas, memórias, notas técnicas e acompanhando os encaminhamentos pactuados.

c. Apoiar a identificação e o fortalecimento de parcerias estratégicas relacionadas à transformação digital, inovação, inteligência artificial, gestão do conhecimento e modernização institucional.

d. Planejar e apoiar ações de capacitação, transferência de conhecimento e fortalecimento de capacidades voltadas às equipes dos projetos e parceiros institucionais.

e. Contribuir para a disseminação de soluções inovadoras, boas práticas e aprendizados entre projetos, unidades e instituições parceiras.

Os (As) Associados(as) de Projetos de tecnologia e Gestão do Conhecimento desempenharão outras funções dentro do seu perfil funcional consideradas necessárias ao bom funcionamento do programa.

Arranjo Institucional

Os (As) Associados(as) de Projetos de tecnologia e Gestão do Conhecimento atuarão sob a orientação geral e supervisão da Coordenação da Unidade de Gestão de Projetos (UGP).

Os resultados-chave esperados para este posto visam a estruturação de estratégias de ação e acompanhamento de modo a garantir a qualidade, eficiência e efetividade na implementação dos projetos em âmbito nacional, de forma alinhada com as metas e prioridades acordadas pelo PNUD e seus parceiros institucionais, contribuindo para promoção do acesso à Justiça de forma ampla, interseccional e pautada nas normativas nacionais e internacionais de Direitos Humanos.

Competências

Alcançar resultados:

LEVEL 1: Planeja e monitora o próprio trabalho, presta atenção aos detalhes, entrega um trabalho de qualidade dentro do prazo

Pensamento inovador:

LEVEL 1: Aberto a ideias criativas/riscos conhecidos, é pragmático para resolver problemas, faz melhoria.

Aprendizagem continua:

LEVEL 1: Mente aberta e curiosa, compartilha conhecimento, aprende com os erros, pede feedback

Adaptar com agilidade:

LEVEL 1: Adapta-se à mudança, lida de forma construtiva com a ambiguidade/incerteza, é flexível

Atuar com determinação:

LEVEL 1: Mostra determinação e motivação, capaz de entregar com calma diante da adversidade, confiança

Engajar-se e ser parceiro:

LEVEL 1: Demonstra compaixão/compreensão para com os outros, forma relacionamentos positivo

Promover diversidade e inclusão:

LEVEL 1: Valoriza e respeita as diferenças, está consciente de vieses inconscientes e enfrenta a discriminação.

Competências multifuncionais e técnicas

Direção de negócios e estratégia - Pensamento estratégico:

• Desenvolver estratégias eficazes e planos prioritários alinhados com a missão e os objetivos do PNUD, baseando-se em uma análise sistêmica de desafios, oportunidades e riscos potenciais; conectar a visão geral à realidade no campo para criar soluções tangíveis e direcionadas; aprender a partir de diversas fontes para antecipar e responder de forma eficaz às tendências atuais e futuras; demonstrar capacidade de previsão.

Direção e Estratégia de Negócios - Futuro e Previsão:

• Capacidade de analisar informações passadas e presentes, identificar padrões e tendências e usá-los para orientar a tomada de decisões com uma visão de longo prazo. Sensibilidade para escanear horizontes e captar sinais fracos de mudança, explorando suas possíveis implicações e avaliando seu impacto e urgência. Utilizar criatividade e imaginação para comunicar insights de forma envolvente e impactante, desafiando os modelos mentais atuais; habilidade para desenvolver cenários e designs especulativos para apresentar visões de futuro ou torná-los uma experiência prática. Capacidade de facilitar debates e discussões sobre possíveis cenários futuros. Ajudar pessoas a se sentirem confortáveis com o desconforto causado pela incerteza.

Gestão de negócios - Gestão de projetos:

• Capacidade de planejar, organizar, priorizar e controlar recursos, procedimentos e protocolos para atingir objetivos específicos.

Gestão de negócios - Trabalho com evidências e dados:

• Capacidade de inspecionar, limpar, transformar e modelar dados com o objetivo de descobrir informações úteis, informar conclusões e apoiar a tomada de decisões.

Agenda 2030: Engajamento e Eficácia - Inovação:

• Ecossistema de Inovação

Agenda 2030: Paz - Estado de Direito, Segurança e Direitos Humanos:

• Instituições Eficazes do Setor de Justiça.

Agenda 2030: Paz - Estado de Direito, Segurança e Direitos Humanos:

• Acesso à Justiça.

Habilidades e experiência necessárias

Requisitos mínimos de educação:

• Diploma do Ensino Médio completo é requerido.

• Diploma Universitário (Ensino Superior) em Administração Pública, Direito, Ciências Sociais, Gestão Pública, Ciência da Computação, Engenharias ou áreas afins será dada a devida consideração, mas não é um requisito.

Anos mínimos de experiência profissional relevante:

• Mínimo de 7 anos (para Ensino Médio) ou 4 anos (para Ensino Superior) de experiência profissional em gestão, implementação ou acompanhamento de projetos e iniciativas de tecnologia, transformação digital, inovação ou gestão do conhecimento, com atuação em melhoria de processos, realização de pesquisas, análise de dados e soluções digitais, produção de documentos técnicos, aplicação de metodologias de gestão de projetos, monitoramento de resultados e/ou articulação institucional.

Habilidades necessárias:

• Experiência no uso de tecnologias da informação, incluindo o uso de sistemas corporativos, como o sistema ERP para organizações e ferramentas digitais de comunicação (Outlook, SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams, Zoom e plataformas similares).

Habilidades desejadas, além das competências abordadas na seção Competências:

• Pós-graduação ou certificação com ênfase em projetos tecnológicos e/ou Inteligência Artificial.

• Experiência no uso de ferramentas digitais e soluções tecnológicas, com experiência no uso de recursos inovadores, automação e inteligência artificial aplicados à análise e monitoramento de dados, gestão da informação e otimização de processos (ex.: Excel avançado, Power BI, Power Query, Power Platform ou ferramentas equivalentes).

• Experiência nas áreas de Justiça, Desenvolvimento Sustentável, Direitos Humanos, e áreas correlatas.

• Experiência com negociação de requisitos para projetos de inovação e pesquisa.

Idiomas exigidos:

• Fluência em português é requerido.

• Nível básico de Inglês é desejável.

Certificações Profissionais:

• Não se aplica.

Igualdade de oportunidades

Como empregador que promove a igualdade de oportunidades, o PNUD valoriza a diversidade como expressão da multiplicidade de nações e culturas onde atua e, dessa forma, incentiva candidatos qualificados de todas as origens a se candidatarem às oportunidades na organização. Nossas decisões de contratação são baseadas no mérito e na adequação ao cargo, sem discriminação.

O PNUD também está comprometido com a criação de um ambiente de trabalho inclusivo, onde todos os colaboradores estejam empoderados para contribuir com nossa missão, sejam valorizados, possam prosperar e se beneficiar de oportunidades abertas a todos/as.

Assédio sexual, exploração e abuso de autoridade

O PNUD não tolera assédio, assédio sexual, exploração, discriminação e abuso de autoridade. Portanto, todos/as os/as candidatos/as selecionados/as passam por verificações rigorosas e espera-se que cumpram os respectivos padrões e princípios.

Direito de selecionar múltiplos candidatos

O PNUD reserva-se o direito de selecionar um/a ou mais candidatos/as a partir deste anúncio de vaga. Também poderemos manter os currículos recebidos e considerar os/as candidatos/as para outras vagas semelhantes no PNUD, com o mesmo nível e com descrições de cargo, requisitos de experiência e formação acadêmica similares.

Uso de IA por candidatos

Os candidatos são convidados a ler as orientações do PNUD sobre o uso responsável de Inteligência Artificial nos processos de recrutamento e seleção do PNUD.

Alerta de fraude

O PNUD não cobra nenhuma taxa em nenhuma etapa do seu processo de recrutamento. Para mais informações, consulte: www.undp.org/scam-alert

jobs.title: Gender Analyst (Open to Tier 1 & 2 Applicants)
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

UNDP Somalia is implementing its Country Programme Document (CPD) 2026–2030, supporting national priorities across inclusive governance, peacebuilding, sustainable economic transformation, climate resilience, durable solutions and social cohesion. Gender equality and women’s empowerment are cross-cutting priorities for achieving inclusive, equitable and sustainable development results.

Within this context, the Country Office is strengthening the systematic integration of gender equality across programmes and operations and its institutional accountability for results. Priorities include gender-responsive and gender-transformative programming, gender analysis, Women, Peace and Security (WPS), the Gender Equality Seal, Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) and safeguarding, women’s leadership and participation, social inclusion, partnerships, capacity development, knowledge management, monitoring and reporting.

The Gender Analyst will provide technical and coordination support across the Country Office, helping translate these commitments into programme design, implementation, monitoring, reporting and partnerships. The Analyst will work with programme and project teams, operations colleagues, management, government counterparts, civil society and women’s organizations, UN entities and development partners. The function will apply gender and intersectional analysis to Somalia’s fragile and conflict-affected context, including barriers affecting women and girls and the differentiated experiences of displaced people, persons with disabilities, youth and marginalized groups. The Gender Analyst will support practical, conflict-sensitive and locally grounded approaches that strengthen women’s agency, participation and access to development opportunities.

Institutional Arrangement

The Gender Analyst will work under the direct supervision of the Gender and Partnerships Specialist unser the overall supervision of the . The Gender Analyst will work closely with Country Office programme and project andoperations teams, management, the Gender Task Team (GFT) and relevant focal points. An organigram should be attached as an annex showing the position of the function within the office structure without indicating names of individuals.

Duties and Responsibilities

Provide gender analysis and programme quality support

- Conduct gender and intersectional analysis to inform programme design, policy dialogue, implementation and adaptive management.

- Provide technical inputs to programme documents, project proposals, theories of change, results frameworks, annual work plans and donor submissions.

- Review programme and project documents, assessments, budgets and reports to strengthen gender-responsive and gender-transformative approaches.

- Support meaningful integration of Leave No One Behind principles and identify gender-specific barriers, risks and opportunities relevant to Somalia’s context.

Strengthen gender mainstreaming and accountability across the Country Office

- Guide and support implementation and monitoring of the UNDP Somalia Gender Equality Strategy and related action plans.

- Guide and support implementation of the Gender Equality Seal Action Plan, including evidence collection, internal coordination, progress tracking and reporting.

- Support application of the UNDP Gender Marker, including the integration of gender results, indicators and appropriately resourced activities across programmes and projects.

- Facilitate the Gender Task Team and follow up agreed actions with programme and operations teams.

Guide and support Women, Peace and Security, PSEA, safeguarding and inclusive programming

- Guide and support integration of Women, Peace and Security priorities across relevant programme portfolios and initiatives that strengthen women’s leadership and meaningful participation in governance, peacebuilding and decision-making.

- Provide technical support on PSEA and safeguarding within the scope of the function and in coordination with designated office focal points and accountability mechanisms.

- Promote conflict-sensitive and do-no-harm approaches and the inclusion of women with disabilities, youth, internally displaced persons, minority groups and other marginalized populations.

Strengthen partnerships, policy engagement and resource mobilization

- Support engagement with government institutions, women’s rights and women-led organizations, civil society, UN entities, academia, private sector actors and development partners.

- Contribute to stakeholder and donor mapping and identify partnership and financing opportunities for gender equality and women’s empowerment.

- Contribute gender analysis and technical content to concept notes, donor briefs, project documents and funding proposals.

- Support UNDP participation in relevant gender coordination mechanisms, technical working groups and inter-agency forums.

Facilitate gender capacity development, knowledge building and learning

- Assess gender capacity needs and support the design and delivery of practical learning initiatives for personnel and implementing partners.

- Develop and adapt tools, guidance notes, training materials and knowledge products on gender mainstreaming, intersectional analysis, WPS, Gender Marker and institutional gender accountability.

- Identify, synthesize and document lessons learned, promising practices and results from UNDP Somalia programmes and share them through relevant communities of practice and knowledge networks.

Contribute to the monitoring, reporting, communications and advocacy for gender results

- Support collection, analysis and use of sex-, age- and disability-disaggregated data and qualitative evidence.

- Monitor gender-related indicators, targets and commitments and prepare analytical reports, dashboards, briefs, talking points and management updates.

- Contribute to donor, annual and corporate reporting on gender equality results.

- Support gender-responsive communications and advocacy, ensuring that messaging and knowledge products use inclusive language and accurately reflect women’s agency and diverse experiences.

Provide cross-functional support

- Perform other duties within the functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Competencies

Core Competencies

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 1 – Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline.

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 1 – Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements.

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1 – Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback.

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 1 – Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible.

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 1 – Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident.

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 1 – Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships.

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 1 – Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination.

Cross-Functional & Technical Competencies

Business Direction & Strategy

- Systems Thinking Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system.

Business Management

- Monitoring & Evaluation Ability to systematically monitor results of strategies, programmes, and activities with a view to make sure that they are being implemented effectively; Ability to provide managers and key stakeholders with regular feedback and reporting on the consistency or discrepancy between planned activities and programme management and results. Ability to make independent judgment of the management and results of strategies, programmes and activities based on set criteria and benchmark, keeping in mind the needs and concerns of client, current and upcoming. Knowledge and understanding of monitoring and evaluation frameworks, concepts, methodologies, systems, processes, and tools. Ability to make an independent judgement based on set criteria and benchmarks. Ability to anticipate client's upcoming needs and concerns.

- Communication Communicate in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience. Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels.

2030 Agenda: People

- Gender Gender Equality Seal for public institutions. Gender and Intersectional Analysis.

Communications

- Digital Capacity Building Ability to increase impact of digital communications through trainings, partnerships and relevant resources.

Required Skills and Experience

Minimum Academic Education

- Advanced university degree (Master’s degree or equivalent) in Gender Studies, Women’s Studies, Social Sciences, Development Studies, Public Policy, Human Rights, International Relations or another relevant field is required; Or

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the above fields in combination with an additional two (2) years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Minimum Years of Relevant Work Experience

- A minimum of two (2) years (with a Master’s degree) or four (4) years (with a Bachelor’s degree) of relevant professional experience in gender equality, women’s empowerment, gender mainstreaming, social inclusion, governance, peacebuilding or development programming is required.

Required Skills and Competencies

- Demonstrated experience in gender and intersectional analysis.

- Experience providing technical inputs to programme/project design, implementation, monitoring or reporting.

- Experience working with diverse stakeholders including developing partnerships and supporting resource mobilization for gender equality, including contributions to concept notes, donor proposals and engagement with government institutions, UN entities, civil society and women’s organizations.

- Demonstrated ability in strong analytical, drafting, communication and facilitation experience/skills.

- Proficiency in standard office software applications.

Desired Additional Skills and Competencies

- Experience in applying gender analysis and gender mainstreaming to programme or project design, implementation, monitoring and reporting, preferably in Somalia or another fragile and conflict-affected setting.

- Experience in using gender-responsive programme quality and accountability tools, including gender-sensitive monitoring and evaluation, sex-, age- and disability-disaggregated data, the UNDP Gender Marker and/or the Gender Equality Seal.

- Experience in supporting Women, Peace and Security, PSEA, safeguarding and/or inclusive programming, including initiatives that advance women’s leadership and the meaningful participation of marginalized groups.

- Experience in designing and facilitating gender capacity development and providing technical guidance to programme teams, implementing partners and/or government or civil society counterparts.

Required Languages (at Working Level)

- Fluency in English and Somali is required.

Professional Certificates

- Relevant certification in Gender, Monitoring and Evaluation, Data Analysis or Research is an asset.

Equal opportunity

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNDP is also committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, are valued, can thrive, and benefit from career opportunities that are open to all.

Sexual harassment, exploitation, and abuse of authority

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

Right to select multiple candidates

UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement. We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.

Use of AI by candidates

Applicants are invited to read UNDP’s guidance for candidates on using AI responsibly in UNDP recruitment and selection

Scam alert

UNDP does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process. For further information, please see www.undp.org/scam-alert.

jobs.description:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

The Global Environment Facility (GEF) Small Grants Programme (SGP) is implemented by UNDP on behalf of the GEF Partnership. UNDP oversees the Small Grants Programme (SGP) through the Vertical Hub and the Nature Hub of BPPS. Funded by the Global Environment Facility (GEF), the Small Grants Programme efficiently channels direct grants to non-governmental and community-based organizations to help them cope with climate change; conserve biodiversity; protect international waters; reduce the impact of Persistent Organic Pollutants; and prevent land degradation. Helping communities with their initiatives for sustainable livelihoods while generating global environmental benefits is the core inspiration of the Small Grants Programme.

Launched in 1992 as a corporate programme of the GEF, the GEF Small Grants Programme (GEF SGP) has supported local action for over thirty years to address global environmental concerns. SGP aims to deliver global environmental benefits in the GEF focal areas of biodiversity conservation, climate change mitigation, protection of international waters, prevention of land degradation, and elimination of persistent organic pollutants through community-based approaches. To date, SGP has funded over 29,000 community-based projects covering more than 120 countries. It has gained considerable experiences at the community level, including adapting to climate change while addressing issues of the GEF focal areas. Further information can be found at: https://sgp.undp.org/.

Duties and Responsibilities

Support Programme Implementation:

- Contribute to day-to-day programme/project implementation, ensuring conformity to expected results, outputs, objectives and work-plans.

- Assist the National Coordinator (NC) in prescreening project concepts and project proposals and evaluate the financial part of the project proposals.

- Assist the NC in development and revision of grant application forms and other management tools, requirements of the programme, and other SGP documents.

- Advise potential grantees on project preparation processes and guidelines, and report to NC and National Steering Committee (NSC) on project development activities, as required.

- Provide day-to-day support and guidance to new and ongoing projects and its grantees, as required.

- Assist the NC in project implementation, matters related to the grievance redress mechanism, monitoring and evaluation, including participation in field visits.

- Support organization and preparation of minutes of NSC meetings and other SGP events.

- Maintain contacts and professional working relationship with NGOs, governmental institutions, donors, other SGP stakeholders.

- Assist NC in reporting regularly to the Central Programme Management Team (CPMT), United Nations Development Programme Country Office (UNDP CO), and assist NC in timely preparation of annual monitoring survey, and other CPMT, UNDP surveys and reports as required.

- Support the NC in meeting relevant M&E requirements (e.g. Project Implementation Report (PIR), Midterm Review (MTR) and Terminal Evaluation (TE)

- Draft memos and other operational documents on behalf of NC and respond to queries on SGP programme matters.

- Regularly update and maintain SGP project database as well as stakeholders’ database.

Support Programme Financial Management :

- Provide guidance, review, and control the accuracy of supporting documentation of projects’ interim and final financial reports, such as invoices, and advise the NC as required

- Process payment requests from grantees and vendors through obtaining necessary clearances and authorizations, and ensuring payments are affected promptly, and in accordance with SGP Standard Operating Procedures.

- Maintain close working contact with respective Regional Focal Point and seek her/his support, advice and guidance on how better to operate Quantum in accordance with SGP SOPs, if needed.

- In collaboration with the NC, maintain financial integrity of the programme, implement and monitor accounting system and databases of SGP country operational budget.

- Prepare and maintain the grant disbursement table and calendar, as well as track the Country Operating Budget to ensure compliance with the approved yearly budget.

- Draft annual SGP Country office administrative and project budget proposals.

- Management of the Petty Cash account with proper documentation and proper tractable records.

- Enter, extract, transfer data from Quantum and SGP database and produce reports as required.

- Follow up of travel arrangements and DSA payments for NC and NSC members

- Provide other financial reports as required.

Provision of Administrative Support:

- Procure office supplies, equipment, and furniture adhering to SGP and CO SOPs on procurement rules and regulation.

- Manage and organize everyday office work.

- Establish a proper filing system, maintain SGP country office administrative, financial, and management files and update them with original documentation or copy of the original documentation as necessary. Special focus on:

- Establish and maintain a separate folder with all signed NSC meetings minutes that approve new SGP granted project

- Establish and maintain projects filing system containing original MOAs and amendments, original or copies of interim and final reports with all supporting documents, and mission reports or evaluation documents.

- Establish and maintain financial folders for all SGP country office financial transactions.

- Maintain personnel files, performance evaluation reports, leave records, and other pertinent personnel/consultant records

- Draft routine correspondence and communications and establish filing system to record communications with local stakeholders.

- Provide administrative and operational support to organization of SGP events and activities as requested

- Prepare background information and documentation, update data relevant to the programme areas and compile background material for the NC and NSC.

- Ensure flow of information and dissemination of materials with all concerned.

- Maintain an updated inventory of all physical assets and register all inventory in the asset inventory sheet.

- Provide logistical and administrative support to visiting missions, travel arrangements, and meetings for the NC, NSC, adhering to SGP SOPs procurement rules and regulation.

- Support with the project audit including with preparation and subsequent implementation of any audit recommendations.

Support Knowledge Management and Communication

- Actively support the SGP country office in the efforts on knowledge management, knowledge networking and visibility of SGP.

- In accordance with SGP branding guidelines, support NC and NSC in the efforts towards proper recognition of SGP in any KM & Communication material produced by SGP grantees or stakeholders.

- Facilitate the organization of SGP advocacy events, workshops, stakeholders’ dialogues and round tables.

- Assist in drafting articles and publications with proper recognition of SGP.

- Participate at events for SGP information dissemination purposes

- Maintain, update or provide valid SGP information for the SGP website, SGP Global database and UNDP CO website.

Provide support to the effective monitoring, evaluation, and reporting on progress of project implementation

- Generate Performance Evaluation Report

- Support implementation of the project monitoring system in alignment with its Monitoring and Evaluation framework to facilitate effective information sharing on project status and achievement of targets.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

- The incumbent will be based in the UNDP [Mogadishu Somalia ] offices;

- The incumbent will report to the SGP National Coordinator;

- The incumbent will be given access to relevant information necessary for the execution of the tasks under this assignment;

- The incumbent will be provided with a workstation (i.e. laptop, internet, phone, scanner/printer, etc.) and access to reliable internet connection

Experience:

jobs.title: Digital Product Manager (Home Based) [Open to Tier 0, 1 and 2]
jobs.description:
Tier Decription

Tier 0: UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026

Tier 1: Other UNDP/ UNCDF/ UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed term (FTA) appointments (defined as “internal” candidates)

Tier 2: UNDP/ UNCDF/ UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

Tier 3: All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates”

Office/Unit/Project Description

UNDP is the knowledge frontier organization for sustainable development in the UN Development System and serves as the integrator for collective action to realize the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). UNDP's policy work, carried out at headquarters, regional, and country office levels, forms a contiguous spectrum from deep local knowledge to cutting-edge global perspectives and advocacy. In this context, UNDP invests in the Global Policy Network (GPN), which brings together field-based and global technical expertise across a wide range of knowledge domains to deliver the signature solutions and organizational capabilities envisioned in the Strategic Plan.

Within the GPN, the Bureau for Policy and Programme Support (BPPS) leads on developing policy and guidance to advance UNDP’s Strategic Plan. BPPS staff provide technical advice to Country Offices, advocate for UNDP’s corporate positions, represent UNDP in multi-stakeholder fora, and engage in inter-agency coordination across thematic areas.

The Digital, AI and Innovation (DAI) Hub is part of this architecture. It brings together UNDP’s expertise in digital transformation, data, AI, and systems innovation to help countries harness new technologies as enablers of sustainable and inclusive development. The Hub serves as an integrated platform, offering advisory support, technical assistance, and capacity development to governments and partners in over 170 countries. It co-creates digital transformation journeys, strengthens national and institutional capabilities, and mobilizes partnerships to build inclusive digital ecosystems. By leveraging UNDP’s global presence, development intelligence, and portfolio approach, the Hub equips countries to anticipate risks, adapt to uncertainty, and harness digital, data and AI responsibly as forces for people and planet.

Read more about the UNDP Strategic Plan 2026 – 2029: https://strategicplan.undp.org/

To bring digital around the globe, we need someone who can manage digital products that advance digital development at UNDP. The position of Digital Product Manager will be part of the team in Product Studio at the Digital, AI and Innovation Hub, BPPS, and report to the Head of Digital Experience. The Digital Product Manager will work in line with the UNDP Digital Standards.

https://www.undp.org/digital/productstudio

https://www.undp.org/digital/standards

Scope of Work

The Digital Product Manager will oversee a portfolio of digital products and support product development process for digital concepts for UNDP and broader UN teams. The role will involve the ongoing evolution and management of products that enable digital transformation and effective delivery of UN and Government programmes.

Specifically, the Digital Product Manager will be responsible for the development of new product ideas, ready-to-scale products, and matured products developed with UN, UNDP BPPS, Crisis Bureau, regional, and country office teams. Under the supervision of the Head of Digital Experience, the product manager will be responsible for the following:

Product planning

- Utilize human-centred design and design research methods to design products which are user-friendly, meet user and stakeholder needs, and solve the problems in focus.

- Facilitate co-design workshops and processes to ensure resulting products are desirable, viable, and feasible.

- Work with internal or vendor software developers to plan, scope, and deliver technical product builds.

- Develop and agree product plans/roadmaps with the relevant UNDP stakeholder/sponsor of the digital product.

- Develop pragmatic agile management processes to ensure products continue to be user centric, cost-efficient and impact oriented.

- Build strong relationships to ensure appropriate product oversight and organisational buy in required for the product vision to be realised.

- Regularly communicate and present product roadmaps to relevant teams within DAI Hub and UNDP at large, including senior and executive stakeholders.

- Drive thought leadership on digital product management.

- Own product and portfolio governance – including performance reporting and financial/budget tracking – to support senior-level prioritisation and investment decisions.

- Shape AI and LLM-enabled product opportunities from use-case discovery through operationalisation, including defining responsible AI guardrails and evaluating AI outputs (e.g. accuracy, hallucination risk, prompt refinement).

Product and service development

- Enable continuous development process for products under management, with iterative customer and stakeholder feedback, deploying regular product releases and fixes.

- Implement and maintain the necessary technical and organizational infrastructure for product delivery, including documentation/communications materials, working with internal or vendor software development teams.

- Develop and implement quality standards and assurance processes by meeting/exceeding relevant UNDP and industry digital standards.

- Manage external technology vendors and partners alongside cross-functional product teams, aligning scope, deliverables, timelines, budgets and quality standards.

Management, learning management, continuous improvement and support

- Implement ongoing product methodology and quality improvements in line with the relevant product roadmap.

- Provide responsive product support to relevant UNDP internal clients.

- Expand the breadth and depth of resources that enable greater levels of customer satisfaction through targeted automation, including templates, detailed documentation and standard operating procedures.

- Provide product training sessions for relevant teams in UNDP, including UNDP regional and country office focal points.

- Act as a trusted product and service advisor to internal client teams throughout the product lifecycle, helping define underlying business and user problems and advising on scope, prioritisation, technical trade-offs and delivery options.

- Facilitate knowledge and capacity building, knowledge sharing, and advocacy.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Competencies

Core

Achieve Results: LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences

Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands

Act with Determination: LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results

Engage and Partner: LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration

Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity

https://undp.sharepoint.com/teams/OHR/competency%20framework/Shared%20Documents/Forms/Gallery%20View.aspx?id=%2Fteams%2FOHR%2Fcompetency%20framework%2FShared%20Documents%2FTechnical%20Competencies%2Epdf&parent=%2Fteams%2FOHR%2Fcompetency%20framework%2FShared%20Documents

BUSINESS DIRECTION & STRATEGY

Systems Thinking

Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system

DIGITAL & INNOVATION

Digital product design

Ability to design digital products which are user-centred, intuitive, functional and achieve desired outcomes

DIGITAL & INNOVATION

Digital product management

Ability to design and lead digital product development including testing, ongoing product iteration, product strategy and delivery.

DIGITAL & INNOVATION

Digital business analysis

Ability to support digital business processes across a range of digital projects, programmes and activities.

DIGITAL & INNOVATION

User-centred design, user research, user testing

Knowledge of user-centred design methodologies and abilityto apply them practically

DIGITAL & INNOVATION

Programming, Web and App Development

Ability to build websites, platforms and apps that are effective and intuitive to use.

DIGITAL & INNOVATION

Agile methodology and processes

Ability to manage projects and processes through continuous iteration, learning and improvement. Ability to manage a self-organising cross-functional teams, foster a team culture of curiosity and learning. Being nimble and being able to improvise and quickly adjust to unforeseen events or changes in conditions or context.

Minimum Qualifications of the Successful IPSA

Min. Education requirements

- Advanced university degree (master's degree or equivalent) in Business, Design, or Technology, or related field is required, or

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the above fields in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Min. years of relevant work experience

Background

The Building Resilient Communities, Wetland Ecosystems and Associated Catchments in Uganda Project is a climate change adaptation initiative funded by the Green Climate Fund (GCF) and implemented by the Government of Uganda through the Ministry of Water and Environment (MWE), with support from the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP). The project aims to address the impacts of climate change on wetland ecosystems and the communities that depend on them by strengthening resilience, restoring degraded wetlands, and improving management of associated catchments through ecosystem-based adaptation approaches. The project supports large-scale restoration and conservation interventions, including wetland boundary demarcation, restoration of degraded wetlands, reforestation and afforestation, and promotion of sustainable land management practices. These interventions enhance ecosystem services, improve water security, reduce soil erosion, and strengthen community resilience to climate-related shocks.

In addition, the project promotes climate-resilient livelihoods for communities living within and around wetland ecosystems. Beneficiaries are supported through climate-smart agriculture, livestock enterprises, agroforestry, irrigation technologies, and other income-generating activities that improve household incomes and food security while reducing pressure on wetland resources. Special emphasis is placed on women, youth, and other vulnerable groups to ensure inclusive participation and benefits. The project also strengthens institutional and community capacities for sustainable wetland governance and climate adaptation planning. Support is provided to national and local government institutions to improve wetland management, environmental compliance, monitoring systems, and community-based natural resource management structures. Public awareness, stakeholder engagement, and knowledge-sharing initiatives further promote ownership and sustainability.

A key component of the project is improving access to climate, weather, and early warning information, enabling communities to make informed decisions on agriculture, natural resource management, disaster preparedness, and wetland conservation. Implemented across 24 districts in eastern and southwestern Uganda, the project contributes to national climate adaptation priorities and sustainable development goals. To support effective implementation and compliance with GCF, UNDP, and Government of Uganda requirements, the project seeks to recruit a Programme Assistant to provide implementation, coordination, monitoring, operational, financial, and administrative support

1. Support the project team to ensure effective project planning and implementation.

Review project documents for completeness and compliance with relevant rules and procedures and identify inconsistencies for referral to supervisor. - Contribute to and support data collection for gender analysis and gender mainstreaming at the project level.

2. Support partnerships and resource mobilization.

- Assist project team in identifying and gathering information on opportunities for resource mobilization.

Assist team in the design and conduct of internal evaluations and surveys. Identify gaps in implementation and provide support in bridging those gaps in consultation with supervisor and partners.

Background

Em 2025, o Conselho Nacional de Justiça (CNJ) e o Programa das Nações Unidas para o Desenvolvimento (PNUD) firmaram uma parceria voltada à promoção da inovação em segurança cibernética para o Poder Judiciário. O projeto BRA/25/025 – “Fortalecimento da segurança cibernética e da transparência para governança e efetividade da atuação do Poder Judiciário” desenvolve e implementa ferramentas e estratégias para o fortalecimento da segurança cibernética, da preservação digital e da integridade da informação, ampliando a proteção dos sistemas e dos usuários do Judiciário.

A iniciativa fortalece a segurança institucional e promove a transparência, a boa governança e a eficiência dos processos judiciais, contribuindo para a economia de recursos e para uma atuação mais ágil da Justiça em benefício dos cidadãos e da sociedade.

Para isso, a governança do projeto está dividida nas seguintes frentes:

Quatro eixos transversais de coordenação:

- Coordenação Geral;

- Unidade de monitoramento e controle integrado;

- Unidade de gestão técnica e operacional;

- Unidade de formação e comunicação;

Quatro frentes de trabalho, focadas em:

- Compliance normativa;

- Conformidade operacional;

- Governança em rede;

- Fomento à cultura de segurança cibernética;

Por se tratar de uma vaga em regime remoto, espera-se que o(a) candidato(a) disponha de condições adequadas de trabalho, incluindo infraestrutura e equipamentos necessários para o pleno desempenho das atividades.

O(a) profissional atuará em estreita articulação com as equipes do CNJ e do PNUD, contribuindo para o alinhamento com planos de continuidade, controle de acessos, registro de evidências e disseminação da cultura de resposta coordenada.

As seguintes atividades indicativas estão previstas:

1. Monitoramento, Análise de Vulnerabilidades e Alertas (MIAC)

- Coordenar ações preventivas e corretivas com base em sinais de vulnerabilidade, comportamentos atípicos ou riscos identificados no ambiente institucional.

- Acompanhar e interpretar continuamente alertas provenientes do MIAC, convertendo-os em medidas operacionais padronizadas.

2. Condução da Resposta Preventiva e Gestão de Controles

- Conduzir processos de resposta preventiva, orientando áreas técnicas e administrativas na aplicação dos protocolos estabelecidos.

- Colaborar com as equipes responsáveis por Gestão de Identidades e Acessos (IAM) para aplicação de restrições ou ajustes emergenciais.

- Contribuir para o alinhamento de todas as ações de resposta preventivas com os planos de continuidade e diretrizes operacionais da instituição.

3. Procedimentos, Padronização e Melhoria Contínua

- Desenvolver, estruturar e atualizar procedimentos e fluxos operacionais do protocolo preventivo de segurança.

- Participar de revisões periódicas dos protocolos de ação, sugerindo melhorias contínuas baseadas no histórico de ocorrências e em novos riscos identificados.

4. Registro, Auditoria e Conformidade

- Consolidar e manter registros técnicos de evidências, dados e decisões relacionadas à execução das ações preventivas, assegurando a rastreabilidade das informações e subsidiando processos de monitoramento, avaliação e tomada de decisão.

- Participar da organização e facilitação de treinamentos e capacitações relacionadas aos projetos para equipes de programas, operações e parceiros relevantes. Sistematizar e analisar lições aprendidas, boas práticas e evidências de implementação dos projetos.

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) in São Tomé and Príncipe supports the Government in advancing sustainable development pathways that address poverty, inequality, and environmental sustainability. As a Small Island Developing State (SIDS), the country faces structural vulnerabilities linked to its size, remoteness, and exposure to external shocks, particularly climate change and environmental degradation. At the same time, São Tomé and Príncipe is endowed with exceptional natural capital, hosting rich terrestrial and marine biodiversity and functioning as a net carbon sink. The country’s global environmental significance is further reflected in its designation as a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve and the recognition of its traditional cocoa production system as a Globally Important Agricultural Heritage System (GIAHS/SIPAM), highlighting the intrinsic link between biodiversity conservation, sustainable livelihoods, and cultural heritage. UNDP works in close partnership with national institutions, civil society, and development partners to strengthen capacities, mobilize resources, and deliver integrated solutions aligned with national priorities and global commitments.

Within this framework, the Climate and Nature portfolio constitutes a core pillar of UNDP’s programme, focusing on supporting the implementation of the country’s Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC), advancing climate resilience, and promoting the sustainable management of natural resources. The portfolio encompasses a growing pipeline of projects addressing climate mitigation and adaptation, biodiversity conservation, ecosystem restoration, disaster risk reduction, and the transition towards a low-carbon and climate-resilient economy. Key areas of intervention include strengthening climate governance systems—such as transparency, monitoring and reporting—supporting national adaptation planning and implementation, enhancing resilience to climate-related risks (including flooding and water insecurity), and advancing nature-based solutions and biodiversity finance mechanisms.

UNDP’s interventions are characterized by an integrated, cross-sectoral approach that combines policy advisory, institutional capacity development, and on-the-ground implementation. The portfolio places strong emphasis on stakeholder engagement—working closely with government entities, local communities, private sector actors, and development partners—and ensures that climate and environmental actions are inclusive, gender-responsive, and aligned with broader socio-economic priorities, including the promotion of green and blue economy opportunities. jobs.description:
Background

Diversity, Equity and Inclusion are core principles at UNDP: we value diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate, we foster inclusion as a way of ensuring all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, and we ensure equity and fairness in all our actions. Taking a ‘leave no one behind’ approach to our diversity efforts means increasing representation of underserved populations. People who identify as belonging to marginalized or excluded populations are strongly encouraged to apply. Learn more about working at UNDP including our values and inspiring stories.

UNDP does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of harassment, including sexual harassment, and discrimination. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous reference and background checks.

UNDP is the knowledge frontier organisation for sustainable development in the UN Development System and serves as the integrator for collective action to realise the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). UNDP's policy work carried out at HQ, Regional and Country Office levels, forms a contiguous spectrum of deep local knowledge to cutting-edge global perspectives and advocacy. In this context, UNDP invests in the Global Policy Network (GPN), a network of field-based and global technical expertise across a wide range of knowledge domains and in support of the signature solutions and organizational capabilities envisioned in the Strategic Plan.

UNDP’s 2026–2029 Strategic Plan reaffirms our continued commitment to achieving the Sustainable Development Goals by accelerating structural transformations that advance poverty eradication, reduce inequalities, strengthen resilience, and drive sustainable, climate-aligned development.

Within the GPN, the Bureau for Policy and Programme Support (BPPS) has the responsibility for developing all relevant policies and guidance to support the results of UNDP's Strategic Plan. BPPS's staff provides technical advice to Country Offices; advocates for UNDP corporate messages, represents UNDP at multi-stakeholder fora including public-private dialogues, government, and civil society dialogues, and engages in UN inter-agency coordination in specific thematic areas.

As part of GPN in BPPS, the Planet Hub promotes and scales up an integrated approach to deliver UNDP’s environment portfolio across nature, climate, energy, and chemicals and waste, supporting countries in advancing implementation of the Paris Agreement, the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, and related multilateral environmental agreements. It coordinates UNDP’s flagship offers—Nature Pledge, Climate Promise, and Energy Moonshot, and Cooling, Circularity and Pollution Prevention initiatives—to meet strong country demand across more than 140 countries. The Hub enables joined-up policy, programming, and financing solutions that accelerate low-emission, nature-positive, and pollution-free development, while strengthening resilience and advancing sustainable, inclusive growth in line with the Strategic Plan.

UNDP BIOFIN

UNDP’s Biodiversity Finance Initiative is a global program that has developed a methodology to measure biodiversity expenditures, assess financial needs, and design finance solutions to enhance biodiversity management in more than 140 countries. The first phase (2012-2018) focused on assessments and initial finance plan implementation. The second phase expands support for designing and implementing finance solutions, strengthening knowledge management platforms, and producing guidance on effective finance tools. BIOFIN follows a two-pronged approach: raising awareness and technical capacity on finance solutions while actively supporting feasibility studies, policy design, capacity building, and implementation. The fully updated Methodology released in 2024 integrates lessons learned from implementation and highlights practical examples. For more information see BIOFIN website – www.biofin.org.

PANORAMA

UNDP joined the multi-partner initiative PANORAMA – Solutions for a Healthy Planet in 2018, as a co-coordinator for its Protected Areas or 30x30 Solutions thematic community. PANORAMA is an initiative to document, promote and learn from examples of inspiring, replicable solutions across a range of conservation and sustainable development topics. PANORAMA allows practitioners to share and reflect on their experiences, and to learn from peers how similar challenges have been addressed around the globe. The partnership is supported by a PANORAMA Management Unit jointly hosted by IUCN and GIZ.

Finance has been identified as one of the most important learning needs among conservation practitioners, therefore, PANORAMA is collaborating with BIOFIN to share its implementation experiences as replicable Solutions.

BES-NET

The Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services Network (BES-Net) is a capacity sharing “network of networks” initiative managed jointly by UNDP, UNEP’s World Conservation Monitoring Centre, and UNESCO with the financial support of the German Federal Ministry for the Environment, Nature Conservation and Nuclear Safety and SwedBio at Stockholm Resilience Centre. In support of the capacity building work of the Intergovernmental Platform for Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services (IPBES), BES-Net:

• Promotes dialogue between science, policy and practice sectors around the latest IPBES assessment themes for more coordinated and evidence-based BES management, using the Trialogue methodology;

• Supports the development of capacity in selected countries to conduct the national ecosystem assessment (NEA), completing the global assessment being undertaken by IPBES;

• Provides the target countries with catalytic seed fund for the uptake of the key findings and recommendations of the IPBES assessments/NEAs in the policy, science and practice sectors;

Enhances the global BES network by developing a rich database of organizations and experts working on different IPBES assessment theme areas and making the latest BES related news and updates available on the web portal and the social media channels.

The project intends to recruit two interns to provide support across its knowledge management and communications functions. They will support the BIOFIN and PANORAMA projects, with an allocation of 50% to each and the BIOFIN and BESNET projects respectively, with an allocation of 80% to BIOFIN and 20% to BESNET.

Duties and Responsibilities

- Research, analyze and document BIOFIN implementation experiences, liaising with BIOFIN technical advisors and country coordinators, focusing on identifying finance solutions for the PANORAMA global platform;

- Develop an inventory of global and regional publications and academic courses which reference BIOFIN;

- Attend relevant BIOFIN team meetings and prepare concise meeting notes;

- Contribute to developing knowledge products on cross country analysis and financing solutions for biodiversity conservation, including guidance materials for BIOFIN teams in different countries;

- Synthesize and summarize research outcomes and lessons learned into formats tailored to BIOFIN thematic activities;

- Support the organization of events, webinars, meetings, regional calls; assist in maintaining the documentation of meetings and taking meeting minutes;

- Support communications efforts as needed, including contribution to blogs, articles, social media presence etc.;

- Monitor, analyze, and synthesize the media coverage of BIOFIN, and maintain and update the relevant database;

- Research, collect, analyze, and present BIOFIN Impact – assisting BIOFIN to develop 12 transformative case studies for a publication;

- Work with the Comms and KM Team to develop the newly designed Finance Solutions Catalogue;

- Assist the Comms Team in designing and implementing campaigns throughout the year;

- Contribute to the creation of a set of templates that will serve as a Comms and KM Toolkit for BIOFIN Countries;

- Assist in boosting BIOFIN presence in social media; provide assistance as required in the maintenance of the BIOFIN media accounts including Website, Facebook, Twitter, LinkedIn etc.;

- Monitor, analyze, and synthesize the developments, press clippings and reports of BIOFIN, and maintain a database of BIOFIN news coverage and update it regularly;

- Support the development of stories from countries where both projects operate, highlighting synergies between the two initiatives;

- Assist in compiling relevant content for monthly newsletters (e.g., the BES-Net Monthly Blast);

- Contribute to the creation of articles, including the partner/expert series, in coordination with project partner organizations and experts;

- Support the collection of information on BES Solution Fund implementation in relevant countries to aid impact tracking, as needed, including Spanish-speaking countries;

- Help identify collaboration opportunities between projects in relevant country offices, based on requests from the project global team, and coordinate with the BIOFIN team on related matters,

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1: Open-minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback.

Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible.

Act with Determination: LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in the face of adversity, confident.

Engage and Partner: LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships.

Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

Candidates must meet one of the following criteria:

(a) Be enrolled in the final academic year of a first university degree programme (minimum Bachelor’s level or equivalent) such as International Development Studies, Economics, Environmental, Social Sciences, Finance, Business Administration, Communication, or related fields.

(b) Be enrolled in a graduate school programme (second university degree or equivalent, or higher) such as International Development Studies, Economics, Environmental, Social Sciences, Finance, Business Administration, Communication, or related fields;

(c) Have graduated with a university degree (as defined in (a) and (b) above) and, if selected, must start the internship within one year of graduation.

(d) Be enrolled in a postgraduate professional traineeship program and undertake the internship as part of this program.

Experience:

- Previous related work experience would be an asset;

- Excellent writing skills are required, as demonstrated in a previous professional and/or academic experience;

- Experience or knowledge in biodiversity, conservation, finance and environment related areas is an asset;

- Experience in communication related activities; familiarity with social media platforms or digital media channels is an asset.

Language Requirements:

- Fluency in English is required.

- Fluency and/or knowledge in French and Spanish is highly desirable.

Internship Conditions

Applicants should become familiar with the internship conditions prior to signing an internship agreement. For information visit www.undp.org/internships/

Institutional Arrangements

- Communications and Knowledge Management Intern for BIOFIN&PANORAMA will report to the BIOFIN Communication Lead and the PANORAMA Project Coordinator.

- Communications and Knowledge Management Intern for BIOFIN&BESNET will report to the BIOFIN Communication Lead and the BESNET Partnership Development and Facilitation Specialist.

Financial aspects, expenses, and medical benefits

- UNDP will not pay for the internship but may provide a stipend monthly in accordance with the provisions of the UNDP Internship policy;

- UNDP accepts no responsibility for the medical insurance for the intern or for any costs arising from accidents and/or illness during the internship period. Interns, whether engaged in-person or remotely, are responsible for securing adequate medical insurance for the duration of their internship with UNDP and must provide self certification of good health prior to starting the internship. UNDP will not reimburse the medical insurance of the intern. Any costs arising from accidents and illness incurred during an internship assignment will be the responsibility of the intern.

- UNDP is not responsible for any claims by an intern or third party in the case of loss or damage to property or death or personal injury as a result of actions or omissions on the part of the intern during the internship period.

Working conditions:

- When completing a remote internship, interns will be responsible for providing their own equipment, internet and communication access, and workspace.

Subsequent Employment

There is no expectation of employment with UNDP following an internship.

Important note:
